subtitle.en: From sense-certainty to the circle of circles
subtitle.zh: 从感性确定性到圆圈之圆圈

description.en: A spiral tower that retraces Hegel's system. The Phenomenology of Spirit is the ladder up; then come the Logic (being, essence, concept), the Philosophy of Nature and the Philosophy of Spirit, ending with philosophy at the summit, which leads back to the beginning.
description.zh: 一座沿黑格尔体系盘旋而上的塔。《精神现象学》是登塔的阶梯，接着是逻辑学（存在、本质、概念）、自然哲学和精神哲学，塔顶是哲学本身，而它又通回起点。

metaphor.en: A ramp that keeps returning above where it began: each turn cancels, preserves and lifts the last.
metaphor.zh: 一条不断回到起点上方的坡道：每一圈都否定、保留并提升了上一圈。

summary.en: The ladder to science: natural consciousness tests its own knowledge, fails and rises shape by shape, from sense-certainty to absolute knowing.
summary.zh: 通往科学的梯子：自然意识检验自己的知识，屡屡失败，又一个形态接一个形态地上升，从感性确定性直到绝对知识。

summary.en: The Preface and Introduction: why truth is the whole process, why the absolute is subject, and how negation moves the climb.
summary.zh: 序言与导论：为什么真理是整个过程，为什么绝对是主体，否定又如何推动攀登。

summary.en: Truth is not a single proposition or a bare result but the whole process of development, in which each stage is partial yet necessary.
summary.zh: 真理不是单个命题或光秃秃的结论，而是整个发展过程；每个阶段都片面，却都必要。

explain.en: In the Preface to the Phenomenology (1807) Hegel says that 'the True is the whole', and the whole is the essence completing itself through its development; the absolute is essentially a result. His image: the bud vanishes when the blossom breaks out and could be said to be refuted by it; the fruit in turn declares the blossom a false form of the plant. Yet all three are moments of one organic life, each as necessary as the others. So a single stage is partial rather than simply false, and a result cut off from the path that produced it is, in Hegel's word, a corpse. That is why the book walks through every shape of consciousness instead of announcing the answer.
explain.zh: 《精神现象学》（1807）序言说：“真理是全体。”全体只是通过自身发展而完成的本质；绝对本质上是一个结果。黑格尔的比喻是：花朵开放时花蕾消失，可以说花蕾被花朵驳倒了；果实出现时，花朵又被宣布为植物的虚假存在。可是三者都是同一个有机生命的环节，彼此同样必要。所以单个阶段是片面的，而不是简单的错误；脱离了产生它的过程，结果只是一具“尸体”。因此这本书要走遍意识的每一种形态，而不是直接宣布答案。

example.en: Photograph an apple tree on 1 April (buds), 1 May (blossom) and 1 September (apples). Each photo, offered alone as 'the apple tree', is contradicted by the next, yet none is simply false and none is the tree. Hegel's own case: someone who wants to see an oak is not satisfied to be shown an acorn. Likewise a theorem quoted without its proof is a bare result: you can repeat it but do not yet know why it holds.
example.zh: 在 4 月 1 日、5 月 1 日和 9 月 1 日各给一棵苹果树拍照：花蕾、花朵、苹果。每张照片单独冒充“这棵苹果树”，都会被下一张推翻，但没有一张是简单的错，也没有一张就是那棵树。黑格尔自己的例子：想看橡树的人，不会满足于别人给他看一颗橡子。同样，只背定理不看证明，得到的只是光秃秃的结论：会复述，却不知道为什么成立。

image.en: A blossom tree grows straight up through the floorboards of a book-lined study. A scholar in a beret kneels before one giant rose, magnifier raised, declaring it the true plant; at that moment an apple drops from above onto his head. Beside him a sprout pokes up, and a basket of picked apples stands apart, cut off from the tree.
image.zh: 书房的地板上长出一棵开满花的树。戴贝雷帽的学者跪在一朵巨大的玫瑰前，举着放大镜宣布：这才是植物的真相。话音未落，一个苹果从上面砸到他头上。他身边冒出一株嫩芽，一篮摘下的苹果被放在一旁，和树隔开。

means.en: the whole: one life running through all its stages
means.zh: 全体：贯穿各个阶段的同一个生命

means.en: one stage mistaken for the whole truth
means.zh: 被误当成全部真理的一个阶段

means.en: the next stage 'refutes' the last one
means.zh: 后一阶段“驳倒”前一阶段

means.en: the bud: an earlier stage, partial but necessary
means.zh: 花蕾：更早的阶段，片面却必要

means.en: a bare result without its process: a 'corpse'
means.zh: 脱离过程的结论：一具“尸体”

summary.en: The absolute is not an inert foundation but a self-moving activity that sets itself apart and returns to itself, as a self does.
summary.zh: 绝对不是僵死的基底，而是自我运动的活动：它把自己区分开，又从中回到自身，就像一个自我。

explain.en: Hegel's programme in the Preface: everything turns on grasping the true 'not only as substance, but equally as subject'. Spinoza's substance is the one self-caused reality of which all things are modes, but it rests in itself. An absolute in which all differences vanish (usually read as a jab at Schelling) is 'the night in which all cows are black'. A subject is pure negativity: it sets itself apart from itself, becomes other to itself, and comes back to itself out of that otherness. So the absolute is a circle that has its end as its goal and its beginning, and it is actual only by working itself out. In the Logic, substance turns into the concept by the same step.
explain.zh: 序言的纲领：关键在于“不仅把真理理解和表述为实体，而且同样理解和表述为主体”。斯宾诺莎的实体是自因的唯一实在，万物只是它的样态，但它静止在自身中。一切差别都消失的绝对（通常认为是在讥讽谢林）被说成“黑夜里所有的牛都是黑的”。主体则是纯粹的否定性：它把自己与自己区分开，成为自己的他物，又从这种他在中回到自身。所以绝对是一个圆圈，以终点为目标、也以终点为开端，只有把自己展开实现出来才是现实的。逻辑学中实体过渡到概念，走的也是这一步。

example.en: Compare a stone with a person. A stone simply is what it is. A person becomes who she is by acting: a student sets herself the goal of becoming a programmer, passes through failures that make her other than she was, and finally recognises herself in the result. The goal was there at the start but became real only through the process. Hegel claims the absolute has the person's structure, self-relation through otherness, not the stone's.
example.zh: 比较一块石头和一个人。石头就是它所是的样子。人却通过行动成为自己：一个学生给自己定下“成为程序员”的目标，经历一次次让她不再是原来那个人的失败，最后在结果中认出自己。目标从一开始就在，却只有经过这个过程才变成现实。黑格尔认为绝对具有人的这种结构，即通过他在而自我关联，而不是石头的结构。

image.en: A rough block of white marble stands in the study. Out of its top climbs a figure made of the same white stone, swinging a hammer at its own unfinished body: the block is carving itself. Chips of marble lie at its foot, and a bearded bust of Spinoza stares at the spectacle from beside the bookshelf.
image.zh: 书房里立着一块粗糙的白色大理石。石块顶上爬出一个同样由白石构成的人，抡起锤子凿自己尚未成形的身体：石头在雕刻它自己。碎石屑落在脚边，书架旁一尊留胡子的斯宾诺莎半身像瞪着这一幕。

means.en: substance: the one underlying reality
means.zh: 实体：唯一的基底

means.en: subject: activity that shapes and differentiates itself
means.zh: 主体：自我塑造、自我区分的活动

thing.en: figure of the block's own stone

means.en: what it becomes is itself: return to self
means.zh: 它成为的正是它自己：回到自身

means.en: the otherness it produces in becoming itself
means.zh: 它在成为自己时产生的他在

means.en: substance without the principle of the self
means.zh: 缺少自我原则的实体

summary.en: Negating a specific content yields a specific new result, not empty nothing; this is what moves the Phenomenology forward.
summary.zh: 否定一个确定的内容，得到的是有确定内容的新结果，而不是空无；这推动着整部现象学前进。

explain.en: In the Introduction Hegel explains how consciousness can educate itself. It carries its own standard: what it takes the object to be. Testing its knowledge against that standard, it finds a mismatch, and then both its knowledge and its object change; Hegel calls this movement experience. Scepticism sees only pure nothingness in the result. But the nothing that results is the nothing of what was negated, so it has content: a new shape of consciousness that knows why the old one failed. This is determinate negation. It lets the series of shapes generate itself without an outside method. For natural consciousness the road is a 'way of despair'; for philosophy it is the way to science.
explain.zh: 导论说明了意识如何自我教化。意识自带尺度：它认为对象是什么。用这个尺度检验自己的知识，它发现两者不符，于是知识和对象都改变了；黑格尔把这一运动叫作经验。怀疑主义在结果里只看到纯粹的无。可是这个无是被否定之物的无，因而有内容：一个新的意识形态，它知道旧形态为什么失败。这就是确定的否定（bestimmte Negation）。它让各个形态自己产生出来，不需要外加的方法。对自然意识来说这是一条“绝望之路”，对哲学来说却是通往科学之路。

example.en: Conjecture: every prime is odd. The counterexample 2 does not leave you with nothing; it hands you a sharper claim, 'every prime greater than 2 is odd', together with the reason: any other even number has the factor 2. A sceptic who concludes 'so we know nothing about primes' has made an empty negation. Hegel's first case in the book: 'Now is night', refuted at noon, yields 'now' as a universal.
example.zh: 猜想：所有素数都是奇数。反例 2 并没有让你一无所有，而是给出更精确的命题“大于 2 的素数都是奇数”，连同理由：除 2 以外的偶数都有因数 2。若怀疑论者由此断定“我们对素数一无所知”，那就是空洞的否定。黑格尔书中的第一个例子：“此时是夜晚”到中午被推翻，得到的是作为普遍者的“此时”。

image.en: On the study floor sits a big twig nest holding a giant egg. The shell is cracking and a fluffy yellow chick hops out: the old form negated, a definite new one born from it. A few steps away a hooded sceptic has smashed a second egg with his hammer and shrugs at the cracked mess: negation that leaves only nothing.
image.zh: 书房地上放着一个大树枝窝，窝里有一枚巨蛋。蛋壳正在裂开，一只毛茸茸的黄色小鸡跳了出来：旧形式被否定，从中诞生出一个确定的新形式。几步之外，戴兜帽的怀疑论者用锤子砸碎了另一枚蛋，对着一摊碎壳耸耸肩：这种否定只留下空无。

means.en: a shape of consciousness broken by its own test
means.zh: 被自身检验打破的意识形态

means.en: the determinate result: a new shape with definite content
means.zh: 确定的结果：有内容的新形态

means.en: empty negation: 'pure nothingness'
means.zh: 空洞的否定：“纯粹的无”

thing.zh: 拿锤子耸肩的怀疑论者

means.en: scepticism: negating everything from outside
means.zh: 怀疑主义：从外面否定一切

summary.en: To sublate is to cancel, to preserve and to lift up at once: a superseded stage lives on as a moment of the next.
summary.zh: 扬弃同时意味着取消、保存和提升：被超越的阶段作为环节活在下一阶段之中。

explain.en: German aufheben means both 'to end, abolish' and 'to keep, preserve'; Hegel uses the double sense on purpose, and its literal meaning 'to lift up' is usually counted as a third. What is sublated no longer exists in its immediate, independent form, yet it is not annihilated: it survives as a moment, mediated and reorganised, within a richer whole. Hegel explains the term in the Science of Logic right after becoming, where being and nothing persist only as moments of becoming. Sublation is the positive side of determinate negation, and it is why Hegel's progress is a spiral: neither a line of replacements nor a circle that returns unchanged.
explain.zh: 德语 aufheben 既有“终止、废除”的意思，也有“保存、保留”的意思，黑格尔有意利用这种双关；它的字面义“举起、提升”通常被算作第三层。被扬弃的东西不再以直接、独立的形式存在，却没有被消灭：它作为环节，经过中介、重新组织，保存在更丰富的整体中。黑格尔在《逻辑学》“变易”之后专门解释这个词：存在和无只作为变易的环节继续存在。扬弃是确定的否定的肯定一面，也是黑格尔的进展呈螺旋形的原因：既不是一条直线上的替换，也不是原样回到起点的圆圈。

example.en: Everyday German shows all three senses: 'Das Gesetz wurde aufgehoben' (the law was repealed), 'Ich hebe den Brief auf' (I'll keep the letter), 'Er hob den Stein auf' (he picked up the stone). An analogy from physics: relativity cancels Newtonian mechanics as the final truth, preserves it as the limit for slow speeds and lifts it into a wider theory. At Earth's orbital speed, 30 km/s, the factor γ differs from 1 by only about 5 × 10⁻⁹.
example.zh: 日常德语里三层意思都有：Das Gesetz wurde aufgehoben（法律被废除），Ich hebe den Brief auf（我把信留着），Er hob den Stein auf（他捡起石头）。物理学里的类比：相对论取消了牛顿力学作为终极真理的地位，又把它保存为低速下的极限，并提升进更广的理论。以地球公转速度 30 km/s 计算，相对论因子 γ 与 1 只差约 5×10⁻⁹。

image.en: In a corner of the study a man with rolled-up trousers stamps grapes in a wooden barrel, a basket of grapes waiting beside him. The grapes are crushed and gone as grapes, their juice is kept, and on the desk stands a wine bottle three times normal size: lifted up into something richer that still tastes of grapes.
image.zh: 书房一角，一个卷起裤腿的人站在木桶里踩葡萄，旁边放着一篮还没踩的葡萄。葡萄被踩碎，不再是葡萄；汁液却保存下来；书桌上立着一瓶三倍大的葡萄酒，被提升为更丰富的东西，却仍带着葡萄的味道。

means.en: cancel: the old form comes to an end
means.zh: 取消：旧形式终止

means.en: preserve: the content is kept
means.zh: 保存：内容留了下来

means.en: lift up: raised into a richer whole
means.zh: 提升：进入更丰富的整体

means.en: the old stage survives as a moment
means.zh: 旧阶段作为环节存续

summary.en: Consciousness takes its object to be simply out there: first a bare 'this', then a thing with properties, then forces and laws.
summary.zh: 意识以为对象就在外面：先是赤裸的“这一个”，再是有许多性质的物，最后是力与规律。

title.zh: 感性确定性：这一个、这里、这时

summary.en: The knowledge that seems richest, pure 'this, here, now', proves the poorest: all it can say are universals.
summary.zh: 看似最丰富的知识，“这一个、这里、这时”，其实最贫乏：它说得出的只是普遍者。

explain.en: The first shape of consciousness simply takes in the object without concepts and believes this is the richest, truest knowledge. Hegel asks it to say what it knows. 'Now is night': write it down, and at noon the written truth has gone stale. 'Here is a tree': turn around, and here is a house. What survives is not this night or this tree but 'now' and 'here' as such, which fit every moment and every place: universals. Language says the universal, so the unique thing we mean (meinen) cannot be said. Pointing does not rescue it, since every now turns out to be many nows. Sense-certainty must accept an object with general properties, which is perception.
explain.zh: 意识的第一个形态只想不加概念地接受对象，并自以为这是最丰富、最真实的知识。黑格尔让它说出自己知道什么。“此时是夜晚”：把它写下来，到中午再看，这条真理已经过时了。“这里是一棵树”：转个身，这里是一座房子。保留下来的不是这个夜晚、这棵树，而是对任何时刻、任何地点都适用的“此时”“这里”，也就是普遍者。语言说出的总是普遍者，我们所意谓（meinen）的独一无二之物说不出来。指一指也救不了它，因为每个“此时”都包含许多个“此时”。感性确定性只好承认对象是带有普遍性质的物，于是进入知觉。

example.en: Programmers meet the same problem: a log line that says 'today' or 'here' is useless next week. To keep a truth you must write a universal coordinate, such as 1806-10-13 in Jena, at 50.93° N, 11.59° E. Hegel's point is that even 'this', 'here' and 'now' are already universals of this kind: they fit every moment and place, so the unrepeatable particular you meant has slipped away in the very act of saying it.
example.zh: 程序员也会碰到这个问题：日志里写“今天”“这里”，下周再看就毫无用处。要保住一条真理，必须写下普遍的坐标，比如 1806-10-13，耶拿，北纬 50.93°、东经 11.59°。黑格尔的意思是：连“这一个”“这里”“这时”本身也已经是这种普遍者，它们适用于任何时刻和地点，所以你所意谓的那个独一无二的东西，在说出来的那一刻就溜走了。

image.en: At a night market a vendor with a lantern proudly chalks 'Now is night' on a big blackboard. Instantly the noon sun blazes above the board and the moon slinks away. The vendor points at a tree and shouts 'Here is a tree!', but on the other side of the board a little house is just as much 'here'.
image.zh: 夜市上，提着灯笼的摊主得意地在大黑板上写下“此时是夜晚”。转眼正午的太阳就在黑板上方烈烈燃烧，月亮悄悄溜走。摊主指着一棵树大喊“这里是一棵树！”，可黑板另一边的小房子同样是“这里”。

means.en: a truth written down to keep it
means.zh: 写下来保存的真理

means.en: the written truth goes stale: 'now' is a universal
means.zh: 写下的真理过时了：“此时”是普遍者

means.en: 'here' fits whatever you turn to
means.zh: “这里”适用于你转向的任何东西

means.en: meaning 'this', yet able to say only universals
means.zh: 意谓“这一个”，说出的却只有普遍者

title.en: Perception: The Thing and Its Properties

summary.en: The perceived thing is both one and many: a single unit and an 'also' of properties. Consciousness cannot hold the two together.
summary.zh: 被知觉的物既是“一”又是“多”：一个单一的物，又是许多性质的“也”。意识无法把两者统一起来。

explain.en: Perception (Wahrnehmung, literally 'taking-as-true') takes the object as a thing with many universal properties. Hegel's example is salt: this one grain is white, and also tart, and also cubical, and also of a certain weight. As an 'also' the thing is a medium in which properties lie side by side, indifferent to one another; as a 'one' it excludes others. Consciousness shuffles the contradiction back and forth: the thing is one and its many-ness lies in my senses (white to the eye, tart to the tongue), or the properties are in the thing and I supply the unity. At last it sees that the thing is for itself only by being for others. The truth of the object is an unconditioned universal, which only the understanding can grasp.
explain.zh: 知觉（Wahrnehmung，字面是“把握为真”）把对象当作具有许多普遍性质的物。黑格尔的例子是盐：这一粒盐是白的，也是咸的，也是立方体的，也有一定重量。作为“也”，物是一个媒介，各种性质在其中互不相干地并列；作为“一”，它排斥他物。意识来回推卸这个矛盾：要么物是一，多样性在我的感官里（白是对眼睛，咸是对舌头）；要么性质在物里，统一是我加上去的。最后它看到，物只有在为他物存在时才为自己存在。对象的真理是无条件的普遍者，只有知性才能把握。

example.en: In code the grain looks like this: salt = {'colour': 'white', 'taste': 'tart', 'shape': 'cube', 'mass_mg': 0.06}. The dictionary is an 'also': its entries sit side by side, indifferent to each other, and its unity is only the name salt, which we supply. Yet without that unity the entries are properties of nothing. Perception is stuck between these two views until it sees that a thing is what it is only in its relations to others.
example.zh: 在代码里，这粒盐可以写成 salt = {'colour': 'white', 'taste': 'tart', 'shape': 'cube', 'mass_mg': 0.06}。字典就是一个“也”：各个条目并列，互不相干；它的统一只是我们给的名字 salt。可没有这个统一，这些条目就不是任何东西的性质。知觉卡在这两种看法之间，直到看出：物只有在与他物的关系中才是它所是的。

image.en: At a spice stall a white cube of salt as big as a crate sits on top of a crate. A giant eyeball on a stand stares at it (white!), a dog licks it (tart!) and a huge hand rises behind it to feel its edges (cubical!). A shopper in a beret scratches his head: is he buying one thing, or a bundle of properties?
image.zh: 香料摊上，一块木箱那么大的白色盐块摆在木箱上。架子上的巨大眼球盯着它（白的！），一条狗舔它（咸的！），一只巨手从后面伸出来摸它的棱角（立方的！）。戴贝雷帽的顾客挠着头：他买的是一个东西，还是一堆性质？

means.en: the thing as a single 'one'
means.zh: 作为单一的“一”的物

means.en: white, tart, cubical: the 'also' of properties
means.zh: 白、咸、立方：性质的“也”

means.en: consciousness takes the many onto itself
means.zh: 意识把“多”揽到自己身上

means.en: unable to hold one and many together
means.zh: 无法把一和多统一起来

summary.en: The understanding explains appearances by forces and laws behind them, and behind the curtain finds only itself.
summary.zh: 知性用现象背后的力与规律解释现象，掀开帷幕，看到的却只是它自己。

explain.en: The understanding treats the thing's unity as force: a force that expresses itself and is driven back into itself, a play of forces. Behind the flux of appearance it posits a supersensible world, 'a calm kingdom of laws'. But explaining lightning by electric force only restates the appearance: the explanation is a tautology. Pushed further, the world of laws turns into an 'inverted world' in which what is sweet here is sour there. The understanding thus grasps infinity: difference that is self-difference, opposites that contain each other. Hegel concludes that behind the curtain said to hide the inner world there is nothing to see unless we go behind it ourselves. Consciousness of an object becomes self-consciousness.
explain.zh: 知性把物的统一理解为力：力外化自身，又被逼回自身，形成力的交互作用。在变幻的现象背后，它设立一个超感性世界，即“规律的静止王国”。可是用电力解释闪电，只是把现象换个说法重说一遍：这种解释是同语反复。再往前推，规律世界变成“颠倒的世界”：这里是甜的，那里就是酸的。知性由此把握到无限性：差别是自身的差别，对立面彼此包含。黑格尔的结论是：在据说遮盖内在世界的帷幕后面，如果我们自己不走进去，就什么也看不见。对象意识于是变成自我意识。

example.en: Why does the apple fall? 'Because of gravitational force.' And what is that force? 'Whatever makes masses accelerate toward each other.' The law F = Gm₁m₂/r² states the regularity exactly: two 1 kg masses 1 m apart attract with about 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N. But the 'force' posited behind the law adds no content; it repeats the appearance in the form of an inner essence. Hegel's lesson is that this inner world is the understanding's own construction.
example.zh: 苹果为什么落下？“因为引力。”引力是什么？“就是让物体相互加速靠近的东西。”定律 F = Gm₁m₂/r² 精确刻画了规律：相距 1 米的两个 1 千克物体，引力约为 6.67×10⁻¹¹ 牛。可是设定在规律背后的“力”并没有增加内容，只是把现象换成内在本质的形式再说一遍。黑格尔的教训是：这个内在世界是知性自己构造出来的。

image.en: Lightning crackles in front of a heavy velvet curtain at the back of a market stall: the play of forces. A scholar in a top hat yanks the curtain aside to see the hidden laws, and finds a tall mirror showing a man in a top hat yanking a curtain. A red horseshoe magnet lies on the ground nearby.
image.zh: 市集摊位后挂着一道厚重的天鹅绒帷幕，幕前闪电噼啪作响，那是力的交互作用。一个戴高礼帽的学者猛地拉开帷幕，想看藏在后面的规律，却只看到一面高高的镜子，镜中正是一个戴高礼帽、正在拉帷幕的人。一块红色马蹄形磁铁落在旁边的地上。

means.en: appearance as a play of forces
means.zh: 现象：力的交互作用

means.en: forces that solicit and are solicited
means.zh: 相互诱发的力

means.en: the supersensible world of laws 'behind' appearance
means.zh: 现象“背后”的超感性规律世界

means.en: consciousness finds itself in its object
means.zh: 意识在对象中发现了自己

means.en: we must go behind it ourselves
means.zh: 必须我们自己走到幕后

summary.en: Self-consciousness needs to be recognised: a struggle makes lord and bondsman, then come freedom in thought and the unhappy, split soul.
summary.zh: 自我意识需要被承认：斗争产生主人与奴隶，随后是思想中的自由和分裂的苦恼意识。

summary.en: Self-consciousness is desire, but consuming objects never satisfies it; it is satisfied only in another self-consciousness that recognises it.
summary.zh: 自我意识是欲望，但吞噬对象永远满足不了它；只有在承认它的另一个自我意识那里，它才得到满足。

explain.en: Once consciousness finds itself in its object, it becomes self-consciousness, and its first form is desire: it proves its independence by negating things, eating them up. But each satisfaction needs a new object, so desire keeps reproducing both the object and itself. Only an object that negates itself while staying independent can satisfy it, and that is another self-consciousness: 'self-consciousness achieves its satisfaction only in another self-consciousness.' With this the concept of spirit appears, 'I that is We and We that is I'. Recognition (Anerkennung) has to be mutual: each must see the other do what it does itself. The first attempt, however, is a struggle in which recognition comes out one-sided.
explain.zh: 意识在对象中发现了自己，就成为自我意识，它的第一个形式是欲望：通过否定物、吞掉物来证明自己的独立。可是每次满足都需要新的对象，欲望于是不断再生产出对象和它自己。只有一个自己否定自己、同时又保持独立的对象才能满足它，那就是另一个自我意识：“自我意识只有在另一个自我意识中才获得满足。”精神的概念由此出现：“我就是我们，我们就是我。”承认（Anerkennung）必须是相互的：每一方都看到对方做着自己所做的事。不过第一次尝试是一场斗争，承认在其中只是单方面的。

example.en: Compare two ways of getting a 'like'. A bot farm can deliver 10,000 likes in a day, and they feel worthless: nothing that could have refused you has recognised you. One sincere review from a peer whose judgement you respect counts for more, because it comes from someone free to say no. And it works only if you take her judgement seriously in turn: recognition from someone you do not recognise is empty.
example.zh: 比较两种“点赞”。刷量平台一天能给你一万个赞，却毫无分量：没有一个可能拒绝你的人承认了你。一位你敬重的同行真诚地评价一次，分量却重得多，因为她完全可以说不。而且只有你也认真对待她的判断，这份承认才成立：来自一个你不承认的人的承认是空的。

image.en: In the sand of the arena a glutton kneels beside an emptied basket, apples rolling around him, cramming in one more and still hungry. In the centre two giant hands, one pale and one dark, rise from the ground and reach for each other; where they meet, the crowd at the back goes wild.
image.zh: 竞技场的沙地上，一个饕餮者跪在吃空的篮子旁，苹果滚了一地，他又塞进一个，却依然饥饿。场地中央，一白一黑两只巨手从地下伸出，伸向对方；就在它们相会的地方，后面的人群欢声雷动。

means.en: desire: consuming objects never satisfies
means.zh: 欲望：吞噬对象永不满足

means.en: self-consciousness meets another self-consciousness
means.zh: 自我意识遇到另一个自我意识

means.en: recognition must be mutual
means.zh: 承认必须是相互的

means.en: spirit: 'I that is We, We that is I'
means.zh: 精神：“我就是我们，我们就是我”

summary.en: In the struggle for recognition whoever fears death becomes the bondsman; yet through fear and work he gains the truer independence.
summary.zh: 为承认而斗争，怕死的一方成了奴隶；但他通过恐惧和劳动，反而获得了更真实的独立。

explain.en: Each self-consciousness must prove it is not attached to mere life, so recognition begins as a life-and-death struggle. A dead opponent recognises no one, so the outcome is unequal: the one who prefers life to freedom becomes the bondsman, the other the lord. The lord enjoys things through the bondsman's labour, but he is recognised by a consciousness he does not count as an equal, so the recognition is hollow. The bondsman has trembled before death, 'the absolute master', and in serving he works on things. Work is 'desire held in check'; it forms the thing, and in the lasting product the bondsman sees his own independence. The relation reverses: the truth of the lord is the servile consciousness.
explain.zh: 每个自我意识都要证明自己并不执着于单纯的生命，所以承认首先是一场生死斗争。死去的对手不会承认任何人，所以结果是不平等的：宁要生命不要自由的一方成为奴隶，另一方成为主人。主人借奴隶的劳动享受物，但承认他的是一个他并不当作平等者的意识，所以这种承认是空洞的。奴隶在死亡这位“绝对的主人”面前战栗过，又在服务中加工物。劳动是“被遏制的欲望”，它塑造物，奴隶在持久的产品中直观到自己的独立。关系由此颠倒：主人的真理是奴隶意识。

example.en: Picture the outcome after ten years. The lord can still only consume: if the bondsman left, he could not feed himself. The bondsman has learnt to forge tools, build walls and plan a harvest, and the world around him bears his marks. Marx later credited the Phenomenology with grasping labour as the way humans make themselves; Hegel himself, however, leads the bondsman's freedom first into thought (stoicism), not into revolution.
example.zh: 设想十年以后。主人仍然只会消费：奴隶一走，他连饭都吃不上。奴隶却学会了打造工具、砌墙、筹划收成，周围的世界处处留着他的印记。马克思后来称赞《精神现象学》把劳动理解为人的自我生成；不过黑格尔本人让奴隶的自由先走向思想（斯多葛主义），而不是走向革命。

image.en: A sword stands stuck in the arena sand where the bondsman gave up the fight. The lord lolls on a bench, crown askew, sipping from a cup. Beside him the bondsman, a head taller than his master, hammers a gleaming shield on an anvil, while a grinning skull in the sand reminds him whom he truly fears.
image.zh: 竞技场的沙地上插着一把剑，奴隶就是在这里放弃了搏斗。主人歪戴王冠，懒洋洋地坐在长椅上啜饮。他旁边的奴隶比主人高出一头，正在铁砧上锤打一面闪亮的盾牌；沙地里一颗咧嘴的骷髅提醒他，他真正畏惧的是谁。

means.en: the life-and-death struggle he gave up
means.zh: 他放弃了的生死斗争

thing.en: lord on the bench with a cup

means.en: enjoyment without work; hollow recognition
means.zh: 只享受不劳动；空洞的承认

means.en: formative labour: 'desire held in check'
means.zh: 塑造物的劳动：“被遏制的欲望”

means.en: the lasting product in which he sees his independence
means.zh: 他从中直观到自己独立的持久产品

means.en: fear of death, 'the absolute master'
means.zh: 对死亡这位“绝对主人”的恐惧

title.zh: 斯多葛主义与怀疑主义

summary.en: Stoicism is free in thought whether on the throne or in chains; scepticism negates everything in thought yet lives like everyone else.
summary.zh: 斯多葛主义无论在王座上还是锁链中都在思想里自由；怀疑主义在思想里否定一切，却过着和别人一样的生活。

explain.en: The bondsman learnt in work that thinking forms things; stoicism concludes that freedom lies in thought. 'Whether on the throne or in chains', the stoic is free, since only what he thinks touches him; the emperor Marcus Aurelius and the former slave Epictetus share this view. But the freedom is abstract: it withdraws from life instead of shaping it, and its 'true and good' have no content. Scepticism carries out what stoicism only thinks: it negates every claim by showing it unstable. Yet it contradicts itself, declaring seeing and hearing null while it sees and hears, denying ethical rules while obeying them, like squabbling children. Holding both sides in one consciousness gives the unhappy consciousness.
explain.zh: 奴隶在劳动中发现思维能塑造物，斯多葛主义由此得出结论：自由在思想之中。“无论在王座上还是在锁链中”，斯多葛派都是自由的，因为只有他思考的东西才触动他；皇帝马可·奥勒留和奴隶出身的爱比克泰德都持这种看法。可这种自由是抽象的：它从生活中退出，而不去塑造生活，它的“真与善”没有内容。怀疑主义把斯多葛主义只是想想的东西付诸实行：它指出每一个主张都不稳定，从而否定一切主张。但它自相矛盾：一边宣称视听都是虚妄，一边照样看、照样听；一边否认伦理规范，一边照样遵守，像斗嘴的孩子。把这两面放进同一个意识，就是苦恼意识。

example.en: Epictetus, born a slave, taught that some things are 'up to us' (our judgements and choices) and others are not (body, property, reputation): locked in a cell, you remain free in what you assent to. About a century later the sceptic Sextus Empiricus collected arguments for suspending judgement on every claim, yet he practised medicine and followed customs and laws. Hegel's verdict: the first freedom is empty, and the second acts out its own contradiction.
example.zh: 奴隶出身的爱比克泰德教导说：有些事“取决于我们”（判断与选择），有些不取决于我们（身体、财产、名声）；被关在牢房里，你在赞同什么这件事上依然自由。大约一个世纪后，怀疑论者塞克斯都·恩披里柯收集了对一切主张都悬置判断的论证，自己却照样行医，遵守习俗和法律。黑格尔的评语是：前一种自由是空洞的，后一种当场演出了自己的矛盾。

image.en: A heavy chain lies across the arena sand. A shackled slave sits on a stool with eyes closed, smiling; on a throne beside him an emperor sits in exactly the same pose, and one thought bubble floats over both: 'I am free.' Nearby a hooded sceptic yells through a megaphone that nothing is certain, while stepping carefully around a puddle.
image.zh: 竞技场沙地上横着一条沉重的铁链。戴镣的奴隶坐在凳子上，闭眼微笑；旁边王座上的皇帝摆着一模一样的姿势，两人头顶飘着同一个思想气泡：“我是自由的。”不远处，戴兜帽的怀疑论者举着喇叭大喊“一切都不确定”，脚下却小心地绕开一个水坑。

thing.en: emperor and slave in the same pose
thing.zh: 姿势相同的皇帝与奴隶

means.en: stoicism: free in thought whatever one's station
means.zh: 斯多葛主义：无论处境如何，在思想中都自由

thing.zh: 共同的气泡“我是自由的”

means.en: abstract freedom with no content
means.zh: 没有内容的抽象自由

means.en: scepticism negates every claim
means.zh: 怀疑主义否定一切主张

means.en: he lives by the appearances he denies
means.zh: 他靠自己否认的表象过日子

summary.en: Consciousness split in two: a changeable self yearning for an unchangeable beyond, which it can reach only by giving itself up.
summary.zh: 分裂为二的意识：可变的自我渴慕彼岸的不变者，只有放弃自己才能接近它。

explain.en: The unhappy consciousness takes into one consciousness the split that scepticism left unreconciled: on one side its own changeable, finite self, on the other an unchangeable essence that it places beyond itself, though both are its own. Most readers take medieval Christian piety as the historical model. It tries three ways to reach the beyond: devotion, a 'musical thinking' that never gets to concepts, like the formless jingling of bells; desire and work, whose fruits it credits to the unchangeable; and self-mortification. Finally it hands its will to a mediator, the priest. In giving up its own will it learns that the individual and the universal are one, and it becomes reason.
explain.zh: 苦恼意识把怀疑主义没有调和的分裂收进同一个意识：一边是自己可变的、有限的自我，一边是被它放到彼岸的不变本质，而两者其实都是它自己。多数解读把中世纪基督教的虔敬看作它的历史原型。它试过三条路去接近彼岸：默祷，一种到达不了概念的“音乐式思维”，像无形的钟声；欲望和劳动，并把成果归功于不变者；以及禁欲苦行。最后它把自己的意志交给中介者，即神职人员。正是在放弃自身意志的过程中，它认识到个别与普遍是一体的，于是成为理性。

example.en: A medieval crusader travels thousands of kilometres to Jerusalem to touch the unchangeable, and finds what Hegel calls only a grave: the beyond cannot be grasped as a thing here and now. Back home he fasts, labours and credits every success to God, calling himself nothing. When he finally lets his confessor decide for him, he has, without knowing it, joined his particular will to the universal.
example.zh: 一个中世纪十字军战士跋涉几千公里到耶路撒冷，想触摸不变者，找到的却只是黑格尔所说的一座坟墓：彼岸不能作为此时此地的一件东西被抓住。回家后他斋戒、劳作，把每一点成功都归于上帝，称自己什么也不是。当他终于让告解神父替他作决定时，他已不知不觉地把自己的个别意志与普遍者结合起来了。

image.en: A robed figure kneels on the arena sand, holding out a key. High above, a golden star glows out of reach over a short flight of steps that ends in mid-air. Beside him a bell swings with a formless clang, and a hooded priest with a candle waits to take the key: the man's own will.
image.zh: 一个穿长袍的人跪在竞技场沙地上，手里举着一把钥匙。高处，一颗金星在一段悬空断掉的台阶上方闪耀，怎么也够不着。他身旁一口钟摇来摆去，发出没有调子的声响；一位戴兜帽、手持蜡烛的神父等着接过钥匙，那是这个人自己的意志。

means.en: the unchangeable placed in a beyond
means.zh: 被放到彼岸的不变者

means.en: the changeable self that calls itself nothing
means.zh: 自认一无是处的可变自我

means.en: devotion: 'musical thinking' that never reaches the concept
means.zh: 默祷：到达不了概念的“音乐式思维”

means.en: no finite path reaches the beyond
means.zh: 有限的路到不了彼岸

means.en: giving up one's will to a mediator: the way to reason
means.zh: 把意志交给中介者：通向理性

summary.en: Reason seeks itself in the world; spirit lives through the polis, culture, revolution and conscience, and finally knows itself.
summary.zh: 理性在世界中寻找自己；精神经历城邦、教化、革命与良心，最后认识自己。

title.en: Reason: Certain of Being All Reality
title.zh: 理性：确信自己是全部实在

summary.en: Reason is consciousness certain that it is all reality. It looks for itself in nature, ends by calling spirit a bone, and turns to action.
summary.zh: 理性是确信自己即全部实在的意识。它在自然中寻找自己，竟把精神说成骨头，于是转向行动。

explain.en: 'Reason is the certainty of consciousness that it is all reality.' Having united with the universal, consciousness now expects to find itself everywhere. Observing reason searches nature, organisms, the laws of thought and psychology. Its low point is physiognomy and phrenology, which read character from faces and skull bumps; Hegel sums up their claim in the 'infinite judgement' that the being of spirit is a bone, absurd when taken literally. Active reason then tries to make itself real in deeds: the pursuit of pleasure, the law of the heart, virtue fighting the way of the world, and reason that gives and tests laws. Each fails on its own, until reason sees that it already lives inside a shared ethical world: spirit.
explain.zh: “理性是意识确信它自己即是一切实在。”与普遍者结合以后，意识期待处处都找到自己。观察的理性在自然、有机体、思维规律和心理中寻找。它的低谷是相面术和颅相学，即从面相和头骨隆起读出性格；黑格尔用一个“无限判断”概括它们的主张：精神的存在是一块骨头，照字面理解就是荒谬的。行动的理性接着想在行为中实现自己：追求快乐、心的规律、德行与世界进程的斗争，以及立法与审核法则的理性。每一种单独都失败了，直到理性看出自己早已生活在共同的伦理世界之中，这就是精神。

example.en: Franz Joseph Gall's phrenology (around 1800) mapped 27 mental faculties onto regions of the skull and read character from its bumps. Hegel quotes Lichtenberg: if someone claims your face shows you to be a rogue, every honest fellow will answer with a box on the ear, proving that a person is what they do. Neuroscience today does localise functions in the brain, but by measuring activity, not by feeling the skull.
example.zh: 加尔的颅相学（约 1800 年）把 27 种心智能力对应到头骨的不同区域，凭头骨隆起判断性格。黑格尔引用利希滕贝格的话：要是有人说从你的面相看你是个无赖，每个正直的人都会回敬他一记耳光，证明人就是他所做的事。今天的神经科学确实会给脑功能定位，但靠的是测量脑活动，而不是摸头骨。

image.en: Under a theatre spotlight a giant skull lies on a table. A phrenologist in a graduation cap, a huge pair of compasses beside him, points at it and proudly announces 'Spirit is a bone!' A white phrenology bust looks on from the side, and the skull seems to grin at the verdict.
image.zh: 舞台聚光灯下，桌上摆着一颗巨大的骷髅。戴学位帽的颅相学家身边立着一把大圆规，他指着骷髅得意地宣布：“精神是一块骨头！”一旁的白色颅相学半身像默默看着，骷髅仿佛在嘲笑这个结论。

means.en: observing reason looks for spirit in a thing
means.zh: 观察的理性在物中寻找精神

means.en: measuring the outer to find the inner
means.zh: 测量外在以找到内在

means.en: the infinite judgement: absurd if taken literally
means.zh: 无限判断：照字面理解就荒谬

means.en: phrenology reads character off shape
means.zh: 颅相学从形状读出性格

summary.en: Spirit's first world is the Greek polis, where human law and divine law clash tragically, as Antigone and Creon do.
summary.zh: 精神的第一个世界是希腊城邦：人的法与神的法在其中悲剧性地冲突，就像安提戈涅与克瑞翁。

explain.en: Spirit is reason living as a community. Its first shape is the immediate ethical life (Sittlichkeit) of the Greek polis, where individuals simply identify with custom. It holds two laws: human law, the public law of the city, assigned to men, and divine law, the family's duty to its dead, assigned to women (a gendering much criticised today). In Sophocles' Antigone, Antigone buries her brother Polynices against Creon's edict. Each acts on a valid power and each is guilty of violating the other: 'because we suffer, we acknowledge we have erred.' The collision destroys the harmony, and what follows is Rome's 'legal status', in which individuals count only as abstract legal persons.
explain.zh: 精神是作为共同体而生活的理性。它的第一个形态是希腊城邦直接的伦理生活（Sittlichkeit），个人与习俗直接合一。其中有两种法：人的法，即城邦的公共法律，归于男人；神的法，即家庭对死者的义务，归于女人（这种性别划分今天常受批评）。在索福克勒斯的《安提戈涅》中，安提戈涅违抗克瑞翁的禁令，安葬了哥哥波吕尼刻斯。双方各依一种正当的力量行事，又都因侵犯对方而有罪：“因为我们受苦，我们承认我们犯了错。”冲突毁掉了和谐，随后是罗马的“法权状态”，个人只作为抽象的法律人格而存在。

example.en: Thebes after the civil war: Polynices died attacking the city, so King Creon forbids his burial on pain of death. His sister Antigone sprinkles dust on the body and is sentenced to be entombed alive. By the end Antigone, Creon's son Haemon and Creon's wife Eurydice are all dead. Hegel's reading refuses a melodrama of good and evil: the state cannot honour a traitor, and a family cannot leave a brother to the dogs.
example.zh: 内战之后的忒拜：波吕尼刻斯在攻城时战死，国王克瑞翁下令不许安葬，违者处死。他的妹妹安提戈涅给尸体撒上泥土，被判活埋在石墓里。剧终时，安提戈涅、克瑞翁的儿子海蒙和妻子欧律狄刻都死了。黑格尔的解读拒绝把它当成善恶分明的通俗剧：城邦不能礼葬叛徒，家人也不能把兄弟丢给野狗。

image.en: A huge tragic mask looms at the back of the stage. In front of it a body lies on the boards. On one side Antigone kneels in a dark robe beside a mound of stones, pouring a cup over her brother; on the other King Creon, crowned, stands before the city gate, pointing at her and brandishing his scroll of law.
image.zh: 舞台后方高悬一张巨大的悲剧面具，面具前的台板上躺着一具尸体。一边，身穿深色长袍的安提戈涅跪在一堆石头旁，向哥哥身上浇酒祭奠；另一边，头戴王冠的克瑞翁站在城门前，指着她，挥舞着他的法令。

means.en: human law: the city and its public edicts
means.zh: 人的法：城邦与公共法令

means.en: divine law: the family's duty to the dead
means.zh: 神的法：家庭对死者的义务

means.en: the deed where the two laws collide
means.zh: 两种法发生冲突的行为

means.en: tragedy: both powers valid, both guilty
means.zh: 悲剧：双方都正当，又都有罪

summary.en: In the world of culture the self becomes real only by giving itself up to state power and wealth, until a torn consciousness sees through it all.
summary.zh: 在教化世界里，自我只有把自己交给国家权力和财富才变得现实，直到分裂的意识看穿这一切。

explain.en: After Rome, spirit lives in a world it has made yet feels as foreign: the world of culture (Bildung), where an individual counts only by giving up its natural self. Two powers rule it, state power and wealth. The noble consciousness serves the state, first with its life, then with flattery to an absolute monarch; the base consciousness resents both. Soon every value turns into its opposite: the noble proves base and the base noble. Diderot's Rameau's Nephew, witty and shameless, voices this 'disrupted consciousness', which Hegel treats as the truth of this world. Faith flees to a heaven beyond, while pure insight, the Enlightenment, attacks faith and judges everything by its use.
explain.zh: 罗马之后，精神生活在一个自己造成、却又感到陌生的世界里：教化（Bildung）的世界。个人只有放弃自己的自然状态，才算数。统治这个世界的有两种力量：国家权力和财富。高贵意识为国家服务，先献出生命，后来向专制君主献上谄媚的言辞；卑贱意识则对两者都心怀怨恨。很快一切价值都颠倒过来：高贵的显得卑贱，卑贱的显得高贵。狄德罗笔下机智而无耻的“拉摩的侄儿”说出了这种“分裂的意识”，黑格尔视之为这个世界的真理。信仰逃往彼岸的天国，纯粹识见即启蒙则攻击信仰，用“有用”衡量一切。

example.en: Versailles under Louis XIV (reigned 1643–1715): nobles who once proved their honour on the battlefield now compete to hand the king his shirt at the morning lever, and their standing depends on pensions from the royal treasury. Courage has turned into flattery, honour into income. Rameau's nephew, a failed musician living off rich patrons, mimics the whole court in pantomime and says aloud what everyone does.
example.zh: 路易十四（1643—1715 年在位）治下的凡尔赛：曾在战场上证明荣誉的贵族，如今争着在国王的晨起仪式上为他递衬衫，地位取决于王室国库发的年金。勇气变成了谄媚，荣誉变成了收入。“拉摩的侄儿”是个失意的音乐人，靠富人接济过活，他用哑剧模仿整个宫廷，把人人都在做的事大声说了出来。

image.en: On one side of the stage a golden crown rests on a lectern; on the other an open chest overflows with gold. Between them a courtier in a top hat bows low to the crown while clutching a coin from the chest. In front, Rameau's nephew in a beret hops and laughs beside a grinning comedy mask, and a bright light bulb outshines a little candle.
image.zh: 舞台一侧，讲台上放着一顶金王冠；另一侧，一只敞开的箱子里金子满溢。两者之间，一个戴高礼帽的廷臣向王冠深深鞠躬，手里却攥着从箱子里拿的金币。前面，戴贝雷帽的拉摩的侄儿在一张咧嘴笑的喜剧面具旁又跳又笑，一只明亮的灯泡把一支小蜡烛比得黯然失色。

means.en: state power
means.zh: 国家权力

means.en: wealth
means.zh: 财富

thing.zh: 鞠躬又攥着金币的廷臣

means.en: service turned into paid flattery
means.zh: 服务变成了领钱的谄媚

thing.zh: 大笑的侄儿与喜剧面具

means.en: the disrupted consciousness that inverts every value
means.zh: 颠倒一切价值的分裂意识

means.en: pure insight (Enlightenment) against faith
means.zh: 纯粹识见（启蒙）对信仰

summary.en: A universal will that tolerates nothing particular can only destroy: the Terror, where death means no more than cutting a cabbage head.
summary.zh: 一个容不下任何特殊者的普遍意志只能破坏：这就是恐怖统治，死亡的意义不比切开一棵白菜更多。

explain.en: The Enlightenment ends by judging everything by its use, and absolute freedom draws the last conclusion. Self-consciousness demands that the universal will be directly real in each individual, with no estates, institutions or representatives in between. But such a will can produce no positive work, since any law or office would be particular. Its only deed is negation, a 'fury of destruction' aimed at every particular will, which is always suspected of not being the universal one, and being suspected is enough to be guilty. Hegel calls the resulting death 'the coldest and meanest of all deaths', no more significant than cutting off a head of cabbage or swallowing a mouthful of water. Freedom learns its emptiness and turns inward, into morality.
explain.zh: 启蒙最终用“有用”衡量一切，绝对自由则得出最后的结论：自我意识要求普遍意志在每个人身上直接实现，中间不要等级、制度或代表。可这样的意志做不出任何肯定的事业，因为任何法律或官职都会是特殊的东西。它唯一的行动是否定，即针对一切特殊意志的“毁灭的狂暴”，因为特殊意志总被怀疑不是普遍意志，而被怀疑就等于有罪。黑格尔说，这样的死是“最冷酷、最平淡的死”，意义不比切开一棵白菜头或吞下一口凉水更多。自由由此认识到自身的空虚，退回内心，成为道德。

example.en: The Law of Suspects of 17 September 1793 allowed the arrest of anyone suspected of hostility to the Revolution, including people who could not prove their civic loyalty. During the Terror (1793–94) about 17,000 people were officially executed, and Robespierre himself went to the guillotine on 28 July 1794. A will that recognises no particular interests ends up seeing enemies everywhere, even among its own leaders.
example.zh: 1793 年 9 月 17 日的《嫌疑犯法》允许逮捕任何被怀疑敌视革命的人，包括无法证明自己公民忠诚的人。恐怖时期（1793—1794）官方处决了约一万七千人，1794 年 7 月 28 日罗伯斯庇尔本人也上了断头台。一个不承认任何特殊利益的意志，最后到处都看见敌人，连自己的领袖也不放过。

image.en: On a bare stage a hooded executioner raises a huge blade over a chopping block. On the block sits a green cabbage, and a basket beside it already holds more cabbage heads. Behind, a marching crowd advances under a revolutionary flag. At the edge an onlooker sips a cup of water, completely unmoved.
image.zh: 空荡荡的舞台上，一个戴兜帽的刽子手在砧板上方高高举起一把大刀。砧板上放着一棵绿白菜，旁边的篮子里已经装着几颗白菜头。后面，行进的人群举着革命的旗帜涌来。台边一个旁观者端着一杯水慢慢喝，毫无波澜。

means.en: the universal will that tolerates nothing particular
means.zh: 容不下任何特殊者的普遍意志

means.en: its only deed is negation, the 'fury of destruction'
means.zh: 它唯一的行动是否定：“毁灭的狂暴”

means.en: a death no more significant than cutting a cabbage
means.zh: 意义不比切白菜更多的死

means.en: '…or swallowing a mouthful of water': no inner meaning
means.zh: “或吞下一口凉水”：毫无内在意义

summary.en: Conscience acts and is judged; the beautiful soul keeps its hands clean by not acting. Confession and forgiveness reconcile them.
summary.zh: 良心行动而遭评判，优美灵魂为保持清白而不行动。忏悔与宽恕使双方和解。

explain.en: The moral world-view of Kant and Fichte never closes the gap between duty and nature; spirit moves on to conscience, the certainty that what I am convinced of is my duty. But every action is particular, and others can always read it as selfish or hypocritical. The judging consciousness stands aside; as the 'beautiful soul' it refuses to act so as to stay pure, and if it persists it fades away like a shapeless vapour. Hegel turns the tables: 'No man is a hero to his valet, not because the man is not a hero, but because the valet is a valet.' When the one who acted confesses, the hard-hearted judge must at last give up his judgement and forgive. 'The wounds of the spirit heal, and leave no scars behind.' In this reconciliation spirit knows itself.
explain.zh: 康德和费希特的道德世界观始终弥合不了义务与自然之间的鸿沟；此后精神成为良心：确信我所认定的就是我的义务。可任何行动都是特殊的，别人总能把它解读为自私或伪善。评判的意识站在一旁；作为“优美灵魂”，它为了保持纯洁而拒绝行动，若一直如此，就会像一缕无形的烟雾消散。黑格尔反过来说：“仆人眼中无英雄，不是因为那人不是英雄，而是因为仆人只是仆人。”当行动者忏悔时，铁石心肠的评判者终于必须放下评判，给予宽恕。“精神的创伤愈合了，不留任何伤疤。”在这种和解中，精神认识了它自己。

example.en: A doctor in an epidemic triages patients and makes a fatal mistake. A critic who has never treated anyone writes that her motives were vanity. The critic's purity is real but cheap, bought by never acting. Reconciliation starts when the doctor admits the error and the critic recognises that judging is also a particular, fallible act: the very flaw he blamed in her.
example.zh: 疫情中，一位医生给病人分诊，犯了一个致命的错误。一位从未治疗过任何人的评论者写文章说，她的动机是虚荣。评论者的纯洁是真的，却很廉价，是靠从不行动换来的。当医生承认错误，而评论者也认识到评判本身同样是一个特殊的、会出错的行为，也就是他指责她的那种缺陷时，和解才开始。

image.en: A figure in muddy clothes kneels in a brown puddle, hands open in confession. Facing him stands a spotless judge in white robes who has just let his gavel drop to the floor; a small white cloud, the vapour the pure soul nearly faded into, drifts above him. Between them a big red heart hangs in the air, beating, as the judge stretches out his hand.
image.zh: 一个满身泥浆的人跪在褐色水坑里，摊开双手忏悔。对面站着一位一尘不染的白袍法官，刚刚任由法槌掉到地上；他头顶飘着一小朵白云，那是纯洁灵魂差点化成的烟雾。两人之间悬着一颗跳动的大红心，法官正向他伸出手。

means.en: the conscience that acted, and confesses
means.zh: 行动过、又在忏悔的良心

means.en: the beautiful soul that judges but will not act
means.zh: 只评判不行动的优美灵魂

means.en: giving up the hard-hearted judgement
means.zh: 放下铁石心肠的评判

means.en: purity without action fades like vapour
means.zh: 不行动的纯洁像烟雾一样消散

means.en: forgiveness: 'the wounds of the spirit heal'
means.zh: 宽恕：“精神的创伤会愈合”

summary.en: Spirit knows itself as spirit by recollecting every shape it has passed through, and so reaches the standpoint where the Logic begins.
summary.zh: 精神回忆起它走过的每一个形态，从而知道自己是精神，到达逻辑学开始的立场。

explain.en: Religion already knew the absolute as spirit, but in pictures; absolute knowing has the same content in the form of the concept. The gap between consciousness and object that drove the whole journey is closed: spirit knows every object as its own unfolding. Nothing is thrown away. The shapes are kept by recollection (Er-innerung, literally 'inwardising'), which Hegel describes as a slow gallery of images. Taken as history they look contingent; taken as conceptually comprehended organisation they form science. Together they are 'the recollection and the Golgotha of absolute spirit'. The ladder has been climbed: pure knowing, stripped of all content, is simple immediacy, the pure being with which the Science of Logic begins.
explain.zh: 宗教已经知道绝对是精神，但用的是表象；绝对知识具有同样的内容，形式却是概念。推动整个旅程的意识与对象之间的鸿沟被弥合了：精神知道一切对象都是它自身的展开。什么都没有被丢掉。各个形态通过回忆（Er-innerung，字面意思是“内在化”）保存下来，黑格尔把它描述为一条缓慢展开的画廊。作为历史，它们显得偶然；作为被概念把握的组织，它们构成科学。两者合起来是“绝对精神的回忆和髑髅地”。梯子已经登完：纯粹知识去掉一切内容，就是单纯的直接性，即《逻辑学》开端的纯存在。

example.en: Think of a chess player replaying her whole career. Each old game, blunders included, is not erased; it is now understood as a step in how she learnt to see the board. The Phenomenology's 'gallery' works the same way: sense-certainty, the bondsman and the beautiful soul are not wrong answers to discard but stations of one education. Absolute knowing is not knowing everything; it is reaching the standpoint from which the Logic can start.
example.zh: 想象一位棋手回顾自己的整个棋手生涯。每一盘旧棋连同其中的败着都没有被抹掉，而是被理解为她学会看懂棋盘的一步。现象学的“画廊”也是这样：感性确定性、奴隶、优美灵魂都不是要丢弃的错误答案，而是同一场教化的各个驿站。绝对知识并不是无所不知，而是到达逻辑学能够开始的那个立场。

image.en: At the top of a short flight of stairs in the middle of the stage a glowing spirit hovers. Behind it an arc of easels holds the portraits of every shape it has been, and between them an open door leads to an empty stage. At the foot of the stairs lie a skull, the Golgotha of spirit, and a golden chalice.
image.zh: 舞台中央一段短短的台阶顶上，一个发光的精神悬浮着。它身后一排弧形的画架上，挂着它曾经是过的每一个形态的肖像；画架中间一扇敞开的门通向空无一物的舞台。台阶脚下放着一颗骷髅，即精神的髑髅地，还有一只金杯。

means.en: spirit knowing itself as spirit: the top of the ladder
means.zh: 知道自己是精神的精神：梯子的顶端

means.en: the shapes kept by recollection: a gallery of images
means.zh: 通过回忆保存的各个形态：一条画廊

means.en: the Golgotha of absolute spirit: what the path cost
means.zh: 绝对精神的髑髅地：这条路的代价

means.en: the book's last lines: from this chalice foams its infinity
means.zh: 全书结尾：它的无限从这圣杯中涌出

thing.en: open door to an empty stage

means.en: pure being: where the Logic begins
means.zh: 纯存在：逻辑学从这里开始

summary.en: The Science of Logic opens with thought's most immediate categories: quality, then quantity, then measure, where the two unite.
summary.zh: 《逻辑学》从思维最直接的范畴开始：先是质，再是量，最后是两者统一的度。

summary.en: From the emptiest beginning, pure being, through becoming to something with a limit, the infinite and the One.
summary.zh: 从最空洞的开端纯存在出发，经过变易，到有界限的某物、无限和“一”。

summary.en: Logic begins without presuppositions with pure being, utterly indeterminate, which turns out to be no more and no less than nothing.
summary.zh: 逻辑学无前提地从纯存在开始；纯存在毫无规定，恰恰就是无，不多也不少。

explain.en: Where should science begin? Not with a principle that must first be proved, but with what is simply immediate: 'Being, pure being, without any further determination.' Pure being has no content, quality or difference; there is nothing in it to intuit or to think. So it is in fact nothing, 'neither more nor less than nothing'. And nothing, the empty thinking of emptiness, is itself there in thought, so it is the same as being. Hegel's image: in pure light, as in pure darkness, nothing can be seen. Yet the two are also absolutely distinct, and each vanishes immediately into the other. That vanishing is the first concrete thought: becoming. Parmenides, for whom only being is, stands at this start.
explain.zh: 科学应当从哪里开始？不能从一个需要先证明的原理开始，而要从单纯直接的东西开始：“存在，纯存在，没有任何进一步的规定。”纯存在没有内容、没有质、没有差别，其中没有什么可以直观、可以思维。所以它实际上就是无，“不多也不少”。反过来，无作为对空的空洞思维，在思维中也“存在”着，因而与存在相同。黑格尔的比喻是：在纯粹的光明中和在纯粹的黑暗中一样，什么也看不见。但二者又绝对不同，各自直接消失于对方之中。这种消失就是第一个具体的思想：变易。主张“唯有存在”的巴门尼德代表这个开端。

example.en: Strip the predicates from a sentence: 'This apple is red, round and weighs 150 g' becomes 'this apple is', then just 'is'. As an analogy from information theory, a predicate true of everything carries −log₂ 1 = 0 bits, exactly as much as saying nothing. That is Hegel's point in miniature: being without any further determination applies to everything and so tells you nothing; its content and the content of nothing coincide.
example.zh: 把句子里的谓词一个个去掉：“这个苹果是红的、圆的、重 150 克”变成“这个苹果是”，最后只剩“是”。打个信息论的比方：一个对一切都成立的谓词，信息量是 −log₂1 = 0 比特，和什么都没说一样多。这正是黑格尔的意思：没有任何进一步规定的存在适用于一切，因而什么也没告诉你；它的内容与无的内容重合。

image.en: In a quiet garden stands a large brass balance with both pans completely empty, its beam hanging perfectly level. Two identical plaques stand before the pans: one says Being, the other Nothing. A gardener peers at the pans through a huge magnifier and finds nothing to tell them apart, while a crow perched on top of the balance tilts its head.
image.zh: 安静的花园里立着一架黄铜大天平，两个秤盘都空空如也，横梁纹丝不动地保持水平。秤盘前立着两块一模一样的牌子：一块写着“存在”，一块写着“无”。园丁举着巨大的放大镜盯着两个秤盘，找不出任何区别；一只乌鸦站在天平顶上歪着头。

means.en: pure being and nothing: no content in either
means.zh: 纯存在与无：都没有内容

means.en: 'neither more nor less than nothing'
means.zh: “不多也不少”，恰好就是无

means.en: yet the two are meant as absolutely distinct
means.zh: 可二者又被认为是绝对不同的

means.en: thought finds nothing to intuit in pure being
means.zh: 思维在纯存在中找不到可直观的东西

summary.en: The truth of being and nothing is their unity as passing over into each other: coming-to-be and ceasing-to-be.
summary.zh: 存在与无的真理在于它们相互过渡的统一：产生与消灭。

explain.en: Being and nothing are the same and yet absolutely distinct; their truth is neither one but the movement in which each has already passed over into the other. That movement is becoming (Werden), the first concrete category, because it holds two opposed determinations within itself. It has two directions: coming-to-be, nothing passing into being, and ceasing-to-be, being passing into nothing. Heraclitus, with his 'everything flows', thought this stage, and Hegel said there was no proposition of Heraclitus he had not taken into his Logic. Becoming is restless, and its two directions cancel out into a calm result, a being that has a determination: determinate being. Right here Hegel explains the word 'sublate'.
explain.zh: 存在与无既相同又绝对不同；它们的真理不是其中任何一方，而是各自已经过渡到对方的运动。这一运动就是变易（Werden），第一个具体的范畴，因为它在自身中包含两个对立的规定。它有两个方向：产生，即无过渡为存在；消灭，即存在过渡为无。赫拉克利特以“一切皆流”思考的正是这一阶段，黑格尔说，赫拉克利特的命题没有一条他没有吸收进自己的逻辑学。变易是不安息的，它的两个方向相互抵消，沉淀为一个静止的结果：一个有规定的存在，即定在。黑格尔正是在这里解释了“扬弃”一词。

example.en: A garden fountain's jet looks like one fixed shape, yet a small pump pushes about 1,000 litres an hour through it, and every drop arrives and leaves within a second or so. The stable shape is the result of constant coming-to-be and ceasing-to-be. Heraclitus said the same of rivers: you cannot step into the same river twice, because other waters keep flowing on.
example.zh: 花园喷泉的水柱看起来是一个固定的形状，可一台小水泵每小时要推过大约 1000 升水，每一滴水都在一秒左右之间到来又离去。稳定的形状，是不断产生与消灭的结果。赫拉克利特说河流也是如此：人不能两次踏进同一条河流，因为新的水不断流来。

image.en: In the middle of the garden a stone fountain throws up water that falls back the moment it rises. Old Heraclitus in a robe stands at the basin holding out a cup, but the water in it is never the same water. On one side a fresh sprout pushes up through the soil; on the other a dead leaf lies on the ground.
image.zh: 花园中央，一座石喷泉把水抛上去，水刚升起就落下。身穿长袍的老赫拉克利特站在池边伸出杯子，可杯里的水从来不是同一份水。一边，一株嫩芽从土里钻出来；另一边，一片枯叶落在地上。

thing.en: water rising and falling at once

means.en: becoming: arising and passing away in one movement
means.zh: 变易：产生与消灭是同一个运动

means.en: 'everything flows': never the same water
means.zh: “一切皆流”：从来不是同一份水

means.en: the two directions: coming-to-be and ceasing-to-be
means.zh: 两个方向：产生与消灭

means.en: the calm result: determinate being
means.zh: 静止的结果：定在

summary.en: Determinate being is being with a quality: something is what it is by not being its other, through a limit that both defines and negates it.
summary.zh: 定在是有质的存在：某物之所以是它自己，在于它不是他物；界限既规定它，又否定它。

explain.en: Determinate being (Dasein) is being with a determinacy, and this immediate determinacy is quality. Quality includes negation: as Spinoza put it and Hegel stresses, all determination is negation. So we get something and other: a something is what it is by not being the other, and the other is itself a something. The limit (Grenze) separates them and yet belongs to both; only within and through its limit is something what it is. A something whose limit is part of its own nature is finite: it carries its end within itself, and 'the hour of its birth is the hour of its death'. Because the finite always points beyond its limit, the next question is the infinite.
explain.zh: 定在（Dasein）是有规定性的存在，这种直接的规定性就是质。质包含否定：正如斯宾诺莎所说、黑格尔所强调的，一切规定都是否定。于是有了某物与他物：某物之所以是某物，在于它不是他物，而他物本身也是一个某物。界限（Grenze）把它们分开，又同时属于双方；某物只有在界限之内、并通过界限，才是它所是的。界限属于自身本性的某物是有限的：它在自身中带着自己的终结，“它的诞生之时就是它的死亡之时”。有限物总要指向界限之外，于是引出无限的问题。

example.en: Hegel's own case: a piece of land three acres in size has a quantitative limit, but it is also a meadow and not a wood or a pond, and that is its qualitative limit. Move the fence and the meadow is still a meadow; let trees take over and it stops being one. Programmers know the idea from types: a value is an int precisely by excluding strings and lists, and the boundary of the type both defines and restricts it.
example.zh: 黑格尔自己的例子：一块三英亩大小的土地，这是它的量的界限；但它还是一片草地，而不是树林或池塘，这是它的质的界限。把篱笆挪一挪，草地仍是草地；让树木长满，它就不再是草地了。程序员从类型中也熟悉这个思想：一个值之所以是 int，正因为它排除了字符串和列表，类型的边界既规定了它，也限制了它。

image.en: A white picket fence rings a small square of lawn, and inside it a white rabbit sits contentedly: the meadow. Just outside grow a tree and a round pond with a yellow duck. The rabbit turns its nose toward the pond, and the fence that keeps the meadow a meadow is exactly where the meadow stops.
image.zh: 一圈白色尖桩篱笆围着一小块方形草地，里面一只白兔悠闲地坐着：这就是草地。篱笆外面有一棵树，还有一个圆池塘，池里浮着一只黄鸭。兔子把鼻子转向池塘。正是这道篱笆让草地成为草地，也正是在这里，草地到了尽头。

means.en: the limit: it makes the meadow a meadow
means.zh: 界限：它让草地成为草地

means.en: the other: a meadow is not a wood or a pond
means.zh: 他物：草地不是树林，也不是池塘

means.en: the limit separates and connects something and other
means.zh: 界限既分开又连接某物与他物

means.en: finitude: something carries its end within itself
means.zh: 有限性：某物在自身中带着终结

summary.en: The spurious infinite is an endless 'and so on' beyond the finite, like a line; the true infinite is the finite returning into itself, like a circle.
summary.zh: 坏无限是有限之外无穷无尽的“如此等等”，像一条直线；真无限是有限回到自身，像一个圆。

explain.en: The finite must go beyond its limit, but each beyond is a new finite with a new limit: finite, infinite, finite, and so on forever. This endless progression is the spurious (bad) infinite, a perpetual 'ought' that never arrives. Worse, an infinite set over against the finite is limited by it, and so is only another finite. The true infinite does not lie beyond the finite; it is the process in which the finite, in going beyond itself, meets only itself. Hegel's images: the spurious infinite is a straight line running off in both directions, with the infinite only at its ends, where the line never is; the true infinite is a circle, closed and wholly present, without beginning or end. This self-relating being is being-for-self.
explain.zh: 有限物必须超出自己的界限，可每次超出又遇到一个有新界限的有限物：有限、无限、有限……永无止境。黑格尔把这种无尽的进展叫作坏无限（schlechte Unendlichkeit）：一个永远到达不了的“应当”。更糟的是，与有限对立的无限受有限限制，自己也只是另一个有限。真无限不在有限之外，而是这样一个过程：有限在超出自身时只遇到它自己。黑格尔的形象是：坏无限是向两端无限延伸的直线，无限只在它永远到不了的两端；真无限是一个圆，自身封闭、完全在场，没有起点也没有终点。这种自我关联的存在就是自为存在。

example.en: Count 1, 2, 3, … and you never arrive: each new number is just another finite one. That is the spurious infinite, a while-loop with no exit. A recursive definition is a better picture of the true infinite: 'a list is either empty or an item followed by a list'. The definition is finite and refers back to itself, yet it covers lists of every length. The infinite is not reached at the end of a chase; it is present in the self-relation.
example.zh: 数 1、2、3……永远数不到头：每个新数都只是又一个有限的数。这就是坏无限，一个没有出口的 while 循环。递归定义更像真无限：“列表要么为空，要么是一个元素后面跟着一个列表。”这个定义是有限的，并且回指自身，却涵盖了任意长度的列表。无限不是在追逐的尽头才达到的，它就在这种自我关联之中。

image.en: A runner sprints along a long number line laid across the garden, panting after a golden star that always floats one step ahead. Behind him a big golden wheel stands upright, a perfect circle with no start and no end, and a ginger cat sits calmly beside it, watching the runner.
image.zh: 一个跑步的人沿着横放在花园里的长长数轴狂奔，气喘吁吁地追一颗总是领先他一步的金星。他身后立着一个巨大的金色车轮，一个没有起点也没有终点的完美的圆；一只橘猫静静地坐在轮旁，看着那个跑步的人。

means.en: spurious infinity: 'and so on' forever
means.zh: 坏无限：永远“如此等等”

means.en: the beyond as a perpetual 'ought'
means.zh: 彼岸：永远的“应当”

means.en: true infinity: a circle, closed, without beginning or end
means.zh: 真无限：自身封闭、无始无终的圆

means.en: at home with itself, chasing no beyond
means.zh: 安于自身，不追逐彼岸

title.en: Being-for-Self: The One and the Many

summary.en: Quality returned into itself is being-for-self, the One; it repels itself into many Ones that attract one another, and quality turns into quantity.
summary.zh: 回到自身的质就是自为存在，即“一”；一排斥自身成为许多的一，许多的一又相互吸引，质于是转为量。

explain.en: True infinity is being-for-self (Fürsichsein): being that relates only to itself and holds its other as a mere moment. Hegel's most familiar example is the I, which stays itself in all its contents. In its simplest form being-for-self is the One. But a One relates to itself by excluding, so it repels itself into many Ones; and since each of these is exactly like the others, repulsion is equally attraction, and they come together. Ancient atomism, atoms and the void, thought this stage. The outcome: the differences between the Ones are no longer qualitative, since one One is just like another. A determinacy indifferent to what a thing is remains: quality has passed over into quantity.
explain.zh: 真无限就是自为存在（Fürsichsein）：只与自身相关、把他物仅仅作为环节包含在内的存在。黑格尔最常举的例子是“我”，它在一切内容中都保持为它自己。自为存在最简单的形式是“一”。可是一要通过排斥他物来与自身相关，于是它把自身排斥为许多的一；而这许多的一彼此完全相同，排斥同样也是吸引，它们又聚到一起。古代原子论的“原子与虚空”思考的正是这一阶段。结果是：一与一之间不再有质的差别，这个一和那个一毫无二致。剩下的是对事物是什么漠不相关的规定性：质过渡为量。

example.en: Count sheep: each animal is a separate One, yet for counting it does not matter which is which. Ten identical sheep differ from eleven only in how many there are. Bits in memory behave the same way: a 1 in position 3 is just like a 1 in position 7, so a byte's meaning lies wholly in quantity and position (0b0000_1010 = 10). Once the Ones are indistinguishable, the only thing left to say about them is 'how many'.
example.zh: 数羊：每只羊都是一个独立的“一”，可数数时哪只是哪只无关紧要。十只一模一样的羊和十一只的区别只在于有多少。内存里的比特也一样：第 3 位上的 1 和第 7 位上的 1 毫无二致，一个字节的意义完全在于数量和位置（0b0000_1010 = 10）。一旦这些“一”无法区分，关于它们唯一能说的就只剩“有多少”。

image.en: On the garden lawn a lone sheep has sneezed itself into six identical sheep. They stand in a ring with their tails together and their heads pointing outward, pushing apart and clinging together at once. A shepherd in a cap cannot tell them apart and can only point and count: one, two, three…
image.zh: 花园草坪上，一只孤零零的羊打了个喷嚏，变成了六只一模一样的羊。它们尾巴挨着尾巴、头朝外站成一圈，既互相推开，又紧挨在一起。戴帽子的牧羊人分不清它们，只能指着数：一、二、三……

means.en: the One repels itself into many Ones
means.zh: “一”把自身排斥为许多的“一”

means.en: repulsion and attraction at once
means.zh: 排斥与吸引同时发生

means.en: no qualitative difference left between the Ones
means.zh: 各个“一”之间不再有质的差别

means.en: only quantity remains: the passage to quantity
means.zh: 只剩下量：过渡到量

summary.en: Size can change freely without changing what a thing is, until a measure is crossed and a new quality leaps out.
summary.zh: 大小可以随意变化而不改变事物是什么，直到越过某个度，新的质突然跃出。

summary.en: Quantity is a determinacy indifferent to what a thing is: a house stays a house whether it is larger or smaller.
summary.zh: 量是对事物“是什么”漠不相关的规定性：一座房子大一点、小一点，仍然是房子。

explain.en: Quantity is sublated quality: a determinacy that is external and indifferent to being. 'A house remains what it is, whether larger or smaller; red remains red, whether lighter or darker.' Pure quantity has two moments, continuity and discreteness: a stretch of space can be divided anywhere, yet it also consists of units you can count. A limited quantity is a quantum; its developed forms are number, an amount of units, and degree, an intensive magnitude such as temperature. A quantum can always be exceeded, so the spurious infinite returns as endless increase. But in a ratio a quantum's determinacy lies in its relation to another quantum, and quantity shows a qualitative side: the way to measure.
explain.zh: 量是被扬弃了的质：一种外在的、对存在漠不相关的规定性。“一座房子无论大一点还是小一点，仍然是房子；红色无论浅一点还是深一点，仍然是红色。”纯量包含连续性和分离性两个环节：一段空间可以在任何地方分割，同时又由可以计数的单位组成。被限定的量是定量，它的展开形式是数（若干个单位的数目）和程度，即温度这样的内涵量。定量总可以被超出，坏无限于是以无尽增大的形式重现。但在比率中，定量的规定性在于它与另一个定量的关系，量显出质的一面，于是通向度。

example.en: A recipe makes the moments concrete. 500 g of flour is a continuous magnitude: you could weigh out 437.2 g just as well. 12 eggs is discrete: you count them, and 12 is an amount of 12 units of one. An oven at 180 °C has a degree, an intensive magnitude: 180 °C is not 180 separate one-degree pieces. Doubling the recipe changes all the numbers and none of the dishes: a bigger cake is still a cake.
example.zh: 一份菜谱就能把这几个环节说清楚。500 克面粉是连续量：你同样可以称出 437.2 克。12 个鸡蛋是分离量：你一个个数，12 是 12 个单位“一”的数目。180 °C 的烤箱温度是程度，即内涵量：180 °C 并不是 180 个一度拼起来的。菜谱加倍，所有数字都变了，菜却一样也没变：大一点的蛋糕还是蛋糕。

image.en: On the kitchen floor stand three gingerbread houses: one mouse-sized, one shoebox-sized and one big enough for a dog. A mouse scurries into the smallest; a dog waits by the biggest. A pastry cook in a beret shrugs: all still houses. A tall thermometer at the side shows a degree, a quantity you cannot count off piece by piece.
image.zh: 厨房地上摆着三座姜饼屋：一座老鼠那么大，一座鞋盒那么大，一座大得能住下一条狗。一只老鼠钻进最小的那座，一条狗守在最大的那座旁边。戴贝雷帽的糕点师耸耸肩：都还是房子。旁边一支高高的温度计显示着热度，那是一种不能一块块数出来的量。

thing.en: three houses of very different sizes

means.en: quantity changes, quality stays: still houses
means.zh: 量变了，质不变：都还是房子

means.en: size is external to what a house is
means.zh: 大小对房子之为房子是外在的

means.en: indifference: the change makes no difference to the thing
means.zh: 漠不相关：变化不影响事物本身

means.en: degree: an intensive magnitude
means.zh: 程度：内涵量

summary.en: Measure is qualitative quantity: the range of size within which a thing stays what it is. Everything that exists has its measure.
summary.zh: 度是有质的量：事物在其中保持为自身的那个量的范围。一切存在的东西都有它的度。

explain.en: In measure (Maß) quality and quantity unite: a quantum that is no longer indifferent but bound to a quality. 'Everything that exists has a measure.' Within its measure a thing can grow or shrink and remain itself; beyond it, the thing becomes something else. Hegel notes that the Greeks honoured this: Nemesis punished whatever overstepped its measure. In nature, measures appear as specific ratios on which a quality depends, from the proportions in which chemical elements combine to the laws of planetary motion. Measure is therefore the first category in which quantity is grasped as meaningful rather than merely external. Its further development, the nodal line, shows what happens at the edges of a measure.
explain.zh: 在度（Maß）中，质与量统一起来：一个不再漠不相关、而与某种质结合在一起的定量。“一切存在的东西都有一个度。”在度的范围内，事物可以变大变小而仍然是自己；超出了度，它就变成别的东西。黑格尔指出希腊人早已敬畏这一点：涅墨西斯惩罚一切越出其度的东西。在自然中，度表现为某种质所依赖的特定比率，从化学元素化合的比例到行星运动的定律。所以度是第一个把量理解为有意义、而不只是外在的范畴。它的进一步发展，即关节线，揭示度的边缘会发生什么。

example.en: Salt in the pot: a well-seasoned soup has roughly 8–10 g of salt per litre, and within that band a few grams more or less change nothing essential. Keep adding, and at around 35 g per litre you have the saltiness of seawater, no longer soup. Chemistry gives sharper measures: hydrogen and oxygen form water only in the fixed mass ratio of about 1 : 8; other proportions give another substance or leave an unreacted remainder.
example.zh: 锅里的盐：一锅咸淡合适的汤，每升大约含 8–10 克盐，在这个范围内多几克少几克，汤还是那锅汤。一直加下去，到每升35 克左右，就是海水的咸度，再也不是汤了。化学给出更精确的度：氢和氧只有在大约 1 : 8 的固定质量比下才化合成水；别的比例要么得到别的物质，要么剩下没反应的部分。

image.en: A chef in a tall hat stirs a big bubbling cauldron while a giant jar of salt waits beside him for spoon after spoon; it is still soup. Next to the pot a fish leaps hopefully out of a bucket, thinking 'Sea yet?', waiting for the moment the soup turns into the sea.
image.zh: 戴高帽的厨师搅着一口咕嘟冒泡的大锅，旁边一只巨大的盐罐等着他一勺又一勺地加盐；锅里仍然是汤。锅边，一条鱼满怀期待地从水桶里跃起，心想“成海了吗？”，等着这锅汤变成大海的那一刻。

means.en: within its measure a thing stays what it is
means.zh: 在度的范围内，事物保持为自身

means.en: the quantity being changed
means.zh: 正在改变的量

means.en: beyond the measure a new quality: soup becomes sea
means.zh: 超出度就有新的质：汤变成海

means.en: the measure has an edge, even if we cannot see it yet
means.zh: 度有边界，哪怕还没看见

title.en: The Nodal Line: Quantity into Quality

summary.en: Gradual change of quantity reaches a node where the quality changes in a leap, as water freezes at 0 °C and boils at 100 °C.
summary.zh: 量的逐渐变化到达一个关节点，质就飞跃式地改变，就像水在 0 °C 结冰、在 100 °C 沸腾。

explain.en: Measures form a 'nodal line': along a scale of quantity, stretches where the quality holds steady alternate with nodes where it suddenly changes. Water cooled degree by degree does not get gradually harder; at the freezing point it becomes ice, and heated it turns to steam. Gradualness explains nothing at the nodes, so Hegel insists on leaps; the ancient puzzles of the heap and the bald head are about such thresholds. Pushed to the limit, measure meets the 'measureless': qualities keep turning into one another, and what persists through them is an indifferent substrate. The true object is then what lies beneath being's changing surface, and being passes into essence. Engels later made 'quantity into quality' a law of dialectics.
explain.zh: 各种度构成一条“关节线”：在量的标尺上，质保持不变的区段与质突然改变的关节点交替出现。水一度一度地冷却，并不会慢慢变硬，而是到冰点时变成冰；加热时，它会化为蒸汽。在关节点上，渐进性什么也解释不了，所以黑格尔强调飞跃；古代的“谷堆”与“秃头”难题说的正是这种阈值。推到极端，度遇到“无度”：各种质不断相互转化，在其中持存的是一个漠不相关的基质。于是真正的对象是存在变化着的表面之下的东西，存在过渡到本质。恩格斯后来把“量转化为质”定为辩证法的一条规律。

example.en: At 1 atm, heating 1 kg of water from 20 °C to 100 °C takes about 335 kJ, and the temperature climbs steadily. At 100 °C the thermometer stops: another 2,257 kJ go in with no rise at all, and only then is the water steam. Melting ice at 0 °C likewise absorbs 334 kJ per kg with no change of temperature. The heat added changes smoothly; the quality changes at a node.
example.zh: 在 1 个大气压下，把 1 千克水从 20 °C 加热到 100 °C 约需 335 千焦，温度一路平稳上升。到了 100 °C，温度计停住了：再输入 2257 千焦，温度一点也不升，水才变成蒸汽。冰在 0 °C 融化同样每千克要吸收 334 千焦，温度不变。输入的热量平滑地变化，质却在关节点上改变。

image.en: At the back stands a kitchen range with a copper kettle on top, rattling and blasting out steam, and a giant thermometer beside it reads hot. At the other end a block of ice sits next to a thermometer reading cold. In between, a cook in a cap holds up a stopwatch, waiting for the exact instant of the leap.
image.zh: 后面立着一台炉灶，上面的铜水壶咔嗒作响、喷着蒸汽，旁边的巨型温度计指向高温。另一头的冰块旁，温度计指向低温。两者之间，一个戴帽子的厨子举着秒表，等着飞跃发生的那一瞬间。

means.en: below the node: the solid quality
means.zh: 关节点以下：固态这种质

means.en: past the node: a new quality, gas
means.zh: 越过关节点：新的质，气态

means.en: steady quantitative change along the scale
means.zh: 沿标尺平稳的量变

means.en: the leap happens at a sharp threshold, not gradually
means.zh: 飞跃发生在确定的阈值上，而不是逐渐的

summary.en: Being turns inward. Essence seems to lie behind the surface, yet it must appear: reflection, ground, appearance and, finally, actuality.
summary.zh: 存在转向自身。本质看似藏在表面之后，却必定显现：反思、根据、现象，最后是现实。

summary.en: Essence as reflection into itself, and its paired determinations: identity, difference, contradiction, ground.
summary.zh: 本质作为向自身的反思，以及成对出现的反思规定：同一、差异、矛盾、根据。

summary.en: Essence is being that has gone into itself; the 'shine' that seems to hide it is essence's own showing.
summary.zh: 本质是深入自身的存在；看似遮蔽它的假象，其实是本质自己的映现。

explain.en: The Doctrine of Essence begins when being turns inward. Hegel plays on the German: Wesen (essence) echoes gewesen (has been), so essence is being that is 'timelessly past', kept and gone into itself. At first essence is set against the inessential, which looks like mere shine (Schein, illusory being). But shine has no source of its own; it is essence's own reflecting, as light shows itself by bouncing back from a mirror. So the movement of essence is called reflection. The categories of being pass over into one another; the categories of essence come in pairs that shine into each other: identity and difference, ground and grounded, inner and outer.
explain.zh: 存在转向自身，逻辑学就进入了本质论。黑格尔借德语双关：Wesen（本质）与 gewesen（曾在）相通，本质是“无时间地过去了的存在”，被保存下来并深入自身。起初本质与非本质相对，非本质看来只是假象（Schein）。但假象没有自己的来源，它就是本质自身的映现，正像光照到镜面又反射回来。所以本质的运动叫作反思（Reflexion）。存在论的范畴彼此过渡，本质论的范畴则成对出现、相互映照：同一与差异、根据与有根据者、内与外。

example.en: A friend snaps at a harmless joke. You could dismiss it as a mere surface mood, or you could ask what it shows. Taken as shine, the outburst is neither nothing nor a mask over some hidden friend who never appears: it is the friend's own character showing itself. Hegel's target is the sceptic, for whom shine has nothing behind it, and Kant, for whom something unknowable stands behind it.
example.zh: 朋友因一句无伤大雅的玩笑发了火。你可以说那只是表面情绪，也可以追问它显露了什么。作为假象，这次发火既不是虚无，也不是遮住某个永不露面的“真朋友”的面具，而正是他的性格在映现自身。黑格尔批评的是怀疑论（假象背后什么也没有）和康德（假象背后有不可知之物）。

image.en: In a hall of gilt mirrors three tall mirrors curve around a big glowing lantern, and each throws its light back into the room. A curious visitor in a beret has crept behind the middle mirror to find the 'real' lantern hidden back there. All she finds is the mirror's plain wooden back: the light was only ever the lantern's own. A row of candles flickers at the front.
image.zh: 镜厅里，三面高大的镜子围着一盏发光的大灯笼，每面镜子都把光反射回厅中。一位戴贝雷帽的好奇访客绕到中间那面镜子背后，想找藏在后面的“真灯笼”，却只看见镜子朴素的木头背板：光从来都是灯笼自己的光。台前一排蜡烛摇曳着。

means.en: essence, the source of the shining
means.zh: 本质，映现的源头

means.en: reflection: essence showing itself
means.zh: 反思：本质映现自身

means.en: looking for a hidden thing behind the shine finds nothing
means.zh: 在假象背后找隐藏之物，一无所获

summary.en: Abstract identity, A = A, says nothing; real identity contains difference, which deepens into diversity and opposition.
summary.zh: 抽象同一 A=A 空无内容；真正的同一包含差异，差异再展开为杂多与对立。

explain.en: The first determination of reflection is identity. Taken abstractly, as the law A = A, it is an empty tautology: 'a plant is a plant' tells you nothing. A statement says something only when its predicate differs from its subject, so identity already involves difference. Difference first appears as diversity: things that are merely unlike and are compared from outside (Leibniz: no two leaves are exactly alike). It sharpens into opposition, where each side is what it is only through its other: positive and negative, north and south pole, assets and debts. Opposition pushed to the end is contradiction.
explain.zh: 第一个反思规定是同一。抽象地看，同一律 A=A 只是空洞的同语反复：“植物就是植物”什么也没说。一句话要说出点什么，谓词就得不同于主词，所以同一本身已经包含差异。差异先表现为杂多：事物只是彼此不同，由外在的比较来确定（莱布尼茨：没有两片完全相同的树叶）。差异再激化为对立：每一方都只有通过对方才是自身，如正与负、南极与北极、财产与债务。对立推到底就是矛盾。

example.en: +5 and −5 are opposites, and each is defined only relative to the other. In bookkeeping the same 100 dollars is an asset for the lender and a debt for the borrower. Cut a bar magnet in half and you never get a lone north pole: each piece again has both poles.
example.zh: +5 与 −5 是对立的，各自只有相对于对方才有意义。记账时，同样的 100 美元对出借人是资产，对借款人是债务。把条形磁铁切成两半，也得不到单独的北极：每一半又各有两极。

image.en: A green parrot on a crate squawks 'A = A!' over and over, and its owner shrugs: nothing has been said. Nearby a botanist in a cap kneels with a magnifier over two big leaves that look identical, and finds that they differ. In front lies a red horseshoe magnet, its two poles held apart, each pole meaningless without the other.
image.zh: 木箱上一只绿鹦鹉一遍遍尖叫“A＝A！”，主人耸耸肩：什么也没说。旁边戴帽的植物学家跪着，用放大镜看两片一模一样的大叶子，发现它们并不相同。前面躺着一块红色马蹄形磁铁，两极分开，缺了哪一极另一极都无从谈起。

means.en: abstract identity, an empty tautology
means.zh: 抽象同一，空洞的同语反复

means.en: diversity: no two leaves are exactly alike
means.zh: 杂多：没有两片相同的树叶

means.en: opposition: each pole exists only through the other
means.zh: 对立：每一极只因对方而存在

summary.en: Opposition driven to its end is contradiction, which for Hegel is the root of all movement and life, not just an error.
summary.zh: 对立推到极致就是矛盾；在黑格尔看来，它是一切运动和生命的根源，而不只是错误。

explain.en: Each opposite excludes its other and yet depends on it for its own meaning; held together, this is contradiction. Hegel turns the usual view around: 'all things are in themselves contradictory', and contradiction is 'the root of all movement and vitality'. A thing moves, has drives and is alive only because it holds a contradiction within itself and endures it. His example is motion: a moving body is here and not here at one and the same moment. Whether Hegel rejects the formal law of non-contradiction is contested; the mainstream reading is that he targets finite things and fixed concepts, not valid inference. Contradiction does not stay put: it resolves by 'going to the ground'.
explain.zh: 对立的每一方都排斥对方，却又依赖对方才有意义；把这两点合在一起，就是矛盾。黑格尔把通常的看法倒转过来：“一切事物本身都是自相矛盾的”，矛盾是“一切运动和生命力的根源”。事物只因自身包含矛盾并能承受它，才会运动、才有冲动、才有生命。他的例子是运动：运动的物体在同一瞬间既在这里又不在这里。黑格尔是否否定形式逻辑的矛盾律，学界有争议；主流解读认为他针对的是有限事物和僵硬的概念，而非有效推理。矛盾不会停留不动，它通过“走向根据”而消解。

example.en: Zeno argued that a flying arrow cannot move, because at each instant it simply occupies one place. Hegel answers that motion is 'existent contradiction': the moving body is in one place and at the same time not in it. Kant's antinomies are a second case: reason can prove both that the world has a beginning in time and that it has none. Kant blamed reason; Hegel says contradiction is in things themselves.
example.zh: 芝诺论证飞矢不动：在每一瞬间，箭都只占据一个位置。黑格尔回答：运动就是“实存着的矛盾”，运动的物体在同一处又不在同一处。康德的二律背反是另一例：理性既能证明世界在时间上有开端，也能证明它没有开端。康德把责任归于理性，黑格尔说矛盾就在事物本身。

image.en: A giant golden arrow hangs in mid-air in front of a signpost whose two boards read HERE and NOT HERE, pointing opposite ways at once. Below it a spotted dog chases its own tail in a frantic circle: it keeps spinning only because it is at odds with itself. A gentleman in a top hat throws up his hands.
image.zh: 一支金色巨箭悬在半空，背后的路标两块指示牌写着“在此”和“不在此”，同时指向相反的方向。箭下一只花斑狗疯狂地追着自己的尾巴转圈：正因为它跟自己过不去，才停不下来。戴礼帽的绅士无奈地摊开双手。

means.en: motion: here and not here at one moment
means.zh: 运动：同一瞬间在此又不在此

means.en: the two opposed sides held together
means.zh: 两个对立面被合在一起

means.en: contradiction as the drive of movement and life
means.zh: 矛盾是运动与生命的动力

summary.en: Contradiction 'goes to ground' (zugrunde gehen): it perishes and, in perishing, reaches the ground it stood on.
summary.zh: 矛盾“走向根据”（zugrunde gehen）：它在毁灭中退回到自己一直立足的根据。

explain.en: German zugrunde gehen means 'to perish', but literally 'to go to the ground'. Hegel uses the pun: what contradicts itself collapses, and what it collapses into is its ground (Grund). Ground is essence as the basis from which something follows; this is Hegel's reading of the principle of sufficient reason. Ground and grounded have the same content in different forms, so a merely formal ground explains nothing. Hegel works through form and essence, form and matter, form and content. A real ground needs conditions: when all the conditions of a thing are present, the thing steps into existence. So ground passes over into existence and then into appearance.
explain.zh: 德语 zugrunde gehen 意为“毁灭”，字面却是“走到根据里去”。黑格尔用这个双关说：自相矛盾的东西崩塌了，而它崩塌所归入的正是它的根据（Grund）。根据是作为某物所由出之基础的本质，这是黑格尔对充足理由律的思辨解读。根据与有根据者内容相同、形式不同，所以单纯形式的根据什么也解释不了。黑格尔依次讨论形式与本质、形式与质料、形式与内容。真正的根据需要条件：一件事的条件全部具备，它就进入实存。根据由此过渡为实存，再展开为现象。

example.en: Molière's quack doctor explains that opium puts people to sleep because it has a 'dormitive virtue'. That is a formal ground: it restates the effect as a hidden power. A real explanation names conditions: morphine in the drug binding to opioid receptors in the brain, a sufficient dose, a body that absorbs it. When all are present, sleep follows.
example.zh: 莫里哀笔下的庸医解释说，鸦片使人入睡，是因为它有“催眠力”。这是形式的根据：只是把结果换个说法，说成一种隐藏的力。真正的解释要列出条件：药中的吗啡与脑内阿片受体结合、剂量足够、身体能吸收。条件全部具备，睡眠就随之而来。

image.en: A wall of red toy bricks has crashed down into rubble. Where it stood, a worker in a hard hat kneels and points at what the wall was hiding: a huge flat foundation stone, on which a small stone tower already stands. Three crates wait around it like conditions to be gathered.
image.zh: 一堵红色积木墙轰然倒塌，碎了一地。在墙原先的位置，戴安全帽的工人跪下来，指着墙一直遮住的东西：一块巨大平整的基石，上面已经立起一座小石塔。旁边三只木箱，像等着凑齐的条件。

means.en: contradiction perishing: zugrunde gehen
means.zh: 矛盾毁灭：走向根据

means.en: the ground it was standing on all along
means.zh: 它一直立足的根据

means.en: the grounded, same content in another form
means.zh: 有根据者：同一内容，另一形式

means.en: conditions that bring a thing into existence
means.zh: 使事物进入实存的条件

summary.en: Essence must appear; when inner and outer are one, we reach actuality and the absolute relation.
summary.zh: 本质必定显现；内外合一，就达到现实性与绝对关系。

summary.en: Essence must appear. Appearance is not a veil, and its stable content is law, 'the tranquil image' of the shifting world.
summary.zh: 本质必定显现。现象不是面纱，现象中稳定不变的内容就是规律。

explain.en: When ground and conditions are complete, the thing comes into existence: essence becomes a world of existing things with properties and relations. Existence known as the showing of essence is appearance (Erscheinung). Against Kant, who left the thing in itself unknowable behind appearances, Hegel insists that essence is not behind appearance: it appears, and an essence that never showed itself would be empty. Within the shifting play of appearances something stays the same, and that is law. Hegel calls the realm of laws 'the tranquil image of the world of appearance'. A law captures only part of what appears, so the two must be bound more tightly, which happens in the essential relation.
explain.zh: 根据与条件齐备，事物便进入实存：本质成为一个由具有性质和关系的事物构成的世界。被认作本质之显现的实存，就是现象（Erscheinung）。康德把物自体留在现象背后、不可认识；黑格尔反对说，本质不在现象背后，它就显现出来，从不显现的本质只是空洞的。在变动不居的现象中有保持不变的东西，那就是规律。黑格尔称规律的王国是“现象世界的静止映像”。但规律只抓住了现象的一部分，两者还要更紧密地结合，这就是本质的关系。

example.en: A pendulum's swings vary with how hard you push it, with the air and with friction. Yet for small swings the period stays T = 2π√(L/g). For L = 1 m and g = 9.81 m/s², T ≈ 2.0 s, however you start it. The law is not hidden behind the swinging; it is the calm, repeatable content of the swinging itself.
example.zh: 单摆怎么摆，取决于推它的力度、空气和摩擦。但只要摆幅小，周期总是 T = 2π√(L/g)。L = 1 米、g = 9.81 米/秒² 时，无论怎样起摆，T 都约为 2.0 秒。规律并不藏在摆动背后，它就是摆动本身那平静、可重复的内容。

image.en: In front of the bank vault a huge brass pendulum swings wildly to and fro. Beside it stands a blackboard with one calm chalked line, T = 2π√(L/g), which does not move however the pendulum lurches. A child in a cap times the swings with a stopwatch, and a robot clerk nods at the board.
image.zh: 银行金库前，一只巨大的黄铜摆疯狂地来回摆动。旁边的黑板上只用粉笔写着平静的一行：T = 2π√(L/g)，摆再怎么晃，这行字纹丝不动。戴帽的孩子拿着秒表给摆计时，一个机器人职员对着黑板点头。

means.en: the shifting play of appearance
means.zh: 变动不居的现象

means.en: law: the tranquil image of appearance
means.zh: 规律：现象的静止映像

means.en: the law is read off the appearances
means.zh: 规律从现象中读出

summary.en: Whole and parts, force and its expression, inner and outer: what something is inwardly is exactly what it shows outwardly.
summary.zh: 整体与部分、力与表现、内与外：内在的东西，恰恰就是它外在表现出来的东西。

explain.en: Appearance turns out to be a relation of two sides, each of which is what it is only through the other. Hegel runs through three forms. Whole and parts: a whole is nothing apart from its parts, yet parts are parts only of a whole. Force and its expression: a force that never expresses itself is no force; it exists in its expression. Inner and outer: what something is inwardly, it is outwardly, and the reverse. Hegel applies this to people: a man is the series of his deeds, and talents that never show in any work are an empty boast. When inner and outer are known to be one, essence and existence coincide, and we reach actuality.
explain.zh: 现象原来是两方面的关系，每一方都只有通过另一方才是它自身。黑格尔考察了三种形式。整体与部分：整体离开部分什么也不是，部分也只是整体的部分。力与其表现：从不表现的力就不是力，力就存在于它的表现中。内与外：一个东西内在是什么，外在就是什么，反之亦然。黑格尔把这用到人身上：人就是他的一系列行为，从未在任何作品中表现出来的“才华”只是空话。当内与外被认作同一，本质与实存就合而为一，这就是现实性。

example.en: A student says, 'I'm brilliant, my exams just don't show it.' Hegel's answer: a talent that never appears in answers, work or projects is not a talent you have. Likewise a spring's stiffness is nothing over and above how it pushes back. By Hooke's law F = kx, a spring with k = 200 N/m pushes back with 10 N when compressed by 5 cm.
example.zh: 学生说：“我其实很聪明，只是考试没体现出来。”黑格尔会回答：从未在答题、作业或项目中显现的才华，就不是你拥有的才华。同样，弹簧的劲度不在它的回弹之外。按胡克定律 F = kx，k = 200 牛/米的弹簧压缩 5 厘米，就以 10 牛的力回弹。

image.en: A banker in a top hat swings open a big steel safe to show off his 'hidden genius', and the safe is empty. He shrugs. Everything he really has stands in plain sight in front of it: a row of gold coin stacks, one for each deed he has done. On top of the safe a coiled spring shows its force only by pushing a red ball up.
image.zh: 戴礼帽的银行家拉开一只大钢保险柜，想炫耀他“藏在里面的天才”，柜子却是空的。他耸耸肩。他真正拥有的一切都摆在柜前、一目了然：一排金币堆，每一堆是他做过的一件事。保险柜顶上，一根弹簧只靠把红球顶起来显示它的力。

means.en: an 'inner' that never appears is empty
means.zh: 从不显现的“内在”是空的

means.en: a person is the series of his deeds
means.zh: 人就是他的一系列行为

means.en: force exists only in its expression
means.zh: 力只存在于它的表现中

summary.en: Actuality is the unity of essence and existence: 'what is rational is actual, and what is actual is rational'.
summary.zh: 现实是本质与实存的统一：“凡是合乎理性的都是现实的，凡是现实的都是合乎理性的。”

explain.en: Actuality (Wirklichkeit) is where inner and outer, essence and existence, have become one. It is a technical term, not a name for whatever happens to exist: a passing whim, an error or a rotten institution exists but is not actual in Hegel's sense. That is how he glosses (Encyclopaedia §6) the famous line from the preface to the Philosophy of Right. Whether it defends the status quo or demands that reality be made rational has been argued over since his own students. Actuality unfolds through the modal categories: possibility, contingency (what could be otherwise) and necessity. When all of a thing's conditions are present, it cannot fail to be: real possibility is necessity.
