explain.zh: 现实（Wirklichkeit）是内与外、本质与实存合而为一之处。它是专门术语，并不指随便什么存在着的东西：一时的念头、错误或腐朽的制度虽然存在，却不是黑格尔意义上的现实。他自己在《哲学全书》第 6 节这样解释《法哲学原理》序言中的那句名言。这句话是在为现状辩护，还是要求让现实变得合理，从他的学生那一代起就争论不休。现实性展开为模态范畴：可能性、偶然性（可以是别样的）和必然性。事物的条件全部具备时，它就不可能不出现：实在的可能性就是必然性。

example.en: An acorn is possibly an oak. Whether this acorn grows depends on contingent conditions: soil, rain, squirrels. If all the conditions are present, the oak cannot fail to grow, and real possibility has become necessity. A corrupt state exists, but in Hegel's sense it is not fully actual, because its existence does not match what a state is.
example.zh: 橡子可能长成橡树。这颗橡子能否长成，取决于土壤、雨水、松鼠等偶然条件。条件全部具备，橡树就不可能不长出来，实在的可能性成了必然性。一个腐败的国家虽然存在，但在黑格尔的意义上并不完全现实，因为它的存在不符合国家的概念。

image.en: The great round vault door at the back stands open, and out of it strides a cheerful banker: what was inside has stepped outside. Before him lie the three modes of actuality: a green sprout for possibility, a fat die tumbling for contingency, and a heavy iron chain for necessity.
image.zh: 后方巨大的圆形金库门敞开着，一位兴高采烈的银行家从里面大步走出：里面的东西走到了外面。他面前摆着现实性的三种模态：一株嫩芽代表可能性，一颗翻滚的大骰子代表偶然性，一条沉重的铁链代表必然性。

thing.en: banker striding out of the vault

means.en: inner and outer become one: actuality
means.zh: 内外合一：现实

means.en: possibility
means.zh: 可能性

means.en: contingency: could be otherwise
means.zh: 偶然性：可以是别样的

means.en: necessity: all conditions present
means.zh: 必然性：条件全部具备

summary.en: The absolute relation: substance and accidents, cause and effect, and reciprocal action, whose truth is the freedom of the concept.
summary.zh: 绝对关系：实体与偶性、原因与结果、相互作用；它的真理是概念的自由。

explain.en: Essence ends with the absolute relation, with Spinoza in view. Substance is the power that shows itself in its accidents, which come and go. Causality splits this power into cause and effect: the cause passes wholly into its effect, and the effect contains nothing that was not in the cause. But every cause is itself an effect, and following the chain back leads to a spurious infinite. In reciprocal action each side is cause and effect of the other at once, so the chain closes into a circle. What looked like external necessity is then seen as self-determination: 'the truth of necessity is freedom, and the truth of substance is the concept'. The Logic passes from essence to the concept.
explain.zh: 本质论以绝对关系告终，矛头指向斯宾诺莎。实体是在偶性中显示自身的力量，偶性来来去去。因果关系把这力量分成原因与结果：原因完全过渡到结果中，结果里没有原因中没有的东西。但每个原因本身又是结果，沿因果链往回追，就陷入坏的无限。在相互作用中，双方同时互为因果，链条闭合成圆圈。看似外在的必然性于是被看透为自我规定：“必然性的真理是自由，实体的真理是概念。”逻辑学由本质论进入概念论。

example.en: Hegel's example: the customs of the Spartans were an effect of their constitution, and their constitution an effect of their customs. Each explains the other, so neither is simply first. A thermostat gives a modern case: the heater raises the room's temperature, and the temperature switches the heater on and off. Asking which is the cause misses the one system that maintains itself.
example.zh: 黑格尔的例子：斯巴达人的风俗是其政制的结果，其政制又是其风俗的结果。两者互相解释，谁也不是单纯的起点。恒温器是现代的例子：暖气让室温升高，室温又控制暖气开关。追问谁是原因，就错过了那个自我维持的整体。

image.en: Twelve dominoes stand in a ring. The first knocks the second, the second the third, and so on round, until the twelfth knocks the first again: cause and effect have bent into a circle. In the middle stands a calm figure in a crown, cheering. She is no longer pushed by the chain; the ring is her own motion.
image.zh: 十二块多米诺骨牌围成一圈。第一块推倒第二块，第二块推倒第三块，一路转下去，第十二块又推倒了第一块：因果弯成了一个圆。圆心站着一位戴王冠的人，从容地欢呼。她不再被链条推着走，这个圆就是她自己的运动。

means.en: reciprocity: cause and effect close into a circle
means.zh: 相互作用：因果闭合成圆

means.en: every effect is also a cause
means.zh: 每个结果也是原因

means.en: necessity seen through as freedom: the concept
means.zh: 必然性被看透为自由：概念

summary.en: Thought that is free: the concept as subject (judgment, syllogism), as object (from mechanism to purpose) and as idea.
summary.zh: 自由的思维：概念作为主体（判断、推理），作为客体（从机械性到目的性），最后作为理念。

summary.en: The concept and its three moments; it divides itself in judgment and reunites in the syllogism.
summary.zh: 概念及其三个环节；它在判断中自我分割，又在推理中重新联合。

summary.en: The concept has three moments, universality, particularity and individuality, and each of them contains the other two.
summary.zh: 概念有普遍性、特殊性、个别性三个环节，每一个环节都包含另外两个。

explain.en: With the concept (Begriff) the Logic reaches thought that is free. The concept is not a general idea that the mind abstracts from things, but a self-determining whole. Its universality is concrete: it particularises itself into kinds and is actual only in individuals, while each individual is a particular embodiment of the universal. So the three moments are not three separate items. Universality is the identity running through all, particularity is its self-differentiation, and individuality is its return to itself in a definite this. Hegel contrasts Rousseau's general will with the will of all: the general will is not a sum of private wishes. Next the concept divides itself, and that is judgment.
explain.zh: 到了概念（Begriff），逻辑学达到了自由的思维。概念不是头脑从事物中抽出来的共同观念，而是自我规定的整体。它的普遍性是具体的：它把自己特殊化为各个种类，又只在个体中才现实存在；每个个体都是普遍者的一种特殊体现。所以三个环节不是三样分开的东西：普遍性是贯穿一切的同一，特殊性是它的自我区分，个别性是它在确定的“这一个”中回到自身。黑格尔借卢梭区分公意与众意：公意不是私人意愿的总和。接下来概念要分割自己，这就是判断。

example.en: Hegel mocks the invalid who is told to eat fruit and refuses cherries, plums and grapes, because each is a cherry, a plum or a grape and none is 'fruit'. Fruit (universal) exists only as kinds of fruit (particular) and, in the end, as this plum in my hand (individual). In code, an abstract class with no concrete instances is a loose analogy for the empty, abstract universal.
example.zh: 黑格尔嘲笑一个病人：医生让他吃水果，他却拒绝樱桃、李子和葡萄，因为它们分别是樱桃、李子、葡萄，没有一样是“水果”。水果（普遍）只作为各种水果（特殊）存在，最终是我手里的这颗李子（个别）。打个粗略的比方：没有任何具体实例的抽象类，就像空洞抽象的普遍。

image.en: In the courtroom a sick man in a hood slumps in the witness armchair and waves away a huge basket of grapes, pears and apples held out by a waiter in a chef's hat. 'Fruit!' cries his speech bubble: he wants fruit, not these. The fruit he asks for sits right in front of him, in three kinds.
image.zh: 法庭上，一个戴兜帽的病人瘫坐在证人席的扶手椅里，挥手推开戴厨师帽的侍者递来的一大篮葡萄、梨和苹果。他的对话框里喊着“要水果！”：他要的是水果，不是这些。可他要的水果就在眼前，分成三种。

means.en: the universal, actual only in its kinds
means.zh: 普遍，只在种类中现实存在

means.en: the particular kinds
means.zh: 特殊的种类

means.en: the individual, this one
means.zh: 个别，“这一个”

means.en: the empty abstract universal
means.zh: 空洞抽象的普遍

summary.en: In judgment (Urteil) the concept divides itself, an 'original division' (Ur-teilung), into subject and predicate: 'the individual is the universal'.
summary.zh: 判断（Urteil）是概念的“原始分割”（Ur-teilung）：把自己分为主词与谓词，“个别是普遍”。

explain.en: Hegel reads the German Urteil, playing on its parts, as Ur-teilung: 'original division'. In judgment the concept splits itself into subject and predicate and joins them again with the copula 'is'. Its basic form is 'the individual is the universal', so Hegel says that all things are a judgment. Judgments rise through four kinds: of existence ('the rose is red'), of reflection ('this plant is medicinal', 'all men are mortal'), of necessity ('gold is a metal') and of the concept ('this action is good'). At each step the predicate comes closer to the nature of the subject. The unity hidden in the little word 'is' must finally be spelled out by a middle term: the syllogism.
explain.zh: 黑格尔把德语 Urteil（判断）拆开来读，解作 Ur-teilung，即“原始的分割”。在判断中，概念把自己分成主词和谓词，再用系词“是”把它们连起来。判断的基本形式是“个别是普遍”，所以黑格尔说一切事物都是一个判断。判断依次上升为四类：定在判断（“玫瑰是红的”）、反思判断（“这种植物能治病”“所有人都会死”）、必然判断（“金是金属”）和概念判断（“这个行为是好的”）。每上升一步，谓词就更贴近主词的本性。藏在“是”字里的统一，最后要由中项明确说出来：这就是推理。

example.en: 'The rose is red' joins an individual to a quality it could lack: a white rose is still a rose. 'Gold is a metal' joins the subject to its genus, which it cannot lack. 'This house is good' measures the thing against its own concept, against what a house ought to be. All three are judgments, but the bond between subject and predicate grows tighter.
example.zh: “玫瑰是红的”把个体和一个它可以没有的性质连在一起：白玫瑰也是玫瑰。“金是金属”把主词和它不可能没有的类连在一起。“这座房子是好的”则用事物自己的概念，即房子应当是什么样，来衡量它。三者都是判断，但主词与谓词的联系越来越紧。

image.en: A giant pair of golden scissors stands in the middle of the courtroom, having just cut a sentence in two: on the left a sign reads 'the rose', on the right a sign reads 'is red'. Behind the scissors towers a huge red rose, the one thing that was divided. A robed judge raps his gavel.
image.zh: 法庭中央立着一把巨大的金剪刀，刚把一句话剪成两半：左边的牌子写着“玫瑰”，右边的牌子写着“是红的”。剪刀后面耸立着一朵巨大的红玫瑰，正是被分割的那一个。身穿法袍的法官敲响法槌。

means.en: Ur-teilung: the concept's original division
means.zh: 原始分割：概念的自我分割

means.en: subject and predicate
means.zh: 主词与谓词

means.en: the one concept that divides itself
means.zh: 分割自身的同一个概念

means.en: judging as a verdict that joins them
means.zh: 判断：把两端连起来的裁决

summary.en: The syllogism rejoins the two ends that judgment split apart through a middle term; 'everything rational is a syllogism'.
summary.zh: 推理借中项把判断中分开的两端重新联结起来：“一切理性的东西都是推理。”

explain.en: Judgment left subject and predicate joined only by an unexplained 'is'. The syllogism (Schluss, literally a closing) makes the bond explicit through a middle term. Its basic form joins individual and universal through the particular: Gaius is a man, men are mortal, so Gaius is mortal. Hegel claims that 'everything is a syllogism': anything rational is a whole whose moments are mediated by one another. In the three figures each moment takes its turn as the middle. Rationality is therefore not just a property of sentences; the solar system, the state and the whole system have this shape, and the Encyclopaedia ends with three syllogisms. When the mediation is complete and needs no outside link, the concept becomes an object: objectivity.
explain.zh: 判断只用一个未加说明的“是”把主词和谓词连起来。推理（Schluss，字面意思是“闭合”）通过中项把这种联系明确设定出来。基本形式是借特殊把个别和普遍联结起来：卡尤斯是人，人都会死，所以卡尤斯会死。黑格尔说“一切都是推理”：凡理性的东西都是一个整体，它的各环节彼此中介。在推理的三个格中，每个环节轮流充当中项。所以理性不只是句子的属性，太阳系、国家乃至整个体系都有这种形态，《哲学全书》正以三个推理收尾。中介一旦完成、不再需要外在联结，概念就成为客体：客观性。

example.en: I–P–U: Gaius (individual) is a man (particular); men are mortal (universal); so Gaius is mortal. In Hegel's account of the state, each of three terms, the individual person, the system of needs, and the government, serves in turn as the middle that links the other two (Encyclopaedia §198). Only when every term mediates and is mediated is the whole rational.
example.zh: 个别—特殊—普遍：卡尤斯（个别）是人（特殊），人都会死（普遍），所以卡尤斯会死。黑格尔论国家时说，个人、需要的体系、政府三项轮流充当中项，把另外两项联结起来（《哲学全书》第 198 节）。只有每一项既中介别人、又被别人中介，整体才是理性的。

image.en: A stone bridge arches across the stage. On its left bank stands the bust of Gaius; on its right bank grins a giant skull. Halfway across, a man in a graduation cap walks over the bridge: he is the middle term 'man', the only way from Gaius to mortality. A small dog trots after him.
image.zh: 一座石拱桥横跨舞台。左岸立着卡尤斯的胸像，右岸咧嘴笑着一颗巨大的骷髅。桥中央，一个戴学位帽的人正走过桥：他就是中项“人”，从卡尤斯通往“会死”的唯一道路。一只小狗跟在他后面一路小跑。

means.en: the individual extreme
means.zh: 个别的端项

means.en: the universal extreme: mortal
means.zh: 普遍的端项：会死

means.en: the middle term, the particular 'man'
means.zh: 中项：特殊的“人”

means.en: mediation that closes the two ends together
means.zh: 把两端闭合起来的中介

summary.en: The concept sunk into objects: external push, chemical affinity, purpose working through means.
summary.zh: 沉入客体中的概念：外在推动、化学亲和、借手段实现的目的。

summary.en: Objects that are indifferent to one another and related only from outside, by push and collision.
summary.zh: 客体彼此漠不相关，只靠外力的推动和碰撞发生联系。

explain.en: When the concept first becomes objective, its moments fall apart into separate objects. In mechanism each object is a self-contained whole that is indifferent to the others: whatever happens to it comes from outside, by pushing, pressure and collision, and it passes the motion on without being changed in what it is. Hegel finds the same pattern outside physics: learning by rote, mechanical religious practice, a state run like a machine. Mechanism rises to 'absolute mechanism', where objects are held together by a centre, as planets are by the sun; the Philosophy of Nature treats the real solar system. Objects that are inwardly related to one another take us to chemism.
explain.zh: 概念初次客观化时，它的环节分散为各自独立的客体。在机械性中，每个客体都是自成一体的整体，对别的客体漠不关心：它遭遇的一切都来自外部，即推、压和碰撞，它把运动传下去，自身是什么却不变。黑格尔在物理学之外也看到同样的模式：死记硬背、机械的宗教仪式、像机器一样运转的国家。机械性上升为“绝对的机械性”，客体由一个中心维系，就像行星由太阳维系；真实的太阳系在自然哲学中讨论。客体之间一旦有了内在关联，就进入化学性。

example.en: Billiard balls are Hegel's kind of mechanical object. A 0.17 kg ball moving at 2 m/s strikes an identical ball at rest. In an ideal elastic head-on collision the first stops and the second moves off at 2 m/s. Neither ball becomes anything else; the momentum, 0.34 kg·m/s, simply passes from one to the other.
example.zh: 台球就是黑格尔所说的机械客体。一个 0.17 千克的球以 2 米/秒撞上一个静止的相同球。理想的弹性正碰中，前一个球停下，后一个以 2 米/秒离开。两个球都没有变成别的东西，0.34 千克·米/秒的动量只是从一个球转到另一个球。

image.en: Four black bowling balls stand in a tight row on the workshop floor. A worker in a cap shoves the end ball hard; the knock runs down the line, and a fifth ball at the far end rolls away spinning. None of the balls cares about the others; each passes on only what it was given. Behind them an old gear train turns, all teeth and no purpose.
image.zh: 工坊地上，四个黑色保龄球紧挨着排成一行。戴帽的工人狠狠推了一下最末端的球，撞击沿着队列传过去，最远端的第五个球转着滚开了。没有一个球在乎别的球，每个球只是把收到的东西传下去。它们后面，一组旧齿轮在转，只有齿，没有目的。

means.en: objects indifferent to each other
means.zh: 彼此漠不相关的客体

means.en: all motion comes from outside
means.zh: 一切运动都来自外部

means.en: motion passed on unchanged in kind
means.zh: 运动被原样传递

means.en: a machine: mechanism without purpose
means.zh: 机器：没有目的的机械

summary.en: Objects with an affinity: each lacks the other, and together they neutralise into a product, as acid and base do.
summary.zh: 客体彼此有亲和性，各自缺少对方；结合后中和为一个产物，如酸与碱。

explain.en: In chemism objects are no longer indifferent. Each is one-sided and has a tension towards its other: it is what it is only in relation to what it lacks. Their union is a neutral product in which both are cancelled as separate things and preserved as moments, as acid and base vanish into a salt. But the process stops in its product, and to start again the product must be split apart from outside. Hegel finds chemism wherever things are drawn together by a lack, and by analogy in love and friendship. Since neither mechanism nor chemism contains its own end, the concept's next shape is purpose: teleology.
explain.zh: 在化学性中，客体不再漠不相关。每个客体都是片面的，带着朝向对方的张力：它之所以是它，只在于它与所缺之物的关系。二者的结合是一个中和的产物，双方作为分离之物被取消、作为环节被保留，就像酸和碱消失在盐里。但过程在产物中停了下来，要重新开始，必须从外部把产物分解。黑格尔认为，凡是因缺乏而相互吸引之处都有化学性，打个比方，爱情与友谊也是如此。机械性和化学性都不包含自己的目的，于是概念的下一个形态是目的：目的性。

example.en: Hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide react: HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O. Mix equal amounts, say 1 mol of each, and the solution is neutral, about pH 7 at 25 °C. The sharp acid and the caustic base are gone, and salt and water remain. Getting acid and base back takes an outside process such as electrolysis.
example.zh: 盐酸与氢氧化钠反应：HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O。各取 1 摩尔混合，溶液呈中性，25 °C 时 pH 约为 7。刺鼻的酸和腐蚀性的碱都不见了，只剩盐和水。要重新得到酸和碱，就需要电解之类的外部过程。

image.en: Over a bubbling cauldron two chemists strain towards each other from opposite sides, one dressed all in red, one all in blue, as if each were pulled by the other. A red flask stands by one and a blue flask by the other. What bubbles in the pot between them is neither red nor blue but a calm, neutral green. A red horseshoe magnet in front names the pull.
image.zh: 一口冒泡的大锅两边，两位化学家拼命朝对方探身，一个全身红衣，一个全身蓝衣，好像彼此在拉着对方。一个身旁立着红色烧瓶，另一个身旁立着蓝色烧瓶。两人之间锅里翻滚的，既不是红也不是蓝，而是平静中和的绿色。前面一块红色马蹄磁铁点明了这股吸引力。

means.en: two one-sided objects with affinity
means.zh: 两个有亲和性的片面客体

means.en: each is what it is only through what it lacks
means.zh: 各自只因所缺之物而是自身

means.en: the neutral product: both cancelled and kept
means.zh: 中和的产物：双方被取消又被保留

title.en: Teleology and the Cunning of Reason

summary.en: A purpose sets objects to work as its means and lets them wear each other out, while it stays intact: the cunning of reason.
summary.zh: 目的把客体当作手段，让它们彼此消耗，自己却保全下来：这就是理性的狡计。

explain.en: In teleology the concept exists for itself as a purpose (Zweck) that is realised through objects. The purpose does not grapple with the material directly. It puts another object, the means, between itself and the material, and lets mechanism and chemism do the work, so that objects rub each other down while the purpose survives untouched. Hegel calls this the cunning of reason. Hence his remark that the plough is more honourable than the enjoyments it procures: the tool lasts, the enjoyments pass. Every end achieved can become a means to a further end. In the realised purpose concept and objectivity are one, which is the idea. The phrase returns in the philosophy of history.
explain.zh: 在目的性中，概念作为目的（Zweck）自为地存在，并通过客体来实现。目的并不亲自与材料搏斗。它在自己和材料之间插入另一个客体，即手段，让机械和化学的作用去做工，于是客体彼此磨损，目的却毫发无伤。黑格尔称之为理性的狡计。所以他说，犁比它带来的享受更尊贵：工具留存，享受消逝。每个达成的目的又可以成为更远目的的手段。在实现了的目的中，概念与客观性合一，这就是理念。这个说法后来在历史哲学中再次出现。

example.en: A farmer wants bread. She does not tear at the soil with her hands; she sets an ox and a plough between herself and the field. Over the seasons the ploughshare wears down and the ox tires, but her purpose is carried out, and the plough passes to her children while each loaf is eaten in a day. The means outlast the satisfactions they serve.
example.zh: 农夫想要面包。她不会用手去刨地，而是在自己和田地之间放上牛和犁。年复一年，犁铧磨损、耕牛疲惫，但她的目的实现了；犁还会传给孩子，而每个面包一天就吃完了。手段比它所服务的享受更长久。

image.en: A craftsman lounges in an armchair, a glowing light bulb of purpose over his head, and does not lift a finger. An industrial robot arm pounds away at an anvil for him, and at its feet lies a heap of worn-out hammers. The work gets done, the tools are spent, and the craftsman has not been touched.
image.zh: 工匠懒洋洋地靠在扶手椅里，头顶亮着一只代表目的的灯泡，一根手指都不动。一台工业机械臂替他敲打着铁砧，脚下堆着一堆用坏了的锤子。活儿干完了，工具耗尽了，工匠自己却毫发无损。

means.en: the purpose that keeps itself out of the fray
means.zh: 置身事外的目的

means.en: the purpose as an idea in mind
means.zh: 心中的目的

means.en: the means inserted between purpose and material
means.zh: 插在目的与材料之间的手段

means.en: objects wear each other out: cunning of reason
means.zh: 客体相互磨损：理性的狡计

summary.en: The unity of concept and objectivity: life, cognition of the true and the good, the absolute idea.
summary.zh: 概念与客观性的统一：生命、对真与善的认识、绝对理念。

summary.en: Life is the idea in immediate form: an organism whose members exist only through the whole, and the whole only through them.
summary.zh: 生命是直接形态的理念：有机体的各个肢体只通过整体而存在，整体也只通过它们而存在。

explain.en: The idea is the unity of concept and objectivity, and its first, immediate shape is life. In a living being the concept is the soul and the objective side is the body, and the soul is not one part beside the others but present in every part. Each member is both means and end: the organs sustain the whole, and the whole sustains them. Hegel cites Aristotle: a hand cut off from the body is a hand in name only, because it has stopped being a living member. Life runs through three processes: the living individual forming itself, its exchange with an outer world that it assimilates, and the genus, which goes on through reproduction while individuals die. Life does not yet know itself; the idea comes to know itself in cognition.
explain.zh: 理念是概念与客观性的统一，它最初的直接形态是生命。在生物中，概念是灵魂，客观的一面是身体；灵魂不是与其他部分并列的一个部分，而是遍在于每个部分。每个肢体既是手段又是目的：器官维持整体，整体也维持器官。黑格尔引用亚里士多德：从身体上砍下的手只是名义上的手，因为它已不再是活的肢体。生命经历三个过程：活的个体塑造自身，它与外部世界交换并同化外物，以及类的过程，个体死去而类通过繁殖延续。生命还不认识自己；理念在认识中才认识自身。

example.en: At rest a human heart pumps about 5 litres of blood a minute, and part of that blood feeds the heart muscle itself through the coronary arteries. Each organ works for the others and lives off their work. A kidney removed for transplant must be cooled and placed in a new body within roughly a day, or it stops being a kidney in more than name.
example.zh: 人在静息时心脏每分钟泵出约 5 升血，其中一部分经冠状动脉回头供养心肌本身。每个器官都为别的器官工作，也靠它们的工作活着。为移植摘下的肾脏必须冷藏，并在大约一天内植入新的身体，否则它就只剩下“肾”的名字了。

image.en: In the greenhouse a big red heart pulses on the stage. Around it, facing in, stand a brain and a giant eyeball, members that live only while they are tied to the beat. In front, one grey hand has been cut off and stands apart, cold; a crow pecks at it, for it is a hand in name only. To one side a nest of eggs waits for the next generation.
image.zh: 温室里，一颗巨大的红心在台上搏动。一个大脑和一只巨大的眼球围着它、面朝它站着，它们只有与心跳连在一起才活着。前方一只灰色的手被砍了下来，孤零零地立着，冰冷僵硬；一只乌鸦在啄它，因为它只是名义上的手。一旁的巢里，几只蛋等着下一代。

means.en: the soul, one life present in every member
means.zh: 灵魂：遍在于每个肢体的同一生命

thing.zh: 朝向心脏的大脑和眼球

means.en: members that exist only through the whole
means.zh: 只通过整体而存在的肢体

means.en: a hand cut off is a hand in name only
means.zh: 砍下的手只是名义上的手

means.en: the genus, which goes on as individuals die
means.zh: 类：个体死去，类延续

title.en: Cognition: The True and the Good

summary.en: The idea knows itself in two ways: theoretically, taking the world in as it is (the true), and practically, willing to make it good.
summary.zh: 理念以两种方式认识自身：理论地按世界本来的样子接受它（真），实践地要把它变好（善）。

explain.en: In cognition the idea splits into a subjective side and an objective world that it presupposes. Theoretical cognition, the idea of the true, takes the world in as it is and tries to fill the empty forms of its concepts with that content. Its methods are analytic, breaking a given object into abstract features, and synthetic: definition, division and theorem, as in geometry. Practical activity, the idea of the good, does the reverse: it treats the world as something to change and its own end as what counts. Each is one-sided. The true lacks the will to act, and the good faces a world that never fully obeys. Their unity, the good known as already at work in the world, is the absolute idea.
explain.zh: 在认识中，理念分为主观的一面和它所预设的客观世界。理论认识即“真”的理念，按世界本来的样子接受它，并用这些内容充实概念的空洞形式。它的方法有分析的，把给定对象分解为抽象的特征；也有综合的，即定义、分类和定理，如几何学。实践活动即“善”的理念，方向相反：它把世界当作要改变的东西，把自己的目的当作要紧的东西。两者都片面：真缺少行动的意志，善面对的世界从不完全服从。二者的统一，即认识到善已在世界中起作用，就是绝对理念。

example.en: A botanist studies a fern under a microscope. Breaking it into features (frond, sori, spores) is analytic; building a definition of the genus and deriving consequences from it, as Euclid derives theorems from definitions, is synthetic. A gardener who prunes the same fern so that it thrives acts for the good. Hegel's claim is that complete knowing needs both attitudes at once.
example.zh: 植物学家在显微镜下研究一株蕨。把它分解为叶片、孢子囊群、孢子等特征，是分析方法；给这个属下定义并由此推出结论，就像欧几里得由定义推出定理，是综合方法。修剪同一株蕨让它长得更好的园丁，则是在为善而行动。黑格尔认为，完整的认识同时需要这两种态度。

image.en: Two people share one fern in the greenhouse. On the left a botanist in a beret bends over a giant brass microscope to see the fern exactly as it is. On the right a gardener in a cap swings a hammer to build a fence-trellis, determined to make the fern grow as it ought to. Neither looks at the other.
image.zh: 温室里，两个人共用一株蕨。左边戴贝雷帽的植物学家伏在一台巨大的黄铜显微镜上，想看清这株蕨本来的样子。右边戴帽的园丁挥着锤子搭篱架，一心要让蕨长成它应有的样子。两人谁也不看谁。

means.en: theoretical cognition: the idea of the true
means.zh: 理论认识：真的理念

means.en: practical activity: the idea of the good
means.zh: 实践活动：善的理念

means.en: one world, two one-sided attitudes
means.zh: 同一个世界，两种片面态度

summary.en: The idea that knows itself: its only content is the method of the whole Logic, and it ends by freely releasing itself as nature.
summary.zh: 认识自身的理念：它唯一的内容就是整部逻辑学的方法；最后它自由地把自己释放为自然。

explain.en: The absolute idea unites the theoretical and the practical idea and is the last category of the Logic. It has no new content of its own: its content is the whole system just travelled, and what it adds is knowledge of the form running through it, the method. The method has three moments: an immediate, universal beginning; a progression in which the beginning differentiates and negates itself; and an end, the negation of the negation, which returns to the beginning made concrete. So the Logic is a circle. But pure thought is still abstract, and the idea 'freely releases itself' as nature. This is not a creation in time, and how to read the transition is much debated.
explain.zh: 绝对理念是理论理念与实践理念的统一，也是逻辑学的最后一个范畴。它没有自己的新内容：它的内容就是刚走过的整个体系，它所增加的只是对贯穿其中的形式即方法的认识。方法有三个环节：直接的、普遍的开端；开端自我区分、自我否定的进展；以及终结，即否定之否定，回到已变得具体的开端。所以逻辑学是一个圆圈。但纯粹思维仍是抽象的，理念“自由地释放自己”成为自然。这不是时间中的创造，如何理解这一过渡，学界争论很多。

example.en: Trace the method on the first triad: the beginning is pure being; the progression shows that being is nothing; the end, becoming, holds both and starts the next step. Larger triads such as quality, quantity, measure, or being, essence, concept, have the same shape. The last step loops back: as simple self-relation, the absolute idea is again being, now filled with the whole development.
example.zh: 用第一个三一体来看方法：开端是纯存在；进展表明存在就是无；终结是变易，它包含二者，又开始下一步。更大的三一体，如质、量、度，或存在、本质、概念，形态相同。最后一步回到起点：作为单纯的自身关系，绝对理念又是存在，只是已被整个发展所充实。

image.en: Three curved arrows chase each other round the stage in a ring: beginning, progression, end, and back to the beginning. In the middle a giant open hand rises from the floor and lets go of a white dove, which is already flying off towards a blossoming tree. The circle of thought is closed, and the hand freely gives its bird away to nature.
image.zh: 三支弯曲的箭头在台上首尾相逐、围成一圈：开端、进展、终结，又回到开端。圆心处一只巨大的手从地面伸起，张开手掌放走一只白鸽，白鸽已朝一棵开花的树飞去。思想的圆圈闭合了，那只手自由地把它的鸟交给了自然。

means.en: the method: beginning, progression, end
means.zh: 方法：开端、进展、终结

means.en: the Logic is a circle
means.zh: 逻辑学是一个圆圈

means.en: the idea freely releases itself
means.zh: 理念自由地释放自己

means.en: nature, where the idea goes next
means.zh: 自然：理念的下一站

summary.en: The idea outside itself: from space and time through light and chemistry to plant and animal, climbing back towards spirit.
summary.zh: 外在于自身的理念：从空间、时间经过光与化学过程，到植物与动物，一步步回升到精神。

summary.en: Nature as sheer externality: space, time, matter and gravity, and the solar system.
summary.zh: 纯粹外在性的自然：空间、时间、物质与重力，以及太阳系。

title.zh: 自然：他在形式中的理念

summary.en: Nature is the idea in the form of otherness: its moments lie outside one another, ruled by necessity and contingency rather than freedom.
summary.zh: 自然是以他在形式出现的理念：各环节彼此外在，受必然性与偶然性支配，而非自由。

explain.en: Released by the Logic, the idea exists as nature, 'the idea in the form of otherness'. Its mark is externality: the moments of the concept fall apart, side by side and indifferent to one another. So nature shows necessity and contingency, not freedom. Hegel speaks of the 'impotence of nature': it cannot hold fast to the concept and throws up a wild profusion of forms that philosophy should not try to deduce one by one. Nature is a system of stages, each arising necessarily from the one before in the order of the concept, but not produced from it by a natural process: Hegel rejects the idea that species evolve. The Philosophy of Nature climbs from space to the animal, and so back towards spirit.
explain.zh: 理念从逻辑学中释放出来，作为自然而存在，即“以他在形式出现的理念”。自然的标志是外在性：概念的环节彼此分离、并列、漠不相关。所以自然显示的是必然性和偶然性，而不是自由。黑格尔说“自然的无力”：自然不能牢牢守住概念，冒出纷繁杂乱的形态，哲学不该逐一去推演它们。自然是一个阶段的体系，每个阶段按概念的次序必然地从前一阶段产生，却不是由自然过程从前一阶段生出来的：黑格尔不接受物种进化的观点。自然哲学从空间一路上升到动物，由此回到精神。

example.en: The philosopher W. T. Krug once challenged idealists to deduce his writing pen. Hegel replied that philosophy has more important things to do: whether this pen exists is a matter of contingency, and nature is full of it. Philosophy derives the stages of nature, mechanics, physics and organics, not every pen, pebble or species of beetle.
example.zh: 哲学家克鲁格（W. T. Krug）曾要求唯心论者把他的钢笔“推演”出来。黑格尔回答，哲学有更重要的事要做：这支笔是否存在属于偶然，而自然中充满了偶然。哲学推演的是自然的各个阶段，即力学、物理学、有机物理学，而不是每一支笔、每一块石子、每一种甲虫。

image.en: A great glowing crystal has shattered across the observatory floor, and its shards lie scattered side by side, each still faintly shining. An astronomer kneels with a magnifier, looking for the light of reason in one of them. Three big dice lie tumbled among the pieces. At the back stands a ladder of stages, and a frog sits at its foot without climbing a single rung.
image.zh: 一块发光的巨大水晶在天文台地上摔碎了，碎片散落一地、彼此并列，每一块都还微微发亮。一位天文学家跪着拿放大镜，想在其中一块里找出理性之光。碎片间翻倒着三颗大骰子。后面立着一架阶梯，一只青蛙坐在梯脚，一级也没往上爬。

means.en: the idea outside itself, side by side
means.zh: 外在于自身、彼此并列的理念

means.en: philosophy finding reason in nature
means.zh: 哲学在自然中寻找理性

means.en: contingency, the impotence of nature
means.zh: 偶然性，自然的无力

means.en: a system of stages, not evolution
means.zh: 阶段的体系，而非进化

summary.en: Space is pure side-by-side externality; time is its negativity, 'intuited becoming'; place and motion unite the two.
summary.zh: 空间是纯粹的彼此外在；时间是空间的否定性，即“被直观的变易”；地点与运动统一了二者。

explain.en: Nature's first and most abstract determination is space: pure being-outside-itself, a continuous side by side without any difference. Its dimensions come from negation: the point negates space, the line negates the point, the plane the line, and planes enclose a solid. When this negativity is posited for itself it is time, 'the being which, in being, is not, and in not being, is': intuited becoming, nature's echo of becoming in the Logic. The now exists only as vanishing; Hegel recalls Chronos, who brings forth all things and devours his offspring. Space and time are not empty containers that things fill. Their unity is place, the change of place is motion, and what persists in motion is matter.
explain.zh: 自然最初、最抽象的规定是空间：纯粹的“在自身之外”，没有任何差别的连续并列。空间的维度来自否定：点否定空间，线否定点，面否定线，面又围成立体。这种否定性一旦被自为地设定，就是时间，“存在时不存在、不存在时存在的存在”，即被直观的变易，是逻辑学中变易在自然中的回声。“现在”只作为消逝而存在；黑格尔借用克罗诺斯的神话：他生出万物，又吞食自己的孩子。空间和时间不是等待事物去填满的空容器。二者的统一是地点，地点的变化是运动，运动中持存的东西是物质。

example.en: Mark a point on paper: it has no extent, a negation of space. Drag it and you get a line; drag the line and you get a plane; planes bound a cube. Now watch the second hand of a clock: each 'now' is gone the moment you name it, yet there is always a now. Compare sense-certainty, whose written 'now is night' is stale by noon.
example.zh: 在纸上点一个点：它没有广延，是对空间的否定。拖动它得到线，拖动线得到面，面围成立方体。再看钟的秒针：每个“现在”一说出口就已过去，可“现在”又总在那里。对照感性确定性：写下的“现在是夜晚”，到中午就过时了。

image.en: A giant hourglass stands at the back of the observatory, its sand forever running: time, space's restless negation. In front, flat space is laid out as a rug, with a ruler for a line and a ball for a point. A turtle plods across the rug, trading one place for the next with every step; its plodding is motion, place and time made one.
image.zh: 天文台后方立着一只巨大的沙漏，沙子不停地流：时间，空间那永不安宁的否定。前面铺着一块地毯，代表平面的空间，上面放着一把尺子当线、一个球当点。一只乌龟慢吞吞地爬过地毯，每走一步就用一个地点换下一个地点；它的爬行就是运动，地点与时间合为一体。

means.en: time: the negativity of space, intuited becoming
means.zh: 时间：空间的否定性，被直观的变易

means.en: plane, line and point: space by negation
means.zh: 面、线、点：由否定得出的空间

means.en: motion: place and time united
means.zh: 运动：地点与时间的统一

summary.en: Matter is the unity of space and time. Its essence is gravity, a striving for a centre that the solar system realises as free motion.
summary.zh: 物质是空间与时间的统一，本质是重力，即对中心的追求；太阳系把这种追求实现为自由运动。

explain.en: Matter is what persists of place in motion: the unity of space and time. Its substance is gravity, which Hegel reads as matter's striving for a centre outside it; matter is outside itself and seeks its unity elsewhere. Finite mechanics deals with inert bodies moved from outside: impact, pressure, falling. Absolute mechanics is the solar system, where bodies move freely around a centre and the motion belongs to the system itself. Hegel held that Kepler's laws express this rational structure and that Newton merely recast them in terms of forces. That preference is generally judged mistaken, since Newton's mechanics derives Kepler's laws and goes beyond them. In physics matter gains inner qualities.
explain.zh: 物质是地点在运动中的持存，即空间与时间的统一。它的实体是重力，黑格尔把重力理解为物质对一个在它之外的中心的追求：物质在自身之外，到别处去寻找自己的统一。有限力学讨论被外力推动的惰性物体：碰撞、压力、落体。绝对力学是太阳系：天体围绕中心自由运行，运动属于这个体系本身。黑格尔认为开普勒定律表达了这种理性结构，牛顿只是用“力”重新表述了它们。这种偏好一般被认为是错误的，因为牛顿力学推导出开普勒定律，并且超越了它们。到了物理学，物质获得内在的质。

example.en: Kepler's third law: a planet's period squared is proportional to its mean distance from the sun cubed. Earth: 1 year at 1 AU. Mars orbits at about 1.524 AU, so its period is √(1.524³) ≈ 1.88 years, as observed. Hegel admired such laws as the self-determination of a free system; Newton showed that they follow from universal gravitation, which Hegel undervalued.
example.zh: 开普勒第三定律：行星公转周期的平方与它到太阳平均距离的立方成正比。地球：1 年，1 天文单位。火星约在 1.524 天文单位处，所以周期是 √(1.524³) ≈ 1.88 年，与观测相符。黑格尔推崇这类定律，视之为自由体系的自我规定；牛顿则证明它们可由万有引力推出，这一点被黑格尔低估了。

image.en: A blazing sun hangs over the middle of the observatory, and a ringed planet swings round it on its own. Below, a ring of rocks all lean towards the centre as if they longed to fall into it. At the side an astronomer stands at a brass telescope, following the planet and admiring the law that glows on the backdrop: T² ∝ a³.
image.zh: 天文台中央悬着一轮炽热的太阳，一颗带环的行星自顾自地绕着它转。下方一圈石头都朝中心倾着，好像渴望落进去。一旁的天文学家站在黄铜望远镜边，追踪那颗行星，欣赏背景上发光的定律：T² ∝ a³。

thing.zh: 朝中心倾斜的一圈石头

means.en: gravity: matter striving for a centre
means.zh: 重力：物质追求中心

means.en: the centre outside matter
means.zh: 物质之外的中心

means.en: absolute mechanics: free motion of the system
means.zh: 绝对力学：体系的自由运动

thing.zh: 天文学家与发光的定律

means.en: Kepler's laws, which Hegel favoured
means.zh: 黑格尔推崇的开普勒定律

summary.en: Matter gains a self in light and chemistry, then life in plant and animal, and dies into spirit.
summary.zh: 物质在光与化学过程中获得自我，又在植物与动物中获得生命，最后在死亡中化为精神。

summary.en: Light is matter's first ideal self: weightless, pure self-manifestation that makes everything else visible.
summary.zh: 光是物质最初的观念性自我：没有重量，纯粹地显现自身，并使他物得以显现。

explain.en: Physics begins where matter gains a qualitative self, and its first form is light. Hegel calls light the first ideality of nature: matter that has shed heaviness and exists as pure self-manifestation. Light shows itself and, in doing so, makes other things manifest, much as the I is a pure self-identity to which objects appear. Light is set against darkness, and Hegel, following Goethe, explains colour as an interplay of light and dark in a turbid medium rather than, with Newton, as a mixture of rays that a prism separates. That theory of colour is historically dated and wrong as physics. The core thought, light as matter's self-showing, prepares the step from bodies to selves.
explain.zh: 物理学开始于物质获得质的自我之处，它的第一个形态是光。黑格尔称光为自然最初的观念性：摆脱了重力的物质，作为纯粹的自我显现而存在。光显示自身，同时让别的东西显现出来，就像“我”是纯粹的自身同一，对象向它显现。光与黑暗相对；黑格尔追随歌德，把颜色解释为光与暗在混浊介质中的交互作用，而不是像牛顿那样，看作被棱镜分开的各种光线的混合。这套颜色理论在历史上已经过时，作为物理学是错的。但其核心思想，即光是物质的自我显现，为从物体走向自我做了准备。

example.en: Newton passed sunlight through a prism into a spectrum, then recombined the colours into white light, showing that white light is a mixture. Goethe objected that colours arise where light meets darkness, as at the edges of a bright patch seen through a prism, and Hegel sided with Goethe. Modern optics vindicates Newton: white light spans wavelengths from about 380 to 750 nm.
example.zh: 牛顿让阳光穿过棱镜分成光谱，又把各色光重新合成白光，证明白光是混合的。歌德反驳说，颜色产生于光与暗交界之处，比如透过棱镜看一块亮斑时出现在它边缘的彩色；黑格尔站在歌德一边。现代光学证明牛顿是对的：白光包含约 380 到 750 纳米的各种波长。

image.en: In a dark laboratory a giant light bulb glows on a bench, and a white butterfly circles it. The bulb shines for no one in particular, yet in its light every flask in front stands out. To the right a gentleman in a top hat glares at a glass prism throwing out a rainbow and shrugs it off, as Hegel shrugged off Newton.
image.zh: 昏暗的实验室里，一只巨大的灯泡在工作台上发光，一只白蝴蝶绕着它飞。灯泡并不为谁而亮，可在它的光里，前面每一只烧瓶都清清楚楚。右边一位戴礼帽的绅士瞪着一块射出彩虹的玻璃棱镜，耸耸肩不予理会，就像黑格尔不理会牛顿。

means.en: light: pure self-manifestation
means.zh: 光：纯粹的自我显现

means.en: light makes other things manifest
means.zh: 光使他物显现

means.en: Hegel's dated rejection of Newton's optics
means.zh: 黑格尔对牛顿光学过时的拒斥

summary.en: In the chemical process bodies transform one another, but the process dies out in its product; a process that renewed itself would be life.
summary.zh: 化学过程中物体相互转化，但过程在产物中熄灭；能自我更新的过程就是生命。

explain.en: The chemical process completes inorganic physics. Bodies with particular qualities react: they combine, separate, burn and dissolve, lose their old individuality and produce new bodies. Their qualities prove not to be fixed but to exist in relation to other bodies. Yet the process has a limit: it runs down into a neutral product and comes to rest, and it can start again only if fresh conditions are supplied from outside. Hegel draws the conclusion: if the products of a chemical process could themselves restart it, we would have life. Life is a chemical process that sustains itself, and so the inorganic passes over into the organic. Hegel's chemistry is that of around 1800, but the point about self-renewal does not depend on its details.
explain.zh: 化学过程是无机物理学的完成。具有特殊性质的物体发生反应：化合、分解、燃烧、溶解，失去原有的个体性，产生新的物体。这表明它们的性质不是固定的，而是存在于与其他物体的关系中。但这个过程有限度：它衰减为一个中和的产物、归于静止，只有从外部提供新的条件才能重新开始。黑格尔由此得出结论：如果化学过程的产物能自己重新启动这一过程，那就是生命。生命就是自我维持的化学过程，无机自然由此过渡到有机自然。黑格尔的化学是 1800 年前后的化学，但关于自我更新的论点并不依赖这些细节。

example.en: A candle burns: wax and oxygen become carbon dioxide and water, and when the wax is gone the flame dies. A living cell also burns fuel, C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂ → 6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O, but it uses the energy to rebuild the very enzymes and membranes that keep the reaction going. The candle is a chemical process; the cell is a chemical process that renews itself, which is life.
example.zh: 蜡烛燃烧：蜡和氧变成二氧化碳和水，蜡烧完，火焰就熄灭。活细胞也在“燃烧”燃料，C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6 O₂ → 6 CO₂ + 6 H₂O，但它用释放的能量重建维持这个反应的酶和细胞膜。蜡烛是化学过程，细胞是自我更新的化学过程，也就是生命。

image.en: On the lab floor a huge round flask has finished fizzing and holds only dull grey liquid. A robot assistant points at it beside a battery flashing low: someone from outside must restart the reaction. Next to the dead flask a green sprout has pushed up, and a frog hops beside it, keeping itself going with no help at all.
image.zh: 实验室地上，一只巨大的圆底烧瓶刚冒完泡，里面只剩一摊灰暗的液体。机器人助手指着它，旁边一块电池闪着低电量：得有人从外面重新启动反应。死寂的烧瓶旁冒出一株绿芽，一只青蛙在旁边蹦跳，完全不用帮忙，自己就能一直活下去。

means.en: the process dies out in its neutral product
means.zh: 过程在中和产物中熄灭

means.en: restarting needs conditions from outside
means.zh: 重新开始需要外部条件

means.en: life: a chemical process that renews itself
means.zh: 生命：自我更新的化学过程

summary.en: The first organism: it grows by adding parts that are each almost a whole plant, and it seeks its self outside itself, in the light.
summary.zh: 最初的有机体：它靠添加部分来生长，每一部分几乎都是一整株植物；它在自身之外、在光中寻找自我。

explain.en: The plant is the first true organism, but its subjectivity is incomplete. Its growth is a constant going out of itself: it multiplies by putting forth new parts, and each part, a shoot or a bud, is almost a whole individual, which is why a cutting can grow into a complete plant. The plant has no inner centre above its members, no feeling and no free movement from place to place. It turns outward to the light and finds its self there, outside itself. It takes in water, air and light and gives back flowers and seeds, but it never becomes a self for itself. That step is the animal's.
explain.zh: 植物是第一种真正的有机体，但它的主体性并不完整。它的生长是不断地走出自身：靠长出新的部分来增殖，每一部分，无论枝条还是芽，几乎都是一个完整的个体，所以一根插条就能长成一整株植物。植物在各部分之上没有内在的中心，没有感觉，也不能自由移动位置。它向外朝着光，在自身之外、在光中找到它的自我。它吸收水、空气和阳光，开花结籽，却始终没有成为自为的自我。这一步要由动物迈出。

example.en: Snip a 10 cm shoot from a willow or a pothos, stand it in water, and within a few weeks it grows roots and becomes a new plant. Try the same with a dog's ear and nothing grows. A young sunflower tracks the sun from east to west during the day (heliotropism), its life turned outward to the light.
example.zh: 从柳树或绿萝上剪一段 10 厘米的枝条插在水里，几周内它就会生根，长成一株新植物。对狗耳朵做同样的事，什么也长不出来。幼年的向日葵白天从东到西追着太阳转（向日性），它的生命是向外朝着光的。

image.en: Five sunflowers stand in a row, all craning their heads towards a glowing sun that hangs at the right. A kneeling gardener has just pushed a snipped shoot into a pot, and it has already become a whole new little plant. Nothing in the bed has a centre of its own; every head looks outward, to the light.
image.zh: 五株向日葵排成一行，全都伸长脖子朝向右边悬着的太阳。一位跪着的园丁刚把剪下的枝条插进花盆，它已经长成了一株完整的小植物。花圃里没有谁有自己的中心，每一朵花都向外望着光。

means.en: the plant finds its self outside, in light
means.zh: 植物在外面、在光中找到自我

means.en: each part is almost a whole individual
means.zh: 每一部分几乎都是完整个体

means.en: growth by adding parts, no inner centre
means.zh: 靠添加部分生长，没有内在中心

summary.en: The animal is a genuine subject: it moves itself, feels, has a voice and inner warmth, and its self is present in every part.
summary.zh: 动物是真正的主体：自己运动、有感觉、能发声、有体温，它的自我遍在于全身每一处。

explain.en: In the animal the organism gains a true self. It moves freely from place to place, has a voice in which its inwardness sounds out, keeps its own warmth and, above all, feels: a stimulus is not just an outside effect but something felt by a self that is present throughout the body. Its parts are moments of one whole and cannot, like a plant's, grow into new individuals. Hegel orders animal life by three functions: sensibility (nerves), irritability (muscles and blood) and reproduction (digestion and breeding). The animal keeps itself going by assimilating its surroundings, and continues its kind through the genus process of mating, offspring and death.
explain.zh: 到了动物，有机体获得了真正的自我。它能自由移动位置，有声音来表达内在，自己保持体温，最重要的是有感觉：刺激不只是外来的作用，而是被一个遍在全身的自我感受到。它的各部分是一个整体的环节，不能像植物的部分那样长成新的个体。黑格尔用三种机能来安排动物生命：感受性（神经）、应激性（肌肉与血液）和再生性（消化与繁殖）。动物通过同化周围环境来维持自己，并通过交配、生育、死亡的类过程延续种族。

example.en: Touch a sleeping dog's tail and the whole dog wakes: the head turns, the ears go up, it may growl. The feeling is not in the tail alone; one self is present in every part. Mammals also keep a steady inner warmth, about 38–39 °C in dogs, whatever the air around them. A plant has neither feeling nor warmth of its own.
example.zh: 碰一下熟睡的狗的尾巴，整条狗都醒了：头转过来，耳朵竖起，也许还低吼一声。感觉不只在尾巴上，同一个自我遍在于每一部分。哺乳动物还能保持稳定的体温，狗约为 38–39 °C，不管周围空气冷热。植物既没有感觉，也没有自己的体温。

image.en: A big spotted dog stands at the centre, barking 'Woof!' Behind it a giant hand rises from the floor and pinches the tip of its tail, and the whole dog swings round at once, ears up. A thermometer beside it reads hot: it keeps its own warmth. A puppy sits at its feet, the genus going on.
image.zh: 一条花斑大狗站在中央，汪汪大叫。它身后一只巨手从地面伸起，捏住它的尾巴尖，整条狗立刻扭过身来，耳朵竖起。旁边的温度计显示“热”：它自己保持体温。一只小狗坐在它脚边，类在延续。

means.en: one self present in every part: feeling
means.zh: 自我遍在全身：感觉

means.en: a stimulus felt, not just suffered
means.zh: 刺激被感受到，而不只是被承受

means.en: voice and inner warmth
means.zh: 声音与体温

means.en: the genus process: offspring
means.zh: 类过程：后代

title.en: Death and the Birth of Spirit

summary.en: The individual animal can never match its genus and dies; in the death of natural individuality the universal rises to exist for itself as spirit.
summary.zh: 动物个体永远无法与它的类相符，因而死去；在自然个体性的死亡中，普遍者上升为自为存在的精神。

explain.en: The animal is a self, but only as this single creature, while its true universal is the genus. The individual can never be adequate to the genus; this inadequacy is, Hegel says, its 'original disease' and the inborn germ of death. The genus maintains itself only through a series of individuals, each born and dying: in nature the universal exists only as this endless replacement, a spurious infinite of generations. With death nature reaches its last step. The universal must come to exist for itself, as a self that knows itself to be universal. 'Above this death of nature', Hegel writes, 'a more beautiful nature' emerges: spirit. The Philosophy of Nature hands over to the Philosophy of Spirit, and the idea returns to itself from its otherness.
explain.zh: 动物是一个自我，却只是这一个个体，而它真正的普遍是类。个体永远无法与类相符；黑格尔说，这种不相符是它“原始的病”，是与生俱来的死亡萌芽。类只通过一系列生生死死的个体来维持自己：在自然中，普遍只作为这种无尽的更替而存在，是世代的坏无限。死亡是自然的最后一步。普遍必须成为自为的存在，成为知道自己是普遍的自我。黑格尔写道，在自然的这一死亡之上，出现了“一个更美的自然”：精神。自然哲学交棒给精神哲学，理念从它的他在中回到自身。

example.en: An adult mayfly may live only a day; an elephant may live 60 or 70 years. Either way the individual dies while the species goes on, as parents pass their traits to offspring. In nature the universal, the species, exists only as this chain of individuals. In a human being, Hegel says, the universal knows itself: a person can think 'human being' and recognise it in herself, which no animal can.
example.zh: 成年蜉蝣也许只活一天，大象可以活六七十年。无论哪种，个体都会死，而物种借父母把性状传给后代而延续。在自然中，普遍即物种，只作为这条个体之链而存在。黑格尔说，在人身上普遍认识了自己：人能思考“人”这个概念，并在自己身上认出它，这是任何动物都做不到的。

image.en: An old bleached skull lies on a rock. Out of it a glowing spirit slowly rises, looking about as if it saw itself for the first time. On one side a nest holds an egg that is just hatching; on the other three sheep plod past, the flock unbothered. The species goes on as always, but something new has woken.
image.zh: 一颗发白的旧骷髅躺在石头上。一团发光的精灵正从里面缓缓升起，四下张望，好像第一次看见了自己。一边的巢里，一只蛋正在破壳；另一边三只绵羊慢吞吞走过，羊群毫不在意。物种照旧延续，但某种新的东西已经醒来。

means.en: the death of the natural individual
means.zh: 自然个体的死亡

means.en: the genus goes on through replaced individuals
means.zh: 类靠个体更替而延续

means.en: the universal existing for itself: spirit
means.zh: 自为存在的普遍：精神

summary.en: Spirit leaves nature behind: first as an individual mind (soul, intelligence, will), then as freedom built into a world of right, morality, ethical life and history.
summary.zh: 精神摆脱自然：先是个体心灵（灵魂、理智、意志），再把自由建成一个世界：法、道德、伦理与世界历史。

summary.en: The individual mind climbs from the feeling soul and habit through intelligence and memory to a will that wills its own freedom.
summary.zh: 个体心灵从感受的灵魂与习惯出发，经过理智与记忆，上升为意欲自身自由的意志。

summary.en: Spirit begins as a soul sunk in nature; habit, a 'second nature', makes the body run by itself and so sets the mind free.
summary.zh: 精神起初是沉浸于自然的灵魂；习惯作为“第二天性”让身体自行运转，从而解放心灵。

explain.en: Subjective spirit opens with Anthropology. The soul is spirit still immersed in nature: temperament, the ages of life, sleep and waking, sensation and feeling. Hegel calls it the 'sleep of spirit'. The soul becomes master of its body through habit. Repetition turns a skill into a second nature: nature, because it now runs immediately; second, because the soul itself has made it so. This looks like mechanism, yet it frees: the soul no longer attends to each step and can turn to other things. Hegel even counts upright posture as a habit kept up by the will. Habit, he says, is the mechanism of self-feeling, as memory is the mechanism of intelligence. The cost is that the merely habitual can harden into lifeless routine.
explain.zh: 主观精神从人类学开始。灵魂是仍沉浸在自然中的精神，受气质、年龄阶段、睡眠与清醒、感觉与感受支配，黑格尔称之为“精神的睡眠”。灵魂靠习惯成为身体的主人。反复练习把能力变成第二天性：说它是天性，因为它直接运转；说它是第二的，因为它是灵魂自己造成的。这看似机械化，实为解放：灵魂不必照看每一步，便能转向别的事。黑格尔甚至把直立也看作由意志维持的习惯。他说，习惯是自我感受的机制，正如记忆是理智的机制。代价是：纯粹的习惯也会僵化成无生气的例行公事。

example.en: A child learning to write watches every stroke of every letter. An adult writes a postcard while thinking only about what to say. The skill has not vanished; it has sunk into the hand, and that is exactly what frees attention for meaning. Touch-typing, driving and sight-reading music work the same way: what once took full concentration now runs on its own.
example.zh: 刚学写字的孩子盯着每个字母的每一笔；成年人写明信片时只想着要说什么。技能没有消失，而是沉入了手中，正因如此注意力才腾出来照顾意义。盲打、开车、视奏也是一样：当初要全神贯注的事，如今自己就会完成。

image.en: An arched stone bridge spans the classroom stage. A grown-up strolls over its hump with her nose in a book, her feet finding every step on their own; a thought bubble above her reads 'Logic'. At the foot of the bridge a toddler crawls on hands and knees, staring hard at the first step.
image.zh: 教室舞台上架着一座石拱桥。一位成年人捧着书走过桥顶，眼睛不离书页，双脚却自己踩准每一步；她头顶的思想泡泡写着“逻辑”。桥脚下，一个幼儿手脚并用地爬，死死盯着第一级台阶。

means.en: habit: the body walks by itself, so the mind is free
means.zh: 习惯：身体自己走，心灵得自由

means.en: the soul still absorbed in every bodily act
means.zh: 仍被每个身体动作占据的灵魂

means.en: attention freed for higher activity, up to thinking
means.zh: 被解放、转向更高活动乃至思维的注意力

means.en: the body, mastered and made the soul's instrument
means.zh: 被掌握、成为灵魂工具的身体

summary.en: Intelligence makes the given its own: images sink into a 'nocturnal pit', imagination makes signs, and memory keeps names, the medium of thought.
summary.zh: 理智把外来材料变成自己的：图像沉入“黑夜般的深井”，想象制作符号，记忆保存名称，而思维就在名称中进行。

explain.en: In Psychology, theoretical spirit, or intelligence, moves from intuition through representation to thinking. Recollection takes an intuited image inward and keeps it, unconsciously, in what Hegel calls a 'nocturnal pit' of countless images. Imagination calls images back, links them and finally makes signs. A sign, unlike a symbol, has nothing in common with what it means: Hegel calls it a pyramid into which a foreign soul has been placed. Memory then holds names. 'It is in names that we think': to think 'lion' I need no picture of one. Even mechanical memory, rote learning of words without images, matters: in it intelligence becomes a pure space for names, which prepares the passage to thinking.
explain.zh: 在心理学中，理论精神即理智，从直观经过表象走向思维。回忆把直观到的图像收进内心，无意识地保存在黑格尔所说的“黑夜般的深井”里。想象把图像唤回、加以联结，最后制作符号。符号与象征不同，它与所指的意义毫无相似之处，黑格尔把它比作一座金字塔，里面安放着外来的灵魂。记忆随后保存名称。“我们是在名称中思维的”：想到“狮子”，不必在脑中画一头狮子。连不带图像的死记硬背也很重要：理智在其中成为纯粹的名称空间，为过渡到思维做好准备。

example.en: The word 'lion' looks nothing like a lion: it is a sign. A lion painted on a coat of arms is a symbol, chosen for a likeness (courage). Reading 'the lion sleeps', you understand at once without picturing anything. Hegel even mocked the revived image-mnemonics of the ancients, the very method of loci this palace uses, for turning names back into images and so dragging memory down to imagination.
example.zh: “狮子”这个词与狮子毫无相像，这是符号；纹章上画的狮子是象征，因相似（勇猛）而被选中。读到“狮子在睡觉”，你立刻就懂，不必在脑中画出任何东西。黑格尔甚至嘲讽过当时复兴的古代记忆术，也就是本宫殿所用的位置记忆法：它把名称又变回图像，等于把记忆降回想象。

image.en: A stone well stands in the middle of the classroom, black as night inside. On the left a girl in a graduation cap shoves a small painting of a tree towards its rim, to be stored down in the dark. On the right a boy has fished it back up as a single chalked word on the blackboard, 'tree', and points at it: no picture needed.
image.zh: 教室中央立着一口石井，井里黑得像夜。左边，一个戴学士帽的女孩把一幅画着树的小画推向井口，要把它存进黑暗里。右边，一个男孩把它“捞”了回来，只剩黑板上粉笔写的一个字：“树”。他指着这个字：不需要图画了。

means.en: the 'nocturnal pit' that keeps images unconsciously
means.zh: 无意识地保存图像的“黑夜般的深井”

means.en: an intuited image, taken inward by recollection
means.zh: 直观得来、由回忆收入内心的图像

means.en: a sign and a name, kept by memory
means.zh: 由记忆保存的符号与名称

thing.en: the boy pointing at the word

means.en: we think in names, not in pictures
means.zh: 我们在名称中思维，而非在图像中

summary.en: Choosing among given impulses is only formal freedom; the truly free will wills freedom itself and so must build it into a world.
summary.zh: 在既定冲动之间挑选只是形式的自由；真正自由的意志以自由本身为内容，因而必须把自由建成一个世界。

explain.en: Practical spirit starts with feelings and impulses. Next comes arbitrary choice (Willkür): I can pick among my impulses. Most people call this freedom; Hegel calls it formal, because the options and my urges are simply given. Chasing happiness, a sum of satisfied impulses, does not escape this. The will is truly free when its content is freedom itself: 'the free will which wills the free will'. Nor is freedom pure negation: a will that tolerates nothing determinate is the 'freedom of the void', which ends in destruction, as in the Terror. Concrete freedom is being with oneself in an other, as in friendship and love. Such a will cannot stay inward; it must give itself existence in right, morality and institutions. Objective spirit begins here.
explain.zh: 实践精神从感受和冲动开始，随后出现任意（Willkür）：我可以在各种冲动之间挑选。多数人称之为自由，黑格尔却说它只是形式的，因为选项和欲求都是现成给定的。追求幸福即满足冲动的总和，也跳不出这一点。意志以自由本身为内容时才真正自由，即“意欲自由意志的自由意志”。自由也不是纯粹的否定：容不下任何确定事物的意志是“空虚的自由”，终将走向破坏，如恐怖统治。具体的自由是在他者中即在自身（bei sich selbst），如友谊和爱。这样的意志不能只留在内心，必须在法、道德和制度中给自己定在。客观精神由此开始。

example.en: At a vending machine you may press A3 or B7: that is Willkür, and both the snacks and your cravings were stocked by someone else. Two friends who agree to meet every Sunday each accept a limit, yet each finds himself in the arrangement: being with oneself in an other. To will a law that lets every person own property and make contracts is to will freedom itself.
example.zh: 在自动售货机前，你可以按 A3 也可以按 B7：这是任意，而零食和馋虫都是别人备好的。两个约好每周日见面的朋友各自接受了限制，却都在这个约定中找到自己：在他者中即在自身。去意欲一部让每个人都能拥有财产、订立契约的法律，才是意欲自由本身。

image.en: A giant red vending machine glows on the left, and a child jabs its buttons over and over, wanting everything at once. On the right a woman has turned her back on the machine. She holds up a big brass key and walks towards an open door, beyond which the world of right begins.
image.zh: 左边一台巨大的红色自动售货机闪着光，一个孩子一遍遍猛按按钮，什么都想要。右边，一位女子背对机器，举起一把大铜钥匙，走向一扇敞开的门：门外，法的世界开始了。

means.en: arbitrary choice: options and urges are given
means.zh: 任意：选项和欲求都是给定的

means.en: impulse chasing every satisfaction
means.zh: 追逐一切满足的冲动

means.en: the will that wills freedom itself
means.zh: 以自由本身为内容的意志

means.en: freedom must exist outwardly: on to objective spirit
means.zh: 自由须有外在定在：走向客观精神

summary.en: Freedom exists first outwardly, as persons who own property, then inwardly, as a subject answerable for purpose and conscience.
summary.zh: 自由先外在地存在为拥有财产的人格，再内在地存在为对故意与良心负责的主体。

summary.en: 'Be a person and respect others as persons': freedom first exists in property, and two owners' wills meet in contract.
summary.zh: “成为一个人，并尊重他人为人”：自由最初的定在是所有权，两个所有者的意志在契约中相遇。

explain.en: The Philosophy of Right starts from right as the existence of free will. In abstract right the will is a bare person, a capacity for rights that every human has equally. Its command: 'be a person and respect others as persons.' A person must give its freedom an external sphere, and that is property. I put my will into a thing by seizing, forming or marking it; seen from freedom, property is not just a means to needs but freedom's first existence. In contract two owners recognise each other and form a common will. Some goods cannot be alienated: my personality, freedom of will, ethical life and religion. Marriage and the state are not contracts. And since the common will is only a chance agreement of two wills, wrong becomes possible.
explain.zh: 《法哲学原理》从“法是自由意志的定在”出发。抽象法中的意志只是赤裸的人格（Person），即人人平等具有的权利能力。它的命令是：“成为一个人，并尊重他人为人。”人格必须给自己的自由一个外在领域，这就是所有权。我通过占取、加工或标记把意志放进物中；从自由来看，财产不只是满足需要的手段，而是自由最初的定在。在契约中，两个所有者相互承认，形成共同意志。有些东西不可转让：人格、意志自由、伦理和宗教。婚姻和国家也不是契约。共同意志只是两个任意意志偶然的一致，所以不法成为可能。

example.en: Hegel's own case (§67): I may sell my labour for a limited time, say eight hours a day, because that is a particular use of my powers. Selling the whole of my working time for life would sell my personality itself and make me a slave, so such a contract is void. A farmer who fences and ploughs a field has put his will into it: the fence is a mark, the furrows are form.
example.zh: 黑格尔自己的例子（§67）：我可以出卖有限时间的劳动，比如每天八小时，因为那只是我能力的一种特殊使用；若把一生的全部劳动时间都卖掉，就等于卖掉人格本身、使自己成为奴隶，这样的契约无效。农民给一块地围上篱笆、犁出垄沟，就把意志放进了地里：篱笆是标记，垄沟是加工。

image.en: A big wooden crate stands on the library floor. A woman leans on a giant rubber stamp and presses a red seal onto its lid: mine. Facing her, a man holds out a gold coin, ready to trade. At their feet lies a heavy chain whose padlock has sprung open: whatever they swap, neither can sell himself.
image.zh: 图书馆地板上立着一只大木箱。一位女子压着一枚巨大的橡皮图章，在箱盖上盖下红印：归我。对面一个男人递出一枚金币，准备交换。他们脚边躺着一条粗铁链，挂锁已经弹开：无论交换什么，谁也不能把自己卖掉。

thing.en: the red stamp on the crate

means.en: putting my will into a thing: property
means.zh: 把意志放进物中：所有权

means.en: contract: two owners form a common will
means.zh: 契约：两个所有者形成共同意志

means.en: persons recognising each other as equals
means.zh: 彼此承认为平等的人格

thing.en: the sprung padlock on the chain

means.en: personality and freedom cannot be sold
means.zh: 人格与自由不可转让

summary.en: Crime negates right; punishment negates that negation and restores right, honouring the criminal as a rational being.
summary.zh: 犯罪否定了法；刑罚否定这一否定而恢复法，并把罪犯当作理性的存在者来尊重。

explain.en: Wrong comes in three grades: unintentional wrong (an honest dispute over ownership), fraud (right's form kept, its substance violated) and crime, which negates right as such. Crime is a nullity claiming validity; punishment cancels it, the negation of the negation, restoring right. Hegel rejects deterrence as its ground: that is like raising a stick at a dog, treating a person as an animal. Punishment is the criminal's own right, implied in his act, so punishing him honours him as rational. Its measure is equality of value, not literal sameness: 'an eye for an eye' is absurd for a one-eyed offender. In abstract right punishment still looks like revenge, which breeds endless counter-revenge; a will that wills the universal is needed: morality.
explain.zh: 不法分三级：无犯意的不法（如对产权归属的善意争执）、诈欺（保留法的形式，侵犯其实质）和犯罪，后者否定法本身。犯罪是一种自命有效的虚无，刑罚把它取消，即否定之否定，从而恢复法。黑格尔反对以威慑作为刑罚的根据：那就像对狗举起棍子，把人当动物而非自由者。刑罚是罪犯自己的法，已包含在他的行为里，所以惩罚他恰恰是尊重他为理性的人。刑罚的尺度是价值上的等同，而非字面上的相同：对独眼罪犯讲“以眼还眼”就很荒唐。但在抽象法中，刑罚仍带着报复的形式，报复又引出无尽的反报复，于是需要一个意欲普遍的意志：道德。

example.en: A thief takes a bicycle worth €300. On Hegel's analysis the act asserts 'your right does not count'. A fine or sentence of equivalent weight answers 'it does count', and right is restored; nobody steals the thief's bicycle back. Fraud is different: selling a gilded brass ring as gold keeps the outward form of a fair sale, since both parties agreed, while violating its substance.
example.zh: 小偷偷走一辆价值 300 欧元的自行车。按黑格尔的分析，这一行为在宣称“你的权利不算数”。一笔价值相当的罚金或刑期回答说“它算数”，法由此恢复；没有人会去把小偷的自行车偷回来。诈欺则不同：把镀金黄铜戒指当金戒指卖，保留了公平买卖的外在形式（双方都同意了），却侵犯了它的实质。

image.en: A giant seesaw stands in the library. A hooded thief jumped onto one end and slammed it down; now the judge, gavel in hand, has stepped onto the other end with exactly the same weight, and the board is level again. Perched on his end, the thief nods, as if he had asked for it. Nearby a puzzled dog pricks up its ears: this time nobody is waving a stick at him.
image.zh: 图书馆里立着一架巨大的跷跷板。戴兜帽的小偷跳上一端，把它猛地压了下去；此刻手持木槌的法官带着与他恰好相等的分量站上另一端，木板重新恢复水平。小偷坐在自己那一端点了点头，仿佛这正是他自己要求的。旁边一只狗困惑地竖起耳朵：这一回，没有人对它挥棍子。

means.en: right restored
means.zh: 被恢复的法

thing.en: the hooded thief on one end

means.en: crime, a negation of right; his act sets the measure
means.zh: 犯罪是对法的否定，他的行为给出尺度

means.en: punishment: negation of the negation, equal in value
means.zh: 刑罚：否定之否定，价值相等

means.en: deterrence treats people like dogs; Hegel rejects it
means.zh: 威慑论把人当狗，黑格尔予以拒绝

summary.en: The subjective will answers only for what it knew and intended; it seeks the good through conscience, which can slide into empty formalism or evil.
summary.zh: 主观意志只对自己所知所愿负责；它凭良心追求善，而良心可能滑向空洞的形式主义乃至恶。

explain.en: Morality (Moralität) is the right of the subjective will. First, purpose and responsibility: of a deed's many consequences, I own as my action only what I knew and purposed. Second, intention and welfare: an action has a universal side (an arsonist cannot plead he lit only one square inch of wood), and I may seek my own satisfaction in it. Third, the good and conscience. Hegel praises Kant for grounding duty in free will but calls 'duty for duty's sake' empty formalism: Kant's test finds a contradiction only if content, such as property, is presupposed. Conscience is the subject's certainty of the good; held merely formally, it can set its own particularity above the universal: evil. Good and conscience stay abstract; their unity is ethical life.
explain.zh: 道德（Moralität）是主观意志的法。其一，故意与责任：在行为的诸多后果中，我只把自己所知、所故意的部分认作我的行动。其二，意图与福利：行动有普遍的一面（纵火者不能辩称自己只点着了一小块木头），我也有权在行动中寻求自己的满足。其三，善与良心。黑格尔赞赏康德把义务建立在自由意志上，却批评“为义务而义务”是空洞的形式主义：普遍化检验只有预设了财产之类的内容，才找得出矛盾。良心是主体对善的确信；若只停留于形式，它就可能把自己的特殊性置于普遍之上，这就是恶。善与良心都还抽象，它们的统一是伦理。

example.en: Oedipus kills an old man at a crossroads, not knowing he is his father. Hegel says he cannot be charged with parricide: the deed includes the father, but his action, what he knew and intended, does not. Greek tragedy, by contrast, made the hero answer for the whole deed. And Kant's maxim 'keep a deposit when no one can prove it' contradicts itself only if we already assume that property ought to exist.
example.zh: 俄狄浦斯在十字路口杀了一个老人，不知道那是他父亲。黑格尔说，不能控告他弑父：“行为”里包括了父亲，他的“行动”即他所知所愿却不包括。希腊悲剧则相反，让英雄为全部行为负责。再看康德的准则“没人能证明时就吞掉寄存物”：只有在已经假定财产应当存在时，它才自相矛盾。

image.en: A signpost stands at a crossroads by a heap of stones, its arms pointing to Thebes and Delphi. A crowned old man lies in the dust beside it. A young traveller strides off the other way, sword at his side, untroubled; his thought bubble says only 'a stranger'. The moral question hangs in that bubble: what did he know?
image.zh: 十字路口的石堆旁立着一块路牌，一边指向忒拜，一边指向德尔斐。一位戴王冠的老人倒在路边尘土里。一个年轻旅人佩着剑，若无其事地朝另一个方向走去；他的思想泡泡里只写着“陌生人”。道德的问题就悬在这个泡泡里：他当时知道什么？

means.en: the right of knowledge: I answer for what I knew
means.zh: 认知的法：我只对所知负责

means.en: the deed's full consequence: a father unknown to him
means.zh: 行为的全部后果：他不认识的父亲

means.en: action (Handlung): only what was known and willed
means.zh: 行动（Handlung）：只含所知所愿

means.en: the subject's own choice and responsibility
means.zh: 主体自己的选择与责任

summary.en: Right and morality united in living institutions: the family's love, civil society's market and the state.
summary.zh: 法与道德在活的制度中统一：家庭的爱、市民社会的市场，以及国家。

summary.en: Freedom as the living good: customs and institutions in which right and morality are united and individuals feel at home.
summary.zh: 自由作为活的善：法与道德在风俗和制度中统一，个人在其中感到自在。

explain.en: Abstract right gave freedom outward existence without inwardness; morality gave inwardness without content. Ethical life is their unity and truth, 'the Idea of freedom as the living good'. The good is no longer a mere ought: it exists in customs, laws and institutions, and individuals recognise these as their own essence, not as alien commands. Once habitual, the ethical becomes a second nature. Its duties restrict only drives and empty reflection; in duty, Hegel says, the individual finds his liberation. Asked how best to raise a son ethically, a Pythagorean replied: make him a citizen of a state with good laws. Ethical life unfolds as family, civil society and state. The Phenomenology's Greek ethical world was its immediate, unreflective form.
explain.zh: 抽象法给了自由外在的定在却缺少内在性，道德有了内在性却缺少内容。伦理是二者的统一与真理，即“作为活的善的自由理念”。善不再只是应当，而是存在于风俗、法律和制度之中；个人把它们认作自己的本质，而非外来的命令。习以为常之后，伦理成为第二天性。伦理义务限制的只是冲动和空洞的反思；黑格尔说，个人在义务中反而获得解放。有人问怎样最好地教育儿子，一位毕达哥拉斯派回答：让他成为法律良好的国家的公民。伦理展开为家庭、市民社会和国家。《精神现象学》中的希腊伦理世界是它直接的、尚未经过反思的形态。

example.en: You do not derive from first principles that you should stop at a red light, visit your sick grandmother or pay your taxes. You grow up inside practices that already embody these goods, and on reflection you can endorse them as your own. When the practices are rational, keeping them feels like freedom rather than obedience. The lonely moralist who asks 'what ought I to do?' from scratch is the exception, not the rule.
example.zh: 你不会从第一原理推出该在红灯前停车、该去探望生病的祖母、该纳税。你在早已体现这些善的习俗中长大，反思之后又能把它们认作自己的。如果这些习俗是合理的，遵守它们就像自由，而不像服从。从零开始追问“我应当做什么”的孤独道德家，是例外而非常态。

image.en: Under the throne room's banners six citizens dance a ring around a tall flagpole, arms raised, never glancing at their feet or at a rulebook: the steps are second nature. From the side a father leads his small son by the hand towards the ring, following the Pythagorean's advice: make him a citizen of a state with good laws.
image.zh: 王座厅的旗帜下，六位市民绕着一根高高的旗杆跳圆圈舞，双臂高举，从不低头看脚，也不翻规则手册：舞步已是第二天性。一旁，一位父亲牵着小儿子走向舞圈，照毕达哥拉斯派的建议：让他成为法律良好的国家的公民。

means.en: custom: freedom lived together as second nature
means.zh: 风俗：共同生活中的自由，已成第二天性

means.en: shared institutions the life turns around
means.zh: 生活所环绕的共同制度

means.en: duties felt as one's own, not as alien commands
means.zh: 义务被视为自己的，而非外来命令

means.en: upbringing as citizenship in a state with good laws
means.zh: 教育即成为良法之邦的公民

summary.en: Ethical life in its immediate form, bound by love; it raises children into independent persons and so dissolves itself.
summary.zh: 伦理的直接形态，以爱为纽带；它把子女培养成独立的人格，从而使自己解体。

explain.en: The family is ethical life as feeling: love, the awareness of my unity with another, so that I am not isolated. Marriage is not a contract. In it two persons freely consent to make themselves one person, an ethical bond based on love and trust, not mere sexual inclination. The family holds property in common, a lasting resource for all its members. Its third moment is raising children, and the aim of upbringing is to make them free, independent persons. So the family prepares its own dissolution: grown children leave and found new families, which meet as independent units in civil society. Hegel's account of the roles of men and women reflects his time and is widely criticised.
explain.zh: 家庭是以感受为形式的伦理：爱，就是意识到我与另一个人的统一，使我不再孤立。婚姻不是契约，而是两个人格自愿同意结合为一个人格，是以爱和信任为基础的伦理纽带，而不只是性的吸引。家庭拥有共同财产，是为全体成员保存的持久资源。第三个环节是教育子女，教育的目的正是让他们成为自由独立的人格。所以家庭在为自己的解体做准备：成年子女离家，建立新的家庭，这些家庭作为独立单位在市民社会中相遇。黑格尔对男女角色的论述带有时代局限，受到广泛批评。

example.en: A couple marry and pool their savings in a joint account: no longer 'mine' and 'yours' but the family's, managed for all. Twenty years later their daughter, raised to think for herself, takes a job in another city, signs her own lease and starts a family. The parents' success shows in her independence, which is also the end of the old household as a unit.
example.zh: 一对夫妻结婚后把积蓄并入共同账户：不再分“我的”“你的”，而是全家的，为所有人打理。二十年后，被培养得有主见的女儿去外地工作、自己签租约、组建家庭。父母成功与否，正体现在她的独立上，而这也意味着原来那个家作为一个单位结束了。

image.en: On top of an open treasure chest sits a big twig nest. Two green lovebirds nestle side by side as if they were one bird, guarding two hatching eggs. A grown fledgling has already hopped down and is bouncing across the floor towards a little house of its own.
image.zh: 一只敞开的宝箱上架着一个大鸟巢。两只绿色的爱情鸟紧紧依偎，像是合成了一只鸟，守着两枚正在破壳的蛋。一只长大的雏鸟已经跳了下来，蹦蹦跳跳地奔向一座属于自己的小房子。

means.en: marriage: two persons consent to become one
means.zh: 婚姻：两个人格自愿合为一体

thing.en: the open chest under the nest

means.en: family property held in common
means.zh: 共同的家庭财产

means.en: children, to be raised into persons
means.zh: 要被培养成人格的子女

thing.en: the fledgling heading for its own house

means.en: the family dissolves into new families
means.zh: 家庭解体为新的家庭

summary.en: Each pursues his own ends yet depends on all: a system of needs with courts, police and corporations, which breeds wealth and poverty together.
summary.zh: 人人追求私利，却又依赖所有人：需要的体系加上司法、警察和同业公会，财富与贫困在其中一同滋长。

explain.en: Hegel was among the first to separate civil society from the state. In it each person is his own end and others are means, yet to meet my needs I must work for others' needs: a system of needs and division of labour, drawn from Smith, Say and Ricardo. Civil society also contains the administration of justice, the 'police' (public authority: market oversight, welfare) and corporations, trade bodies that give members recognition and security. Hegel calls it the battlefield where everyone's private interest meets everyone else's. Left to itself it piles up wealth while producing a rabble: despite an excess of wealth, it is not rich enough to check poverty. It reaches out for markets and colonies, and needs the state above it.
explain.zh: 黑格尔是最早把市民社会与国家区分开的思想家之一。在其中，每个人都以自己为目的，他人只是手段；可要满足自己的需要，我又必须为他人的需要劳动，于是形成需要的体系与分工，这里吸收了斯密、萨伊和李嘉图的学说。市民社会还包括司法、“警察”（公共权力：市场监管与福利）和同业公会，后者给成员以承认和保障。黑格尔称它为人人私利相互冲突的战场。放任自流时，它一边积累财富，一边制造贱民：尽管财富过剩，它却不够富足，无法消除贫困。它向外寻找市场和殖民地，并需要高于它的国家。

example.en: A baker in Berlin sells bread to a tailor, who sews coats for a printer, who prints the baker's price lists. None of them aims at the others' welfare, yet each can live only through the rest. In Hegel's day such booms coexisted with workers sinking below subsistence, losing not only income but the sense of right and honour that comes from supporting oneself by one's own work.
example.zh: 柏林的面包师把面包卖给裁缝，裁缝给印刷商做大衣，印刷商又替面包师印价目表。谁都不以他人的福祉为目的，却谁都只能靠别人活下去。在黑格尔的时代，这样的繁荣与工人跌到温饱线以下同时存在：他们失去的不只是收入，还有靠自己劳动养活自己而来的正义感与尊严。

image.en: A market stall with a striped awning has been set up in the throne room. A merchant and a customer haggle in front of it, each eyeing only his own gain, while gold coins pile up on a crate beside them. On the cold floor a ragged beggar sits holding out an empty cup, and a guild banner stands at the corner.
image.zh: 王座厅里搭起一个条纹遮篷的集市摊位。商人和顾客在摊前讨价还价，各自只盯着自己的好处，旁边的木箱上金币越堆越高。冰冷的地上坐着一个衣衫褴褛的乞丐，伸出一只空杯子；角落里立着一面同业公会的旗帜。

means.en: each his own end, others mere means
means.zh: 人人以己为目的，他人只是手段

means.en: the system of needs and division of labour
means.zh: 需要的体系与分工

thing.zh: 木箱上越堆越高的金币

means.en: wealth accumulating
means.zh: 不断积累的财富

means.en: poverty and the rabble amid excess wealth
means.zh: 财富过剩中的贫困与贱民

means.en: corporations: recognition and security
means.zh: 同业公会：承认与保障

summary.en: 'The actuality of the ethical Idea': the rational state reconciles each person's particular freedom with the universal good.
summary.zh: “伦理理念的现实”：合理的国家让每个人的特殊自由与普遍利益相互和解。

explain.en: The state is 'the actuality of the ethical Idea' and of concrete freedom: particular interests develop fully in civil society, yet citizens knowingly will the universal as their own end. Social-contract theory, Hegel says, confuses the state with civil society, as if it existed only to protect property. His rational state is a constitutional monarchy whose powers (crown, executive, legislature with estates) interlock like an organism. The monarch's role is small: in a well-ordered state he only says 'yes' and dots the i. The line often rendered 'the march of God in the world', from students' notes, says the state's existence is God's way in the world: reason made real, not worship of power. No judge stands above states; hence world history.
explain.zh: 国家是“伦理理念的现实”，也是具体自由的现实：特殊利益在市民社会中充分发展，公民又自觉地把普遍利益当作自己的目的。黑格尔反对社会契约论，认为它把国家混同于市民社会，仿佛国家只为保护财产而存在。他设想的合理国家是君主立宪制，王权、行政权和立法权（含等级会议）像有机体一样相互贯通。君主的作用很小：在组织良好的国家里，他只需说一声“是”，在 i 上点一点。常被译作“神在世上的行进”的那句话出自学生笔记，意思是国家的存在是神在世界中的道路，即理性的实现，而非崇拜强权。国家之上没有法官，这引向世界历史。

example.en: Hegel's own image: in a fully organised state the monarch's decision is formal. Ministers advise, laws bind, and the king merely signs, putting the dot on the i. Compare a modern constitutional monarch giving royal assent to a bill passed by parliament: the act is needed to complete the decision, yet its content comes from elsewhere.
example.zh: 黑格尔自己的比喻：在组织完备的国家里，君主的决定只是形式上的。大臣提出建议，法律具有约束力，国王只需签字，就像给 i 点上那一点。可对照今天的立宪君主对议会通过的法案给予御准：这一步不可缺少，它使决定得以完成，但内容来自别处。

image.en: A gilded throne stands empty at the back of the throne room. The king has stepped down in front of it, crown on his head, and with a giant pencil solemnly dots a huge letter block printed 'i'. That is his whole job. Beside him a crowd of citizens goes about its business, and a scroll on a stand reads 'Constitution'.
image.zh: 王座厅后方立着一张空着的镀金王座。国王从王座上走下来，头戴王冠，手持一支巨大的铅笔，郑重其事地给一块印着“i”的大字块点上那一点：这就是他的全部工作。他身旁，一群市民各忙各的，架子上的卷轴写着“宪法”。

thing.zh: 给 i 点点的国王

means.en: the monarch only completes decisions: says 'yes'
means.zh: 君主只完成决定：说一声“是”

means.en: the crown is one moment of an organic constitution
means.zh: 王权只是有机宪制的一个环节

means.en: citizens free in their pursuits, willing the universal
means.zh: 在各自追求中自由、又意欲普遍的公民

means.en: a rational constitution of interlocking powers
means.zh: 相互贯通的诸权力构成的合理宪制

summary.en: States rise and fall before the court of history, which Hegel reads as the progress of the consciousness of freedom.
summary.zh: 国家在历史的法庭前兴衰，黑格尔把世界历史读作自由意识的进展。

title.en: National Spirits and the World Spirit

summary.en: Each people embodies one principle for its era; when the principle is spent the world spirit moves on, and world history is the world's court.
summary.zh: 每个民族在自己的时代体现一个原则；原则耗尽，世界精神便继续前行，世界历史就是世界法庭。

explain.en: States face each other with no praetor above them; their disputes and fates are decided in world history. Borrowing a line from Schiller, Hegel says world history is the world's court of judgment (Weltgericht). Each people has a national spirit (Volksgeist), expressed in its religion, law, art, customs and science. In a given epoch one people carries the principle of the world spirit's current stage and is, for that time, dominant. Once its principle has been worked out, it declines and the next principle passes to another people. The world spirit is nothing apart from this succession: it is spirit coming to know itself through it. The scheme is strongly teleological and contested; Hegel insists the verdict is not simply that might is right.
explain.zh: 国家彼此对峙，头上没有裁判官；它们的争端与命运在世界历史中裁决。黑格尔借用席勒的诗句说：世界历史就是世界法庭（Weltgericht）。每个民族都有自己的民族精神（Volksgeist），体现在宗教、法律、艺术、风俗和科学中。在某一时代，一个民族承载世界精神当前阶段的原则，在那个时代居于主导地位。它的原则充分展开之后，这个民族便衰落，下一个原则传给另一个民族。世界精神并不在这种更替之外，它正是借此认识自身的精神。这一图式的目的论色彩很强，向来有争议；黑格尔则强调，这种裁决并不简单等于强权即公理。

example.en: In Hegel's lectures Greece carries the principle of 'beautiful individuality': free citizens at one with their city, as in Pericles' Athens. That harmony could not absorb the reflective, questioning subject that Socrates stood for. After the Peloponnesian War (431–404 BC) and the Macedonian and then Roman conquests, the lead passes to Rome, whose principle is abstract universality and the legal person.
example.zh: 在黑格尔的讲演中，希腊承载“美的个体性”原则：自由的公民与城邦融为一体，如伯里克利时代的雅典。这种和谐容不下苏格拉底所代表的反思、追问的主体。经过伯罗奔尼撒战争（前 431—前 404 年）以及马其顿、罗马的相继征服，主导权传给罗马，其原则是抽象的普遍性与法律人格。

image.en: A steam train stands at the platform, and a glowing ghost, the world spirit, rides on its roof. One flag-bearer, his principle spent, has stepped off and bows out. Another, carrying a new flag, strides up to board. Behind them the tall station clock strikes the hour: judgment time for every nation that has had its turn.
image.zh: 一列蒸汽火车停在站台，车顶上坐着一个发光的幽灵：世界精神。一个旗手的原则已经耗尽，他走下车，鞠躬退场；另一个扛着新旗的人大步走来准备上车。他们身后，高高的站钟敲响：轮到过的每个民族，此刻都要接受审判。

means.en: the world spirit moving through the peoples
means.zh: 穿行于各民族之间的世界精神

means.en: a people whose principle is spent, declining
means.zh: 原则已耗尽、走向衰落的民族

means.en: the next people, carrying a higher principle
means.zh: 承载更高原则的下一个民族

means.en: world history as the world's court of judgment
means.zh: 世界历史即世界法庭

summary.en: Reason lets individuals' passions do its work: great men chase their own ends and unknowingly carry out what their age requires.
summary.zh: 理性让个人的激情替它工作：伟人追逐自己的目的，却在不知不觉中完成时代的需要。

explain.en: History is driven by passions, interests and ambition, and Hegel does not deny it: 'nothing great in the world has been accomplished without passion.' Yet the universal Idea does not throw itself into the struggle. It stays in the background, untouched and unharmed, and sets the passions to work for it; Hegel calls this the cunning of reason. World-historical individuals such as Alexander, Caesar and Napoleon pursue power and glory, but their aims coincide with what their epoch needs. When the work is done they fall away like empty husks. Ordinary people are often sacrificed too: history, Hegel says, is not the theatre of happiness. The idea has a logical twin in teleology, where reason lets objects wear each other out while it preserves itself.
explain.zh: 历史由激情、利益和野心推动，黑格尔并不否认：“没有激情，世界上任何伟大的事业都不会成功。”但普遍的理念并不亲自投入争斗，而是留在幕后，毫发无损，让激情为它工作，黑格尔称之为理性的狡计。亚历山大、恺撒、拿破仑这样的世界历史人物追求权力与荣耀，他们的目的却恰好与时代的需要相合；事业完成，他们便像空壳一样脱落。普通人也常被牺牲：黑格尔说，历史不是幸福的舞台。这个思想在逻辑学的目的论中有一个孪生兄弟：理性让客体彼此消耗，自己却保全下来。

example.en: On 13 October 1806, the eve of the battle of Jena, Hegel saw Napoleon ride out of the town on reconnaissance and wrote to a friend that he had seen the emperor, 'this world-soul', on horseback. Napoleon fought for his own glory, yet his campaigns carried the Civil Code into parts of Germany and swept away feudal privileges there; reason, not the emperor, set the agenda. Napoleon himself ended on St Helena.
example.zh: 1806 年 10 月 13 日，耶拿会战前夕，黑格尔看到拿破仑骑马出城侦察，写信告诉朋友，他看见了皇帝，“这个世界灵魂”，骑在马上。拿破仑为自己的荣耀而战，他的征战却把民法典带进德意志部分地区，扫除了那里的封建特权：定下议程的是理性，而不是皇帝。拿破仑本人最后被流放到圣赫勒拿岛。

image.en: Napoleon gallops across the platform on a white horse, sword raised, flames of passion licking behind the hooves. He thinks he is steering history. On a bench at the back sits the world spirit, a calm glowing ghost, untouched, just watching. In the horse's path lies a fallen soldier with his shield, one of the many used up along the way.
image.zh: 拿破仑骑着白马冲过站台，高举军刀，马蹄后燃着激情的火焰。他以为是自己在驾驭历史。后方的长椅上坐着世界精神，一个安静发光的幽灵，毫发无损，只是看着。马蹄前方倒着一名带盾的士兵，是一路上被消耗掉的众人之一。

means.en: a world-historical individual chasing his own glory
means.zh: 追逐个人荣耀的世界历史人物

means.en: passions: the energy that drives history
means.zh: 激情：推动历史的能量

thing.en: the calm ghost on the bench

means.en: reason stays in the background, unharmed
means.zh: 理性留在幕后，毫发无损

means.en: individuals sacrificed: history is no theatre of happiness
means.zh: 被牺牲的个人：历史不是幸福的舞台

summary.en: World history is the progress of the consciousness of freedom: one is free, then some are free, then all are free as human beings.
summary.zh: 世界历史无非是自由意识的进展：先是一个人自由，再是一些人自由，最后人之为人皆自由。

explain.en: In his Lectures on the Philosophy of World History Hegel claims that world history is nothing but the progress of the consciousness of freedom. In his scheme the Oriental world knew only that one is free, the despot, whose freedom is therefore mere caprice. The Greek and Roman world knew that some are free, for it rested on slavery. The 'Germanic', that is Christian-European, world first grasped that the human being as such is free. The goal is that this freedom be realised in a rational state, not merely believed. Two cautions: the progress is in consciousness and principle, which reality lags behind; and the geography is crudely Eurocentric. Hegel's picture of Asia and his exclusion of Africa from history are widely rejected today.
explain.zh: 黑格尔在《历史哲学讲演录》中说：世界历史无非是自由意识的进展。在他的图式里，东方世界只知道一个人是自由的，即专制君主，而他的自由因此只是任性；希腊和罗马世界知道一些人是自由的，因为它们建立在奴隶制之上；“日耳曼”即基督教欧洲世界才认识到人之为人是自由的。目标是让这种自由在合理的国家中实现，而不只是被信奉。有两点须注意：进展发生在意识和原则上，现实往往滞后；这幅地理图景带有粗糙的欧洲中心论色彩，黑格尔对亚洲的描绘以及把非洲排除在历史之外，今天普遍受到否定。

example.en: Classical Athens had a few tens of thousands of adult male citizens and many slaves: some were free, and only as citizens of that city. Paul's 'there is neither slave nor free' (Galatians 3:28) voices the principle that freedom belongs to humans as such, yet slavery lasted in European colonies into the 19th century. Hegel himself stresses that a principle takes centuries to reshape reality.
example.zh: 古典时代的雅典只有几万名成年男性公民，另有大量奴隶：一些人是自由的，而且只是作为这个城邦的公民才自由。保罗说“并不分自主的、为奴的”（《加拉太书》3:28），表达了人之为人即自由的原则；可欧洲殖民地的奴隶制一直延续到 19 世纪。黑格尔自己也强调，一个原则要用好几个世纪才能改造现实。

image.en: Three groups stand on the platform from left to right. First a lone despot with a crown and a raised sword: one is free. Then two laurelled citizens, with a chained slave kneeling at their feet: some are free. Last a whole crowd cheering, arms up: all are free. A golden arrow on the floor points the way, like a timetable of freedom.
image.zh: 站台上从左到右站着三组人。先是一个头戴王冠、高举宝剑的独裁者：一人自由。接着是两位戴桂冠的公民，脚边跪着一个戴镣铐的奴隶：一些人自由。最后是一整群欢呼的人，双臂高举：所有人自由。地上一支金色箭头指明方向，像一张自由的列车时刻表。

means.en: Hegel's Orient: one is free, and only as caprice
means.zh: 黑格尔笔下的东方：一人自由，且只是任性

means.en: Greece and Rome: some are free, slavery remains
means.zh: 希腊罗马：一些人自由，奴隶制犹存

means.en: Christian Europe: all are free as human beings
means.zh: 基督教欧洲：人之为人皆自由

means.en: history as the progress of the consciousness of freedom
means.zh: 历史即自由意识的进展

summary.en: Spirit knowing itself: art intuits the absolute in sensuous form, religion pictures it, and philosophy conceives it and closes the circle.
summary.zh: 精神认识自身：艺术在感性形象中直观绝对，宗教以表象描绘它，哲学以概念把握它，并让圆圈闭合。

summary.en: The absolute shines through sensuous material, from the colossal symbol to the Greek statue to the inward romantic arts.
summary.zh: 绝对透过感性材料显现：从庞大的象征，到希腊雕像，再到内在的浪漫型艺术。

title.en: Beauty: The Sensuous Shining of the Idea

summary.en: Art presents the absolute, truth itself, in sensuous form, and beauty made by spirit ranks above the beauty of nature.
summary.zh: 艺术以感性形式呈现绝对即真理本身；由精神创造的美高于自然美。

explain.en: Absolute spirit is spirit knowing itself. Art, religion and philosophy share one content, the absolute, and differ in form: art gives it in sensuous intuition, religion in representation, philosophy in concepts. Art comes first. Hegel defines beauty as the sensuous shining (Scheinen) of the Idea: truth appears in a shape we can see or hear. Artistic beauty ranks above natural beauty because it is 'born of spirit and born again'. Even a silly fancy in someone's head, he says, is higher than any product of nature, since spirit and freedom are in it. So art is not imitation: copying nature only competes with it and loses, like Zeuxis' painted grapes, which fooled only doves. The ideal is a shape fully adequate to its content.
explain.zh: 绝对精神是精神对自身的认识。艺术、宗教、哲学的内容相同，都是绝对，区别在形式：艺术用感性直观，宗教用表象，哲学用概念。艺术是第一阶段。黑格尔把美定义为理念的感性显现（Scheinen）：真理显现为一个看得见、听得到的形象。艺术美高于自然美，因为它是“由心灵产生、又由心灵再生的美”。他甚至说，人脑中一个无聊的念头也比任何自然产物高，因为其中有精神和自由。所以艺术不是模仿：照抄自然只是与自然竞争，而且必输，就像宙克西斯画的葡萄，只骗得过鸽子。理想就是与内容完全相称的形象。

example.en: A sunset may be lovely, but it means nothing and knows nothing. A Rembrandt portrait of an old woman shows a lifetime of patience in the set of her mouth; every brushstroke was chosen by a mind to make that inner life visible. That is why, for Hegel, the painting outranks the sunset, even though only the sunset is 'real'.
example.zh: 日落也许很美，但它什么也不意味，什么也不知道。伦勃朗画的老妇人肖像，在嘴角的线条里显出一辈子的忍耐；每一笔都由一个心灵挑选，为的是让内在生命变得可见。所以在黑格尔看来，画作高于日落，尽管只有日落是“真的”。
