image.en: In the gallery a painter in a beret works at a big easel, and a glowing spirit rises from behind the canvas, so the portrait seems lit from inside. A spotlight picks it out. Beside it a real sunflower stands ignored: nature's beauty, outshone by beauty made by spirit.
image.zh: 美术馆里，一位戴贝雷帽的画家在大画架前作画，一个发光的精灵从画布后升起，肖像仿佛从里面被点亮。聚光灯照着它。旁边一株真的向日葵无人理睬：自然美被精神创造的美比了下去。

thing.en: the spirit glowing through the canvas

means.en: the Idea shining in sensuous form
means.zh: 以感性形式显现的理念

means.en: art is born of spirit, not copied from nature
means.zh: 艺术出自精神，而非照抄自然

means.en: natural beauty ranks lower
means.zh: 自然美等级较低

means.en: Scheinen: shining, appearing
means.zh: Scheinen：照耀与显现

title.zh: 象征型、古典型、浪漫型艺术

summary.en: Three relations of meaning and shape: a groping mismatch in symbolic art, a perfect fit in classical art, spirit overflowing form in romantic art.
summary.zh: 意义与形象的三种关系：象征型的摸索与错位，古典型的完美契合，浪漫型的精神溢出形式。

explain.en: Hegel sorts art by how its content, the Idea, relates to its sensuous shape. In symbolic art (ancient Egypt, India, Persia) the meaning is still vague and abstract, so it finds no adequate shape; it reaches for colossal, strange forms that only hint at it. The pyramid, a vast crystal enclosing a hidden dead, is its emblem, and the Sphinx is the symbol of the symbolic itself. In classical art (Greece) content and shape fit perfectly: the god appears as an idealised human body in sculpture. In romantic art (Christian Europe) spirit has become infinite inwardness that no sensuous shape can contain, so art turns to painting, music and poetry. Architecture is the typically symbolic art, sculpture the classical one.
explain.zh: 黑格尔按内容即理念与感性形象的关系划分艺术。象征型艺术（古埃及、印度、波斯）中，意义还模糊抽象，找不到相称的形象，只能借助庞大怪异的形式去暗示。金字塔是它的标志：巨大的晶体，里面藏着逝者；斯芬克斯则是“象征的象征”。古典型艺术（希腊）中内容与形象完美契合：神以理想化的人体出现在雕塑里。浪漫型艺术（基督教欧洲）中，精神已成为无限的内在性，任何感性形象都容纳不下，艺术于是转向绘画、音乐和诗。建筑是典型的象征型艺术，雕塑属古典型。

example.en: The Great Pyramid of Giza, about 146 m tall when built, is an overwhelming mass around a small burial chamber: the meaning is inside, and the shape can only point to it. A Greek statue of Apollo shows divinity entirely in a calm, proportioned body. Bach's St Matthew Passion presents grief and redemption as pure inner movement of sound, with nothing to look at.
example.zh: 吉萨大金字塔建成时高约 146 米，庞大的石块包裹着一间小小的墓室：意义藏在里面，形象只能指向它。一尊希腊阿波罗雕像把神性完全展现在一个宁静匀称的身体上。巴赫的《马太受难曲》把悲痛与救赎呈现为纯粹的声音的内在运动，没有任何东西可看。

image.en: Three works stand in a row under gallery lights. On the left a huge sandstone pyramid squats on the floor, massive and blank, its meaning sealed somewhere inside. In the middle a marble god stands perfect and calm. On the right a glowing spirit floats free above a small painting, as if it had burst out of the frame. A child walks along the row.
image.zh: 美术馆灯光下，三件作品排成一行。左边一座巨大的砂岩金字塔蹲在地上，厚重而空白，意义封在里面某处。中间一尊大理石神像完美而宁静地站着。右边，一个发光的精灵飘浮在一幅小画上方，像是从画框里冲了出来。一个孩子沿着这一排走过。

means.en: symbolic: vague meaning, colossal shape that only hints
means.zh: 象征型：意义模糊，形象庞大，只能暗示

means.en: classical: content and shape in perfect fit
means.zh: 古典型：内容与形象完美契合

means.en: romantic: inwardness overflows every form
means.zh: 浪漫型：内在性溢出一切形式

means.en: the sequence from architecture to sculpture to painting
means.zh: 从建筑到雕塑再到绘画的次序

summary.en: In its highest vocation art is 'a thing of the past': art goes on, but it is no longer the highest way truth comes to us.
summary.zh: 就其最高使命而言，艺术“已是过去的事”：艺术仍在延续，却不再是真理来到我们面前的最高方式。

explain.en: Hegel's thesis: 'art, considered in its highest vocation, is and remains for us a thing of the past.' He does not predict that artists will stop working or that art will decline; he even hopes it will rise and perfect itself. His claim is that for the modern mind a sensuous shape is no longer the supreme way to grasp truth. However perfect the statues of Greek gods or the images of Christ and Mary, 'we bow the knee no longer'. We now need a science of art: we reflect on works and judge them instead of worshipping through them. Romantic art had already shown that spirit's inwardness exceeds every sensuous form, so the absolute is grasped more inwardly, in religious devotion and then in philosophical concepts. How far the thesis holds is still debated.
explain.zh: 黑格尔的论断是：“就它的最高使命来说，艺术对于我们已是并且永远是过去的事了。”他并不预言艺术家会停工或艺术会衰落，甚至希望艺术继续提高和完善。他的意思是：对现代心灵而言，感性形象已不再是把握真理的最高方式。希腊神像再完美，基督和圣母的形象再出色，“我们也不再屈膝膜拜了”。我们需要的是艺术哲学：对作品进行反思和评判，而不是借它们来敬拜。浪漫型艺术早已表明精神的内在性超出一切感性形式，于是绝对要以更内在的方式来把握：先在宗教的虔敬中，再在哲学的概念中。这一论断成立到什么程度，至今仍有争论。

example.en: In the Louvre, crowds photograph the Winged Victory of Samothrace. Some read the wall label, some check the date (around 190 BC), many queue for a selfie; nobody leaves an offering at her feet. Art thrives as an object of enjoyment and study, which is exactly Hegel's point: its works are admired and discussed, not worshipped.
example.zh: 卢浮宫里，人群围着萨莫色雷斯的胜利女神像拍照。有人读墙上的说明，有人看年代（约公元前 190 年），很多人排队自拍，却没有人在她脚下献上供品。艺术作为欣赏和研究的对象依然繁荣，这正是黑格尔的意思：作品被欣赏、被讨论，却不再被敬拜。

image.en: A gilded statue of a god stands under a gallery spotlight, magnificent. In front of it is a church pew, but the visitor on it sits with his back to the god, reading a guidebook about it. Another visitor snaps a photo, and a third strolls past, peering at the god through a magnifying glass. Admired, studied, photographed: no one bows the knee.
image.zh: 聚光灯下立着一尊镀金神像，金碧辉煌。像前摆着一条教堂长凳，坐在上面的参观者却背对神像，埋头读着介绍它的导览手册。另一位参观者举起相机拍照，第三位拿着放大镜边走边打量神像。被欣赏、被研究、被拍照：却没有人屈膝。

thing.en: the gilded god in the spotlight

means.en: art at its height, still beautiful
means.zh: 依然美丽的巅峰艺术

means.en: reflection has replaced devotion
means.zh: 反思取代了虔敬

means.en: we enjoy, study and judge art
means.zh: 我们欣赏、研究、评判艺术

means.en: art is no longer truth's highest form
means.zh: 艺术不再是真理的最高形式

summary.en: The same truth as philosophy, held in pictures, stories and devotion, until thought translates it into concepts.
summary.zh: 与哲学相同的真理，以图像、故事和虔敬来把握，直到思维把它译成概念。

summary.en: Religion has the same content as philosophy, the absolute, but holds it in representation: images, stories, feeling and worship.
summary.zh: 宗教与哲学内容相同，都是绝对，但它以表象来把握：图像、故事、情感与礼拜。

explain.en: Religion is the second shape of absolute spirit. Its content is the same as philosophy's, the absolute truth, God; the difference lies in form. Religion uses representation (Vorstellung): it turns the moments of the concept into images and narratives, sets them side by side in space and one after another in time ('the Father begets the Son', 'God created the world'), and joins the believer to the absolute through faith, devotion and the cult. It is the way truth exists for everyone, not only for philosophers. Religion also has a history: from nature religions through the Greek religion of art to Christianity, which Hegel calls the revealed or consummate religion, because in it God is known as spirit.
explain.zh: 宗教是绝对精神的第二种形态。它的内容与哲学相同，都是绝对真理即上帝，区别在形式。宗教用表象（Vorstellung）：把概念的各个环节变成图像和叙事，在空间中并列，在时间中先后排开（“圣父生圣子”“上帝创造世界”），并借信仰、虔敬与礼拜让信徒与绝对合一。这是真理为所有人存在的方式，而不只为哲学家。宗教也有自己的历史：从自然宗教，经希腊的艺术宗教，到基督教；黑格尔称基督教为天启宗教或完满的宗教，因为在其中上帝被认识为精神。

example.en: 'God created the world in six days' is a picture: it sets creation in time, as an event that happened once. Hegel's conceptual reading is that the world is not self-standing but depends on the absolute, whose nature is to go out of itself into an other. Same content, different form: the believer pictures it with feeling, the philosopher thinks why it must be so.
example.zh: “上帝在六日内创造了世界”是一幅图景：它把创造放进时间，当作曾经发生过一次的事件。黑格尔的概念式解读是：世界不是自立的，而是依赖于绝对，而绝对的本性就是走出自身、进入他者。内容相同，形式不同：信徒带着情感去想象它，哲学家则思考它为何必然如此。

image.en: A tall stained-glass window glows in the cathedral, and a spotlight pours a white beam into it. What comes through is no longer plain light but coloured pictures of stories. A woman kneels before the window holding a candle, praying, and a child beside her points up at a figure in the glass, wide-eyed.
image.zh: 大教堂里一扇高高的彩色玻璃窗在发光，聚光灯把一束白光打进去。透出来的不再是纯白的光，而是一幅幅彩色的故事画面。一位妇女举着蜡烛跪在窗前祈祷，身边的孩子睁大眼睛，指着玻璃上的一个人物。

means.en: the one absolute content, the truth
means.zh: 唯一的绝对内容：真理

means.en: representation: images and narratives
means.zh: 表象：图像与叙事

thing.en: the kneeling woman with a candle

means.en: faith, devotion and worship
means.zh: 信仰、虔敬与礼拜

means.en: truth in a form open to everyone
means.zh: 人人都能接近的真理形式

summary.en: Christianity knows God as spirit: the Trinity pictures the concept's three moments, and death and resurrection picture the negation of the negation.
summary.zh: 在基督教中上帝被认识为精神：三位一体描绘概念的三个环节，死亡与复活描绘否定之否定。

explain.en: For Hegel, Christianity is the revealed, consummate religion: in it God is revealed as spirit. He reads the Trinity as the concept's structure in pictorial form. The Father is the universal, God in himself, like the logical Idea. The Son is particularity: God going out into finitude, in creation and incarnation. The Spirit is the individual return: God present in the believing community. Christ's death is the deepest negation; Hegel cites the Lutheran hymn line 'God himself is dead'. The resurrection is the death of death, the negation of the negation. The reconciliation of finite and infinite that the unhappy consciousness sought in a beyond is reached here, if only in pictures. Whether this reading is orthodox is debated.
explain.zh: 黑格尔称基督教为天启宗教或完满的宗教，因为在其中上帝作为精神启示了自己。他把三位一体读作以表象形式出现的概念结构：圣父是普遍，即自在的上帝，相当于逻辑理念；圣子是特殊，即上帝走入有限，表现为创世与道成肉身；圣灵是个别的回归，即上帝临在于信徒的团契之中。基督之死是最深的否定，黑格尔引用路德派赞美诗的句子“上帝自己死了”；复活则是死亡之死，即否定之否定。苦恼意识在彼岸寻求的有限与无限的和解，在这里实现了，尽管仍以表象的方式。这究竟是正统基督教，还是把它译成了哲学，至今仍有争论。

example.en: Map the creed onto the concept. 'I believe in God, the Father almighty' is the universal. 'And in Jesus Christ, his only Son ... crucified, died and was buried' is the particular: God as one finite human who dies. 'On the third day he rose again' and 'I believe in the Holy Spirit ... the communion of saints' are the individual: spirit alive in a community. Three moments, one God.
example.zh: 把信经与概念对照：“我信上帝，全能的父”是普遍；“我信我主耶稣基督，上帝的独生子……被钉于十字架，受死，埋葬”是特殊，即上帝成为一个会死的有限的人；“第三天从死人中复活”与“我信圣灵……我信圣徒相通”是个别，即活在团契中的精神。三个环节，一个上帝。

image.en: High above the nave hangs a blazing sun. Below it a robed figure lies stretched out on the stone floor, still. A white dove has risen from him and hovers over a small crowd of believers, who look up as one. Light above, death below, and life spreading out among the people.
image.zh: 中殿高处悬着一轮炽亮的太阳。它下方，一个穿长袍的人静静地躺在石地上。一只白鸽已从他身上飞起，盘旋在一小群信徒头顶，众人一齐抬头仰望。上有光，下有死亡，而生命正在人群中扩散开来。

means.en: the Father: the universal, God in himself
means.zh: 圣父：普遍，自在的上帝

means.en: the Son: God made finite, and his death
means.zh: 圣子：成为有限的上帝及其死亡

means.en: the Spirit: God alive in the community
means.zh: 圣灵：活在团契中的上帝

thing.en: from the dead figure to the rising dove

means.en: resurrection as the negation of the negation
means.zh: 复活即否定之否定

summary.en: Philosophy translates religion's pictures into concepts: it keeps the content, lifts the form, and so comprehends why the faith is true.
summary.zh: 哲学把宗教的图像译成概念：保留内容、提升形式，从而理解信仰为何是真的。

explain.en: Religion already has the truth, but in a defective form. Representation sets the moments of the concept side by side and in sequence, as events of a sacred history that happened once or will happen at the end of time. Reconciliation is felt in the believer's heart yet pushed into a beyond: a past event, a future kingdom. Philosophy does not refute religion or swap its content. It translates the same content from representation into concept, showing why it must be so, and grasps reconciliation as actual here and now. Hegel can therefore call philosophy itself a kind of worship. This is sublation at work: the content kept, the pictorial form cancelled, the whole lifted into thought. Critics on both sides doubted that nothing is lost in translation.
explain.zh: 宗教已经拥有真理，但形式有缺陷。表象把概念的各环节并列、排序，变成一部神圣历史中的事件：要么发生在过去，要么发生在末日。和解在信徒心中被感受到，却被推到彼岸：一件过去的事，一个未来的国度。哲学不是要驳倒宗教，也不是替换它的内容，而是把同一内容从表象译成概念，说明它为何必然如此，并把和解理解为此时此地的现实。所以黑格尔可以说，哲学本身也是一种礼拜。这正是扬弃：内容被保存，图像形式被取消，整体被提升到思想。至于翻译中是否毫无损失，左右两派的批评者都有怀疑。

example.en: Picture: 'The Son of God became man, died and rose again.' Concept: the infinite is not a beyond set against the finite; it is the movement of going out into the finite and returning to itself through negation, the true infinite of the Logic. The believer holds this as a story about one man in Palestine; the philosopher sees in it the structure of all spirit, ours included.
example.zh: 表象：“上帝之子成为人，受死，又复活。”概念：无限不是与有限对立的彼岸，而是走进有限、又通过否定回到自身的运动，即逻辑学中的真无限。信徒把它当作巴勒斯坦一个人的故事来持守；哲学家则从中看到一切精神的结构，包括我们自己。

image.en: In the middle of the cathedral a conveyor belt hums. At its left end a stained-glass panel waits beside a funnel that feeds the belt; at the right end out comes an open book printed 'Concept'. Behind the belt a robed philosopher with a magnifying glass checks that the colours on the page match those in the glass: content kept, form transformed.
image.zh: 大教堂中央，一条传送带嗡嗡运转。左端，一块彩色玻璃窗板等在给传送带进料的漏斗旁；右端出来的是一本摊开的书，上面印着“概念”。传送带后面，一位穿长袍的哲学家拿着放大镜核对：书页上的颜色与玻璃上的一模一样。内容保留了，形式改变了。

thing.en: the stained glass by the funnel

means.en: religion's pictures going in
means.zh: 送进去的宗教图像

means.en: the same content in conceptual form
means.zh: 以概念形式呈现的同一内容

means.en: nothing of the content is discarded
means.zh: 内容一点也没有丢弃

means.en: translation as sublation: cancel, keep, lift
means.zh: 翻译即扬弃：取消、保存、提升

summary.en: The absolute in the form of thought: philosophy's history, its lateness, and the circle that returns to the beginning.
summary.zh: 以思想为形式的绝对：哲学的历史、它的姗姗来迟，以及回到开端的圆圈。

title.en: The History of Philosophy Is Philosophy

summary.en: The sequence of philosophical systems is one philosophy developing; each system is refuted only as final and survives as a moment.
summary.zh: 哲学体系的更替是同一个哲学的发展；每个体系被驳倒的只是它的终极地位，它本身作为环节保留下来。

explain.en: Hegel rejects the view of the history of philosophy as a gallery of opinions refuting one another. It is one philosophy developing in time, and the order of systems roughly matches the order of the logical categories: Parmenides grasped being, Heraclitus becoming ('there is no proposition of Heraclitus which I have not adopted in my Logic'), the atomists being-for-self, Spinoza substance. No principle is simply refuted; what is refuted is its claim to be the whole, final truth. It is demoted to a moment of a richer whole. So the latest philosophy, if genuine, is the result of all earlier ones and must contain their principles. This is determinate negation applied to the history of thought, and makes reading old philosophers a way of doing philosophy.
explain.zh: 黑格尔反对把哲学史看作一座陈列互相驳斥的意见的画廊。哲学史是同一个哲学在时间中的发展，诸体系的次序大致对应逻辑范畴的次序：巴门尼德把握了存在，赫拉克利特把握了变易（“赫拉克利特的命题，没有一个我没有纳入我的逻辑学”），原子论者把握了自为存在，斯宾诺莎把握了实体。没有哪个原则被简单驳倒，被驳倒的只是它自称为全部和最终真理的要求；它被降为一个更丰富整体中的环节。所以最新的哲学，只要是真正的哲学，就是此前一切哲学的成果，必须包含它们的原则。这是确定的否定在思想史上的运用，也使研读古代哲学家本身成为在做哲学。

example.en: Parmenides (around 500 BC): only being is, and change is illusion. Heraclitus: everything flows. Refuting Parmenides does not throw being away: the Logic still opens with pure being and shows how it passes into nothing and becoming. Spinoza's single substance, 'God or nature', is likewise kept, but Hegel adds that substance must also be grasped as subject.
example.zh: 巴门尼德（约公元前 500 年）：唯有存在，变化只是幻象。赫拉克利特：万物皆流。驳倒巴门尼德并不等于扔掉存在：逻辑学依然以纯存在开篇，并说明它如何过渡为无和变易。斯宾诺莎“神即自然”的唯一实体同样被保留，只是黑格尔补充说：实体也必须被理解为主体。

image.en: In the temple four marble busts of philosophers stand stacked, each on the head of the one before, a wobbly column taller than a person. Parmenides is at the bottom, named on a little plaque. A young critic swings a hammer at him and a crack runs through the marble, yet the bust holds and keeps carrying all the others: refuted, but still bearing the weight.
image.zh: 神庙里，四尊哲学家的大理石半身像一个顶着一个摞起来，摇摇晃晃，比人还高。最底下是巴门尼德，小牌子上写着他的名字。一个年轻的批评者抡起锤子砸向他，大理石裂开一道缝，可这尊像依然稳住，继续托着上面所有的人：被驳倒了，却仍在承重。

means.en: systems in sequence, each built on its predecessors
means.zh: 依次相承、层层叠加的诸体系

means.en: being: the first principle, still carrying the rest
means.zh: 存在：最初的原则，仍承载其余

means.en: refuted as final truth, kept as a moment
means.zh: 作为终极真理被驳倒，作为环节被保留

means.en: each new system refutes and inherits
means.zh: 每个新体系都在驳斥中继承

summary.en: Philosophy is its own time comprehended in thought; it always comes too late to instruct the world how it ought to be.
summary.zh: 哲学是被把握在思想中的它的时代；要教导世界应当如何，它总是来得太迟。

explain.en: The Preface to the Philosophy of Right calls philosophy 'its own time comprehended in thoughts', so it can no more leap beyond its age than a person can jump over Rhodes. Its task is to recognise reason in what is actual, not to design an ideal state in a beyond. As for teaching the world how it ought to be, philosophy always comes too late: it appears only when actuality has completed its process of formation. 'When philosophy paints its grey in grey, a shape of life has grown old... The owl of Minerva begins its flight only with the falling of dusk.' Minerva is the Roman goddess of wisdom, and the owl is her bird. The point is retrospective comprehension; whether it leaves room for criticising the present is debated.
explain.zh: 《法哲学原理》序言说，哲学是“被把握在思想中的它的时代”，所以它跳不出自己的时代，正如一个人跳不过罗陀斯岛。它的任务是在现实中认出理性，而不是在彼岸设计一个理想国家。至于教导世界应当如何，哲学总是来得太迟：只有当现实完成了它的形成过程，哲学才出现。“当哲学把它的灰色绘成灰色时，一种生活形态就已经变老了……密涅瓦的猫头鹰要等黄昏到来才会起飞。”密涅瓦是罗马的智慧女神，猫头鹰是她的鸟。要点是回顾性的理解；它是否还给批判现实留有余地，则有争论。

example.en: The Philosophy of Right appeared in late 1820 (dated 1821), after the French Revolution, the Napoleonic wars and the Prussian reforms had already reshaped Europe. It does not tell Prussia what to do next; it tries to understand the modern state that had emerged. By the time the system of modern freedom could be written down, that shape of life was already mature.
example.zh: 《法哲学原理》于 1820 年底出版（扉页印 1821 年），那时法国大革命、拿破仑战争和普鲁士改革早已重塑了欧洲。这本书并不告诉普鲁士下一步该做什么，而是试图理解已经形成的现代国家。等到现代自由的体系能被写下来时，那种生活形态已经成熟。

image.en: Dusk in the temple: a crescent moon has risen and a lamp post flickers on. Only now does a great owl lift off from beside the head of Minerva's marble statue and sweep over the stage. Below, a philosopher at an easel paints a canvas entirely grey: the day is done, and now it can be understood.
image.zh: 神庙里已是黄昏：一弯新月升起，路灯闪亮起来。直到此刻，一只大猫头鹰才从密涅瓦大理石像的头边起飞，掠过舞台。下方，一位哲学家在画架前把整块画布涂成灰色：白天已经结束，现在才能被理解。

thing.en: the owl taking off at dusk

means.en: philosophy arrives when an era has matured
means.zh: 哲学在一个时代成熟后才到来

thing.en: the moon and the lit lamp

means.en: dusk: a shape of life has grown old
means.zh: 黄昏：一种生活形态已经变老

means.en: grey in grey: comprehension, not rejuvenation
means.zh: 灰色绘成灰色：理解而非返老还童

means.en: wisdom: its own time comprehended in thought
means.zh: 智慧：被把握在思想中的时代

summary.en: The system is a circle whose end returns to its beginning; each of its parts, logic, nature and spirit, is a circle too.
summary.zh: 体系是一个终点回到起点的圆圈；逻辑、自然、精神每一部分本身也是一个圆圈。

explain.en: Hegel calls philosophy a circle: each part is a whole rounded in itself, and the whole is 'a circle of circles' (Encyclopedia §15; the Science of Logic says the same of its method). The system starts from pure being, the emptiest thought, with nothing presupposed. It ends with absolute spirit thinking itself, which turns out to be what was implicitly there from the start. So the end leads back to the beginning, now fully developed. The Encyclopedia closes with three syllogisms in which logic, nature and spirit take turns as the middle term, and then with Aristotle's words on thought thinking itself. This is Hegel's answer to the problem of a first principle: the beginning is justified only at the end, as a result.
explain.zh: 黑格尔把哲学称为一个圆圈：每一部分都是自身完满的整体，而整体是“圆圈之圆圈”（《哲学全书》§15；《逻辑学》论方法时也这样说）。体系从纯存在这一最空洞、无前提的思想开始，终于思维自身的绝对精神，而这正是从一开始就潜在地存在的东西。终点于是回到起点，只是起点已被充分展开。《哲学全书》以三个推理收尾，逻辑、自然、精神轮流充当中项，最后引用亚里士多德论“思想思维自身”的话。这就是黑格尔对第一原理问题的回答：开端只有在终点处，作为结果，才得到证明。

example.en: Walk the palace: you began with sense-certainty and pure being, climbed through essence and concept, crossed nature, and reached spirit and philosophy. Philosophy's last insight is that the whole climb was thought developing itself, which sends you back to the first room, pure being; but now you know what it was the beginning of. As on a spiral ramp, you stand where you began, one turn higher.
example.zh: 走一遍这座宫殿：你从感性确定性和纯存在出发，穿过本质与概念，越过自然，到达精神与哲学。哲学最后领悟到，整段攀登就是思想自身的展开，于是把你送回第一间展厅，回到纯存在；只是这一次，你知道它是什么的开端了。就像走螺旋坡道，你站回起点，却高了一圈。

image.en: Three huge wagon wheels, gold, green and blue, stand in a ring on the temple floor: logic, nature, spirit. Curved golden arrows on the floor lead from each wheel to the next and from the last back to the first. In the middle a traveller with a lantern completes the round and turns back towards the gold wheel where she set out.
image.zh: 神庙地上，三只巨大的车轮站成一圈，金、绿、蓝三色：逻辑、自然、精神。地上弯曲的金色箭头从一个车轮指向下一个，再从最后一个指回第一个。中间一位提灯的旅人走完一圈，又转身走向她出发时的金色车轮。

means.zh: 整体：圆圈之圆圈
